items.abstract: Organic mixed ionic–electronic conductors (OMIECs) couple electronic doping to ion compensation and water reorganization. As doping increasing, molecular reorganization within the polymer–ion–water environment is thought to underlie the often nonmonotonic response of OMIEC devices, yet this process is essential for the understanding of structure-function relationship in related OMIEC devices but remains unclear. Although advanced operando measurements can resolve charge-state-dependent counterion localization within ordered OMIEC domains, jointly tracking electronic charging, explicit ion compensation, hydration, and molecular exchange across doping remains challenging; conventional simulations likewise do not allow these coupled variables to evolve together under constant electrochemical potential. To address these limitations under experimentally relevant electrochemical conditions, we develop an ion-regulated quantum mechanics/molecular mechanics (QM/MM) grand-canonical molecular dynamics framework that operates at constant electrochemical potential and samples OMIECs across experimentally relevant doping levels. Experimental ²³Na and ³⁵Cl nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectra and layer-resolved computational sum-frequency-generation (SFG) spectra validate the polymer microstructure and polymer–electrolyte interfacial model. The simulations reveal a doping-dependent reorganization mechanism and identify a distinct compensation–exchange balance at the charging level associated with the experimental carrier-mobility maximum. With increasing doping, water–side-chain hydrogen bonding weakens and the glycol-rich environment crosses over from Na⁺ organization to Cl⁻-dominated compensation. Near the mobility maximum, persistent Na⁺ environments and a long-lived Na⁺–Cl⁻ motif coexist with a more rapidly exchanging Cl⁻ population. Further charging disrupts this balance, producing either kinetically trapped Cl⁻ or a more highly hydrated, rapidly exchanging environment. These findings establish distinct ion-compensation and exchange regimes across doping and provide a general framework for resolving polymer–ion–water structure–function relationships in OMIECs.
items.authors: Zixuan Wei, Ying Xiang, Hesam Makki, Wanlin Xu, Xingli Chen, Chao Deng
items.title_zh: 超越膨胀：电化学掺杂调节水合有机混合离子-电子导体的离子补偿与交换平衡
items.summary_zh: 有机混合离子-电子导体（OMIECs）将电子掺杂与离子补偿和水重组相结合。随着掺杂的增加，聚合物-离子-水环境中的分子重组被认为是OMIEC器件常见的非单调响应的基础，但这一过程对于理解相关OMIEC器件的结构-功能关系至关重要，仍不清楚。我们开发了一种离子调节的量子力学/分子力学（QM/MM）大正则分子动力学框架，在恒定电化学势下操作，并在实验相关的掺杂水平下对OMIECs进行采样。实验的²³Na和³⁵Cl核磁共振（NMR）光谱及层分辨计算的和频生成（SFG）光谱验证了聚合物微观结构和聚合物-电解质界面模型。模拟结果揭示了掺杂依赖的重组现象。
items.l1_lead: 研究表明，电化学掺杂显著影响有机混合离子-电子导体的离子补偿与水合重组过程，揭示了其结构与功能之间的复杂关系。
items.l2_summary:
有机混合离子-电子导体（OMIECs）是一种新型材料，结合了电子掺杂、离子补偿与水重组的特性。随着掺杂程度的增加，聚合物-离子-水环境中的分子重组被认为是OMIEC器件表现出非单调响应的基础。然而，尽管这一过程对于理解OMIEC器件的结构-功能关系至关重要，但其具体机制仍不明确。为了解决这一问题，研究团队开发了一种离子调节的量子力学/分子力学（QM/MM）大正则分子动力学框架，能够在恒定电化学势下操作，并在实验相关的掺杂水平下对OMIECs进行采样。

通过实验的²³Na和³⁵Cl核磁共振（NMR）光谱以及层分辨计算的和频生成（SFG）光谱，研究者验证了聚合物的微观结构和聚合物-电解质界面的模型。这些实验结果与模拟结果相结合，揭示了掺杂依赖的重组现象，进一步说明了掺杂对OMIECs性能的影响。研究表明，掺杂不仅影响了电子的传导性，还通过离子补偿和水分子的重组，调节了材料的整体性能。这一发现为深入理解OMIEC材料的工作机制提供了新的视角，并为未来的材料设计和应用奠定了基础。

items.title: Multiscale Insights into CO2 Chemisorption and Proton Transfer in Choline-Imidazolate based Deep Eutectic solvents: Exploring the Effect of Primary, Secondary and Tertiary Alkanolamine on Reaction Pathways and Product Distribution
items.abstract: Understanding how solvent composition governs competitive CO2 chemisorption within solvents is essential for the rational design of solvents for CO2 capture. In this work, we combine density functional theory (DFT), classical molecular dynamics (cMD), and microkinetic modeling to investigate CO2 chemisorption in choline-imidazolate based systems containing different alkanolamine hydrogen bond donors (HBDs): monoethanolamine (MEA), diethanolamine (DEA), and methyldiethanolamine (MDEA). By systematically characterizing the thermodynamics, kinetics and liquid structure influence, our results show that within these systems, choline is the preferred CO2-binding site unless a HBD is present. Accordingly, the MEA system shifts almost entirely to amine-centered carbamate formation, the DEA system retains carbamate dominance but with stronger competition from choline-centered capture, and the MDEA system which additionally includes water shifts back toward choline-centered carbonate together with a competitive water-assisted bicarbonate pathway. The findings illustrate how CO2 chemisorption in multicomponent liquids is controlled by a combination of intrinsic reaction thermodynamics, liquid-structure, and CO2 concentration. More broadly, this work provides insights that will facilitate molecular-level design of solvents for CO2 uptake and regeneration.
items.authors: Osasumwen J. Ikponmwosa, S.M Gulam Rabbani, Stephen P. Vicchio, Rachel B. Getman

items.title: AutoSolveX: automated batch structure solution, initial refinement and guest screening from diffraction data
items.abstract: Modern three-dimensional electron diffraction (3D ED) workflows can collect and process many datasets in a single session, whereas downstream structure solution, refinement and model interpretation often remain manual. Here we present AutoSolveX, a cross-platform Python pipeline with a graphical user interface for automated batch structure solution and initial refinement from processed diffraction data. AutoSolveX integrates SHELXT, SHELXS and SHELXL, applies electron scattering factors to 3D ED data, and extends automation to guest identification by screening candidate molecules against experimental Q-peak clusters and generating guest-containing models for subsequent refinement. We demonstrate AutoSolveX using five deposited electron-diffraction structures from different chemical classes, seven 3D ED datasets of Co-MOF-74, and ten 3D ED datasets of guest-containing structures of Bi-MOF SU-100 and 18 single-crystal X-ray diffraction datasets of Al-MOF-520. For the five deposited structures, AutoSolveX recovered the reported space groups and produced initial models with coordinate root-mean-square deviations of 0.015–0.052 Å from the deposited models. Automated batch solution and refinement of the Co-MOF-74 datasets generated comparable structural models across crystals and identified a dataset with poorer refinement results, demonstrating the value of systematic multi-dataset analysis. Guest screening retained the expected guest among the top three candidates for 9 of 10 SU-100 datasets and among the top five for 12 of 18 MOF-520 datasets. Complete molecular geometries were generated for all but the largest guests. AutoSolveX therefore provides a unified workflow from diffraction data to structural models and guest interpretation, reducing repetitive crystallographic work and facilitating analysis of large numbers of datasets.
items.authors: Sofiia Butonova, Yinlin Chen, Xiaodong Zou
items.title_zh: AutoSolveX：基于衍射数据的自动化批量结构解算与初步精修
items.summary_zh: 现代三维电子衍射（3D ED）工作流程能够在单次会话中收集和处理多个数据集，但后续的结构解算、精修和模型解释通常仍需手动进行。本文介绍了AutoSolveX，一个跨平台的Python管道，具有图形用户界面，用于从处理后的衍射数据中自动化批量结构解算和初步精修。AutoSolveX集成了SHELXT、SHELXS和SHELXL，应用电子散射因子于3D ED数据，并通过筛选候选分子与实验Q峰簇进行客体识别，生成含客体的模型以供后续精修。我们使用来自不同化学类别的五个已存电子衍射结构、七个Co-MOF-74的3D ED数据集，以及十个Bi-MOF SU-100的含客体结构和18个Al-MOF-520的单晶X射线衍射数据集来演示AutoSolveX。对于五个已存结构，AutoSolveX恢复了报告的空间群，并生成了与已存模型坐标均方根偏差为0.015–0.052 Å的初始模型。Co-MOF-74数据集的自动化批量解算和精修生成了可比的结构模型，并识别出一个精修结果较差的数据集，展示了系统性多数据集分析的价值。
items.l1_lead: AutoSolveX是一种自动化工具，能够从电子衍射数据中批量解算和初步精修结构，显著提高了三维电子衍射数据处理的效率和准确性。
items.l2_summary:
现代三维电子衍射（3D ED）技术在数据收集和处理方面取得了显著进展，但在结构解算、精修和模型解释的后续工作中，仍然需要依赖手动操作。为了解决这一问题，本文介绍了AutoSolveX，这是一个跨平台的Python管道，配备了图形用户界面，旨在从处理后的衍射数据中实现自动化的批量结构解算和初步精修。AutoSolveX集成了多个工具，包括SHELXT、SHELXS和SHELXL，能够应用电子散射因子于3D ED数据，并通过筛选候选分子与实验Q峰簇进行客体识别，从而生成含客体的模型以供后续精修。

在研究中，AutoSolveX的有效性通过多个数据集得到了验证，包括来自不同化学类别的五个已存电子衍射结构、七个Co-MOF-74的3D ED数据集、十个Bi-MOF SU-100的含客体结构以及18个Al-MOF-520的单晶X射线衍射数据集。对于这五个已存结构，AutoSolveX成功恢复了报告的空间群，并生成了与已存模型坐标均方根偏差为0.015–0.052 Å的初始模型，显示出其在结构解算中的高效性和准确性。此外，在对Co-MOF-74数据集进行的自动化批量解算和精修中，AutoSolveX生成了可比的结构模型，并识别出一个精修结果较差的数据集，这一结果突显了系统性多数据集分析的价值。

总体而言，AutoSolveX为三维电子衍射数据的处理提供了一种高效的自动化解决方案，能够显著提高结构解算和精修的效率，减少手动操作的需求，推动了电子衍射技术在材料科学和化学领域的应用。

items.title: Lactic Acid Related Molecule Reaction Outcome Prediction via AI Chatbots
items.abstract: Lactic acid (LA) and its related molecules like its polymer (Polylactic acid) have large importance in organic chemistry reactions. The objective of this experimental study was to determine the effectiveness of using AI chatbots to predict the outcomes and key findings of chemical reactions associated with the lactic acid chemical, along with understanding which chatbots are more effective to use in order to investigate a more efficient method to form hypotheses about these reactions. Reaction conditions of chosen reactions were put into specific models of ChatGPT, Perplexity, Copilot, and Gemini to test whether the outcomes they predicted matched with the key findings in the research papers the reactions were sourced from. Using statistical analysis by Cochran’s Q Test (p = 0.247237), a statistically significant difference between types of chatbot used for product prediction was not found. However, a Wilson Score Interval of the Perplexity Pro default model with 90% confidence yielded an interval of (0.6010, 0.8847). The findings essentially suggest a relatively high accuracy interval for the proportion of the types of LA related reactions in this study that the Perplexity Pro default model can predict correctly. The implications of this emphasize the importance of further examining what reactions can and cannot be used in AI chatbots to predict the outcomes.
items.authors: Atharva Sahu

items.title: Language-model-derived training data for polymer glass transition prediction: a controlled benchmark
items.abstract: Experimental glass transition temperatures (Tg) are known for only a few thousand polymers, and each new one costs a synthesis and a measurement. Large language models (LLMs) have read much of the polymer literature and answer questions about polymers for a fraction of a cent. We tested whether such answers can replace or supplement measurements for Tg prediction by two routes: asking Claude Sonnet 5 to write polymers together with their Tg, and asking it to assign a Tg to existing hypothetical polymers. Both datasets were used to train a chemical language model, which was compared on held-out measurements with the same model trained on a growing number of real measurements, alone or after a first stage on the synthetic data. Controls with shuffled Tg values and with the model’s own pseudo-labels separated the value of the LLM’s labels from that of merely seeing more structures. Models trained only on LLM data were about as accurate as the LLM itself and clearly worse than models trained on real data. The LLM data helped only when a few hundred measurements were available, and the benefit disappeared when the Tg values were shuffled. Many “generated” polymers were recalled copies of known polymers, and the LLM’s Tg values were coarse and biased low. LLM-produced data are thus an inexpensive supplement when measurements are scarce, not a substitute for them.
items.authors: Rostislav Rusev

items.title: YOLOX-based detection of C60 molecules in time-resolved TEM
items.abstract: Low contrast and heterogeneous backgrounds hinder automated molecular detection in time-resolved transmission electron microscopy (TEM). We prepared C60-loaded carbon nanohorns by solvent-free mechanochemistry and compared four preprocessing pipelines using YOLOX detectors trained on expert-annotated frames. Wiener filtering combined with contrastlimited adaptive histogram equalization (CLAHE) yielded the highest F1 score of 0.713 at an intersection-over-union (IoU) threshold of 0.30 on temporally held-out frames from the same sequence. Applied to later frames, the model detected partially overlapping C60 candidates and yielded declining detection counts. Some projected intermolecular separations decreased to 0.90 nm, with a cumulative electron dose on the order of 108 e– nm–2 over approximately 15 s. These observations were consistent with, but not diagnostic of, [2+2] cycloaddition. The model also detected some fused structures as C60, indicating that counts reflect C60-like image features rather than true monomer populations. The workflow provides frame-wise localization and counting of molecular candidates. Multiclass detection of monomers, and fused structures, combined with tracking that accounts for detection errors and independent validation, could support quantitative kinetic analysis observed by atomic-resolution TEM.
items.authors: Yoshito Saito, Masaya Sakakibara, Kenta Itakura, Takayuki Nakamuro

items.title: Small-Molecule Data Splitting for Machine Learning in Drug Design
items.abstract: Data splitting is a critical determinant of machine-learning performance in small-molecule drug design. Different strategies impose distinct assumptions about structural similarity, temporal order, data provenance and chemical-space coverage, thereby affecting both evaluation realism and the interpretation of model performance. This perspective critically examines major splitting approaches, discusses their advantages, applicability and limitations, and offers evidence-based considerations for designing partitions aligned with intended prediction scenarios.
items.authors: Cao-Minh Truong, Van-Thinh To, Gia-Bao Truong, Alexey Orlov, Pedro J. Ballester, Olivier Taboureau

items.title: Repurposing drugs for multi-target treatment of cytokine storm using machine learning
items.abstract: Background: Cytokine Release Syndrome (CRS) is a major driver of acute organ failure in critical care settings, affecting approximately 49 million people and killing approximately 11 million people annually. Targeting multiple dysregulated feedback loops via single-molecule polypharmacology offers a promising strategy to blunt excessive immune activation and treat CRS-induced medical conditions such as sepsis. Methods: We used a computational workflow that combined machine-learning classification and molecular docking to identify multi-target modulators of NLRP3, IKBKB, JAK1, CCR5, and SIGMAR1. To eliminate data leakage, feature selection was strictly embedded within a 10-fold cross-validation loop. Candidates were structurally evaluated for binding affinity and active-site contact residues. Results: The model achieved an accuracy of 95.0% to 99.6% and an area under the receiver-operating curve (AUROC) of 0.995 to 1.000 across all five proteins, demonstrating robust generalization. Multiple compounds with average model-predicted scores above 0.50 across all five proteins were discovered. Docking analyses confirmed that the top candidates had favorable binding energetics, displaying stronger binding affinity than known protein inhibitors. Namely, Simeprevir had an average docking score of -10.3 kcal/mol. Shared key contact residues across drug candidates further support the validity of these docking scores and promise interesting in vitro work. Conclusion: Single-drug, multi-target inhibition effectively modulates interconnected inflammatory loops that drive the sepsis-related cytokine storm. This approach provides an alternative to multi-drug combination therapy in intensive care medicine.
items.authors: Leo Meng, Valentina L. Kouznetsova, Santosh Kesari, Igor F. Tsigelny

items.title: Separating hydration propensity from hydrogen bond donation in trifluoromethyl ketone warheads
items.abstract: Trifluoromethyl ketones populate carbonyl and gem-diol states, but the amount of hydrate present need not report how strongly that hydrate donates a hydrogen bond. We benchmarked 14 trifluoromethyl ketones against a recent colorimetric donor-strength dataset using 198 intended Q-Chem calculations, 181 of which completed normally. In the nine-member aryl subset, experimental hydrate abundance correlated weakly with hydrate-adjusted ln K (r = 0.276), whereas ωB97X-D/def2-TZVPD/SMD parent-relative electronic hydration energies correlated strongly (r = -0.896; ρ = -0.917). Four SMD density-functional profiles were nearly superposable (pairwise r = 0.988-0.999), and local mean C-O distance independently tracked donor strength (r = -0.904). Standardized hydrate-sensor interactions at 1.80 A tracked adjusted ln K (r = -0.683) but not hydrate abundance (r = -0.033). Intramolecular hydrogen bonding stabilized closed hydrate conformers yet weakened external donor interactions. These results separate hydrate population, intrinsic donor strength, and donor accessibility as distinct design variables.
items.authors: Aris Tsai

items.title: Linker-Encoded Enzymatic Topology Control Enables Automated Peptide Stapling with Reusable Immobilized mTGase
items.abstract: Microbial transglutaminase (mTGase) readily forms intermolecular isopeptide bonds, but this native bias promotes peptide oligomerization at synthetically useful concentrations. Here we encode reaction topology in a minimal diamine linker to redirect mTGase toward intramolecular stapling of unprotected glutamine-containing peptides. Direct comparison with a linker-free Lys–Gln substrate shows that the linker-encoded architecture maintains macrocyclization as the dominant pathway from 0.25 to 2.0 mM, whereas the native substrate undergoes exclusively intermolecular ligation. Linker and peptide studies establish geometric, electronic, and sequence requirements, and molecular simulations are consistent with the organization of the acyl–enzyme intermediate. The resulting staples serve as versatile synthetic handles for orthogonal bicyclization, late-stage functionalization, and reductive ring opening. The covalent immobilization of mTGase enables catalyst recycling and seamless integration into a continuous, automated peptide-stapling platform capable of processing diverse substrates. This linker-encoded strategy provides a route to control enzymatic reaction topology for programmable constrained-peptide synthesis.
items.authors: Wanglin Zhan, Cheng Fan, Chengrui Hu, Chengxi Li

items.title: Synthesis of metastable t-ZrO2 via solid-state thermolysis of ZrOCl2·8H2O/NaHCO3: thermodynamics, oxygen vacancies, grain growth and phase stability
items.abstract: We present a comprehensive multiscale theoretical framework for the topotactic solid-state thermolysis of ZrOCl2·8H2O and NaHCO3 (1:2 molar ratio) to metastable tetragonal zirconia (t-ZrO2). Six quantitatively coupled sub-models are developed and validated against experimental data [1]: (i) a thermodynamic Hess-cycle analysis yielding ΔG°topo = −287 ± 18 kJ mol-1 per Zr at 400 °C, which is 56 ± 28 kJ mol-1 more negative than the sol–gel benchmark; (ii) a surface-energy crystallite stability model predicting a critical size Dcr = 13.5 ± 2.0 nm at 400 °C, consistent with the experimentally observed coherent scattering region (CSR) of 11.3 nm; (iii) an oxygen-vacancy thermodynamic model with ΔGvacancy = −3.7 to −36.8 kJ mol-1 for O/Zr = 1.63–1.98, rationalising the uniquely reductive micro-atmosphere of the solid-state route; (iv) a gas-wedge fragmentation model with ℱ = 2.07–4.17, confirming primary particle breakdown to 40–80 nm prior to t-ZrO2 crystallisation; (v) a JMAK kinetic analysis of the t → m transformation giving Ea = 81 ± 6 kJ mol-1 and Avrami exponent n = 0.27–0.31, consistent with defect-driven surface nucleation; and (vi) a grain-growth model with Q = 185 ± 15 kJ mol-1 in the presence of NaCl, representing a 25–40 kJ mol-1 reduction compared to NaCl-free systems. A (D, x)-phase stability map predicts a re-entrant t → amorphous boundary at O/Zr 1.60 for D 5 nm — a novel, falsifiable prediction — and quantitatively reproduces all experimental phase fields from ref. [1]. The by-product NaCl acts as a dual-role flux, stabilising t-ZrO2 nanoparticles below 500 °C via grain-boundary pinning but accelerating grain coarsening and the t → m transition above 600 °C. Optimal synthesis conditions are established: 1:2 molar ratio, heating rate β = 8–12 °C min-1, calcination at 350–450 °C, and post-synthesis drying at 55–65% relative humidity.
items.authors: Володимир Трихліб

items.title: Persistent Ti–Cl Bonds Direct Self-Organization in Titanium–Ligand Artificial Photosynthesis Systems
items.abstract: Hydrolyzed TiCl4–ligand systems capable of capturing atmospheric CO2 and converting it into reduced carbon products under ambient moisture and visible light exhibit an unexpected recurring feature: one or more Ti–Cl bonds persist after prolonged atmospheric exposure. Residual chloride is conventionally interpreted as incomplete hydrolysis preceding conversion to condensed Ti–O–Ti networks. The underlying Ti–OH/Ti–O photochemistry connects these systems to established TiO2 photocatalysis, but persistent Ti–Cl bonds and coordinated ligands prevent their simple description as incompletely formed TiO2. Here we propose a broader interpretation in which partial chloride retention is a structural control variable in the active material. By kinetically limiting extensive hydrolysis and condensation, retained chloride may preserve molecular or oligomeric titanium oxychloride–hydroxo species, maintain Lewis-acidic and exchangeable coordination sites, regulate the density and lifetime of Ti–OH groups, and support coexistence of multiple structural and redox generations. The nitrogen-containing ligands may be integral to this persistence: coordination to titanium can moderate hydrolysis and condensation, while ligand protonation can retain hydrolysis-generated acidity as local ligand–H+/Cl- ion pairs. Proton and chloride equivalents may therefore remain distributed among coordinated chloride, protonated ligands, Ti–OH···Cl environments, and more strongly hydrogen-bonded HCl-containing motifs. Such retention could establish a local proton–chloride reservoir and make individual hydrolysis and ligand-exchange steps dynamically reversible without implying global equilibrium. Related persistence of Zr–Cl bonds in zirconium–ligand CO2-capture systems suggests that chloride retention may be a broader feature of evolving Group 4 metal ensembles. The proposal distinguishes direct observations from mechanistic inference: persistent chloride-containing families support incomplete hydrolysis, whereas their roles in redox stabilization, proton-coupled electron transfer, self-repair, and catalytic turnover remain testable hypotheses. If confirmed, controlled partial chloride retention would constitute a design principle rather than a synthetic imperfection in this form of artificial photosynthesis.
items.authors: Gregory G. Arzoumanidis, Michail Paraskevas

items.title: Chemistry, Generative AI, and English: implications for chemistry researchers from diverse language backgrounds
items.abstract: Background, context, purpose: English is essential in global science but poses challenges for researchers who speak it as an additional language (Eng+). We investigated how chemistry researchers’ language backgrounds shape their experiences and the impact(s) of digital tools, including generative artificial intelligence (GenAI). We administered a questionnaire to chemistry researchers having English-as-a-first (Eng1st) or English-as-an-additional (Eng+) language. Results, main findings: Both groups indicated that English proficiency is crucial for productivity, though Eng+ participants reported more difficulties. Eng+ participants viewed digital tools as more helpful, including GenAI, and primarily used for writing support. However, concerns about GenAI’s accuracy, ethics, and plagiarism risks were common. Some Eng+ researchers avoided over-relying on GenAI, preferring to improve their English skills. Few used GenAI beyond summaries and rephrasing/translation. Conclusions: This work is the first to identify how emerging technologies like GenAI are perceived and used by researchers from different language backgrounds, highlighting the potential to enhance equity and productivity for Eng+ scientists.
items.authors: Jacky M. Deng, Makayla Dagenaus, Alison B. Flynn

items.title: ROSE: a Foundation Model for Reusable One-dimensional Spectrum Embeddings in 1H NMR
items.abstract: Most deep learning models for 1H NMR are trained for a single endpoint and do not provide representations that can be reused across analytical tasks. We introduce ROSE (Reusable One-dimensional Spectrum Embeddings), a 7.8-million-parameter spectrum-side foundation model pretrained on 3.2 million experimental and simulated spectra using an InChIKey-14 identity holdout that excludes all molecules appearing in the external benchmark test sets. Its shared spectral encoder supports denoising, peak detection, classification, cross-field alignment, molecular retrieval and structure-tospectrum prediction. Beyond internal evaluation on identity-disjoint holdouts, ROSE was assessed on external benchmarks excluded from pretraining, matching the published QIB PLS-DA result for 60-MHz edible-oil classification (98.8% balanced accuracy vs 98.9% accuracy), reducing NMRNet structure-to-spectrum Chamfer loss by 39% over Morgan+Ridge (0.79 vs 1.29), achieving 69% peak-detection F1 on NMRformer, and, after short domain adaptation, reaching 37.1% Top-1 and 67.7% Top-10 retrieval on NMR-Solver. ROSE represents a first step toward a general-purpose NMR foundation model for scalable industrial analytical applications.
items.authors: Mattia Di Iorio, Carmine Mattia, Andrea Zanda, Maurizio Atzori

items.title: Simultaneous CEA and CDH-17 Detection from Cancer Extracellular Vesicles Via Machine Learning Enabled Bio Silent Azide-Infrared Spectroscopy
items.abstract: Extracellular vesicles (EVs) provide a rich, minimally invasive source of cancer biomarkers, yet EV surface glycoproteins remain comparatively underexploited compared with EV internal cargo. Here, we report a bio silent, azide-based Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopic platform for simultaneous, label-minimal detection of two colorectal cancer (CRC) EV surface biomarkers, carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA) and cadherin-17 (CDH-17), directly from intact vesicles. EVs from five CRC cell lines and a non-cancerous control line were first distinguished by their intrinsic biochemical fingerprints across the lipid, protein, carbohydrate, and nucleic acid spectral regions, achieving up to 97% classification accuracy by multivariate (PCA/SIMCA) and machine-learning (PLS-DA) analysis. Selective azide labeling of CEA and CDH-17 via biotinylated antibodies and streptavidin–azide generated a specific vibrational signal in the 2000–2300 cm⁻¹ bio-silent window without perturbing native EV spectra; peak authenticity was confirmed by Gaussian deconvolution, quantitative signal-to-noise analysis (SNR = 315 ± 99), and buffer/serum-artifact controls. Density-of-states overlap, cosine correlation, and constrained non-negative least-squares regression enabled simultaneous deconvolution and quantification of both biomarkers from mixed-antibody spectra, resolving cell line–specific expression patterns and enabling EV subtyping. Critically, the platform was validated on plasma-derived EVs from CRC patients and a healthy donor, where diagnostic performance exceeded that of the cell-line panel (AUC = 1.0 for metastatic CRC vs. healthy across all six spectral ratios; AUC = 0.58–1.0 for early-stage CRC vs. healthy). These results establish azide-FTIR spectroscopy as a rapid, label-efficient, and artifact-controlled platform for multiplexed EV biomarker detection, with direct evidence of its translatability to clinical liquid biopsy specimens rather than relying on cell-line data alone.
items.authors: Debashish Paul, Natasha Natasha, Sunita Saha, Suchetan Pal, Ananya Ananya, Saroj Kumar

items.title: In situ Ni(II) to Ni(0) Reduction Enables Catalytic H2 Generation from Fe(II)-bearing Minerals
items.abstract: Mechanistic insight into the catalysis of stimulated mineralogical hydrogen production may advance its realization as a scalable, emissions-free hydrogen source. Though enhanced H 2 generation from Ni(II)-catalyzed Fe(II) mineral oxidation has been posited to occur at Ni(II) sites co-precipitated on the Fe(II) mineral surface, operando insight into the active catalyst for H 2 production remains limited. Here, we combine potentiometry and time-resolved mass spectrometry to perform operando studies of exogenous Ni(II) speciation during hydrogen evolution from the coupled oxidation of the ferrous mineral Fe(OH) 2 to Fe 3 O 4 in anoxic water. By studying Fe(II) and Ni(II) systems in isolation, we first establish the thermodynamic competency of Fe(II) for reduction of Ni(II) to Ni(0) in circumneutral aqueous solutions; we then demonstrate that this occurs in situ. We further show that this conversion generates the active Ni(0) catalyst for H 2 evolution coupled to Fe(OH) 2 oxidation, despite the low reductive overpotentials generated by Fe(II). Over the course of the reaction, increasing solution potential due to increasing Fe(III) speciation re-corrodes Ni(0), rendering it undetectable in post-mortem product analysis. Data from Ni(II)-catalyzed hydrogen production from siderite (FeCO 3 ) suggests this in situ reduction of Ni(II) to Ni(0) may be a general mechanistic motif for H 2 generation across ferrous minerals. Insight into this in situ phenomenon is expected to contribute to the mechanistic picture of stimulated mineralogical hydrogen production and guide its optimization – with additional implications for the dynamic speciation of other exogenous metal catalysts for reduction reactions driven by Fe(II) oxidation.
items.authors: Ephraem Tan, Anatole Borisov, Yogesh Surendranath

items.title: Argon Coordination to the 3d Transition-Metal Monohalides: A Systematic Study of σ-Acceptor Accessibility in Ar–MX (M = Sc–Cu; X = F, Cl, Br)
items.abstract: Argon is generally regarded as chemically inert, yet direct Ar–metal coordination has been established for several late transition-metal complexes. Here, we systematically investigate Ar coordination across the 3d transition-metal monofluorides, MF (M = Sc–Cu), and subsequently extend the analysis to the corresponding chlorides and bromides. Density functional theory, population analysis, energy decomposition, and multireference calculations reveal a pronounced and nonmonotonic variation in Ar-binding propensity across the MF series. Ar binding is characterized by Ar 3pσ donation into a metal-centered σ-acceptor manifold of mixed 4s and 3dz2 character. In predominantly single-reference systems, the metal 4s population of bare MF provides a simple descriptor of the accessibility of this manifold: low 4s occupation is generally associated with Ar coordination, whereas high 4s occupation is associated with dissociation. Consistent with this picture, single-reference calculations give shortrange Ar-bound minima for MnF and FeF on lower-spin DFT surfaces with reduced 4s occupation, although these solutions are SCF-unstable and require multireference confirmation. The same metaldependent trend is largely retained for the chlorides and bromides, with additional modulation by the M–X framework. Sc halides mark the multireference limit of the simple 4s-based description.
items.authors: Akane Yano, Ryuto Kambara, Lihao Qu, Takuro Tsutsumi, Yuriko Ono, Tetsuya Taketsugu

items.title: Coupled Field-Gated Nucleation and Autocatalytic Growth in Ferroelectric Switching
items.abstract: Polarization switching in fluorite (HfO2, Hf0.5Zr0.5O2) and wurtzite (AlScN) ferroelectrics is dispersive: nominally identical devices and domains switch over a spread of time rather than at a single threshold. The nucleation-limited-switching (NLS) model treats this phenomenon as a Lorentzian-in-log-time distribution of nucleation waiting times; Kolmogorov–Avrami–Ishibashi (KAI) theory instead treats switching as deterministic nucleation-and-growth. Recent AlScN transport studies report devices moving between these regimes in terms of defect density, thickness, or cycling, motivating a model in which nucleation and growth are explicit, coupled, field-dependent processes.
items.authors: Leon Sandler

items.title: Confinement-Driven Transient Coordination Complexes: H2 Dissociation and Quantum Channel Modification in Single-Atom Contacts
items.abstract: Understanding chemical reactivity at cryogenic temperatures is essential for advancing both fundamental quantum science and next-generation catalytic technologies. At the single-atom limit, geometric confinement can promote ground-state electronic effects that drive novel chemical events without thermal activation. Using the H2 interaction with transition-metal nanocontacts as a benchmark, we report the barrierless formation of a transient tip complex characterized by a diborane-like 4-electron, 3-center bond (Pt–H ~0.17 and 0.18 nm). This 2 ground-state dissociation acts as a selective quantum channel modifier: while the intact, physisorbed molecule yields a conductance of ~0.2 G0, the dissociated transient complex results in a quantized conductance of 1 G0. This mechanism is correctly captured by mean-field orbital models when proper non-local exchange corrections are effectively considered. Furthermore, while bulk palladium is renowned for its high hydrogen affinity, our mean-field models and quantum calculations demonstrate the opposite: Pd nanocontacts merely physisorb H2 (H–H ~0.08 nm), behaving as a noble metal at this quantum limit. These findings illustrate how geometric confinement can drive novel chemical events, opening new avenues for zerotemperature catalysis at the single-atom limit.
items.authors: Yamila García, Yamila Garcia-Martinez

items.title: Many-body machine-learned potential for the hydrated proton at CCSD(T) accuracy with fast analytical gradient
items.abstract: The hydrated proton plays a central role in aqueous chemistry, biological proton transport, and electrochemical energy conversion. Reliable simulations of hydratedproton properties require an accurate reactive potential with low computational cost. Here, we report HP-AQUA, a high-level many-body machine-learned potential for the hydrated proton with fast analytical gradients. HP-AQUA combines the CCSD(T) quality q-AQUA-pol water potential and an accurate H3O + monomer potential with new permutationally invariant polynomial representations of the hydronium-water two-, three-, and four-body interactions. HP-AQUA demonstrates CCSD(T)-level accuracy across a series of gas-phase protonated water clusters for binding energies, harmonic frequencies, proton-transfer profiles, and configurations sampled along molecular dynamics trajectories. Analytical gradients implemented through reverse differentiation reduce the computational cost by more than an order of magnitude relative to our previous
items.authors: Guorui Zhang, Ruitao Ma, Joel M. Bowman, Qi Yu

items.title: Determination of Asbestos Fibre Release Potential from Contaminated Craft Sand and Sand-Based Toys
items.abstract: Over the last century, human exposure pathways for asbestos have changed from those associated with direct interaction with the minerals (e.g. mining) to secondary exposure from a variety of asbestoscontaining materials, including those linked to para-occupational, domestic and environmental pathways. In 2025, the discovery of asbestos in children’s toy sand products caused panic, stress and fear amongst the community. Although there is no safe level of asbestos exposure, these products were deemed to be low risk by some due to uncertainty around whether fibres could become airborne during play. In this experimental study, contaminated sand samples were “played with” inside a Class A asbestos enclosure by an asbestos technician wearing protective equipment. Air samples collected were analysed using a combination of light and electron microscopy undertaken by two independent laboratories. 90% of tested craft sands released asbestos fibres into the air during play activities. Some fibres met the criteria for respirability. Air samples taken during experiments using moulding sand samples did not show any airborne asbestos fibres; however, analytical detection limits for this study were high. This demonstrates that the potential risk from asbestos in the product can create a real risk from fibres in the air; however, the magnitude of this risk has yet to be determined by further research. Nevertheless, no amount of risk of asbestos exposure through toys is acceptable so the most practical way to eliminate this risk would be to avoid the use of artificial sand products in toys or similar consumer products.
items.authors: Terri-Ann Berry, Joanne Low, Gregor Steinhorn, Jason Milner, Elena Belluso, Jasmine Rita Petriglieri

items.title: Non-Covalent Interactions Directed Azobenzene Crystals: Photoisomerization-Induced Melting and Melt-Mediated Polymorphism
items.abstract: Azobenzene molecular crystals have emerged as a compelling class of stimuli-responsive materials, yet the structural factors that determine whether a given crystal bends, melts, or remains entirely inert under UV irradiation are far from understood. Here, we investigate a series of eight structurally homologous 2,2′-dihydroxyazobenzene derivatives (Azo-0 to Azo-7) in which terminal functional groups (‒OH vs. ‒OMe) and pendant alkyl spacer length are independently varied, allowing the contributions of intramolecular conformation, intermolecular packing topology, and lattice compliance to be disentangled. Single-crystal Xray diffraction (SCXRD), UV-vis spectroscopy, differential scanning calorimetry (DSC), together with thermal-stage polarized optical microscopy, reveal two mechanistically distinct melting pathways. The central finding is that an intramolecular O-H···N hydrogen bond, present in four derivatives (Azo-0, Azo-1, Azo-3, Azo-5), forms a pseudo-six-membered chelate ring that locks the azobenzene core in its planar trans conformation, fully suppressing photoisomerization in both solution and solid state. Removal of this intramolecular constraint through ‒OMe substitution liberates the azobenzene core in Azo-2, Azo-4, Azo-6, and Azo-7, enabling efficient and fully reversible cis-trans photoisomerization with visible-light-driven recovery. Critically, irradiation of these unlocked crystals below their equilibrium melting points (Ts Tm) triggers rapid, cooperative crystal-to-liquid transitions that are absent in the dark and under 456 nm light irradiation, establishing photoisomerization-induced lattice strain—not photothermal heating—as the operative mechanism. The sole outlier, Azo-5, melts under intense UV irradiation through a purely photothermal pathway, consistent with its locked conformation and strong 370 nm light absorption. Additionally, Azo-7 undergoes a thermally driven solid, liquid, solid polymorphic transformation: melt-recrystallization converts the high-melting polymorph Azo-7α (Tm ≈ 59 °C) into a structurally distinct, lower-melting polymorph Azo-7β (Tm ≈ 42 °C), demonstrating that thermal history is itself an independent handle for programming crystal packing. These findings translate directly into three molecular design principles for photomechanical organic crystals: phenolic OH gates the photoisomerization switch via intramolecular hydrogen bonding; alkyl chain length tunes lattice compliance and packing dimensionality; and melt-mediated crystals provide access to structurally and thermally distinct polymorphic forms.
items.authors: Ritika Kadiyan, Saptarshi Datta, Jagan Rajamoni, Nicholas Johnson, Jinjia Xu, JINJIA XU

items.title: Hydrogen-Bond-Induced Dual Structural Response in Amide-Functionalized Self-Assembled Monolayers
items.abstract: Internal functionalization can reorganize intermolecular interactions across a self-assembled monolayer (SAM), yet its depth-dependent consequences remain poorly understood. Here, molecular dynamics simulations and vibrational sum-frequency generation (VSFG) spectroscopy reveal a dual structural response in N-(2-mercaptoethyl)heptanamide SAMs on Au(111). A persistent intermolecular hydrogen-bond network suppresses conformational fluctuations between the Au-S interface and the amide plane. Above this plane, however, the larger volume of the amide increases alkyl-chain separation and weakens van der Waals coupling and enhances conformational flexibility with temperature. Thus, a hydrogen-bond-stabilized, solid-like lower region coexists with a weakly coupled, liquid-like upper region. Simulated VSFG spectra reproduce the observed terminal CH3 stretching-mode intensities, including the enhanced asymmetric response. This response occurs without a correspondingly large average methyl tilt angle because inequivalent molecular environments produce broad, heterogeneous orientation distributions. Consequently, the conventional assignment of a single methyl tilt angle from VSFG intensity ratio breaks down for internally functionalized SAMs.
items.authors: Saima Sadiq, Hojeong Yoon, Junhyeok Park, Kyungwon Kwak, Minhaeng Cho

items.title: Playing Domino with Carbon: Electrochemical CO2 Reduction to Methanol with Cobalt Phthalocyanine
items.abstract: Electrochemical reduction of carbon dioxide to methanol represents one of the most demanding transformations in CO 2 conversion, requiring the management of a six-electron, six-proton sequence while suppressing competing pathways toward carbon monoxide, formate, and hydrogen evolution. Among molecular electrocatalysts, cobalt phthalocyanine (CoPc) has emerged as a unique molecular platform capable of extending CO 2 reduction beyond CO through a domino-like cascade of protoncoupled electron transfer steps. Its square-planar Co-N 4 coordination environment provides metalcentered redox couples that enables CO 2 activation at the Co(I) state and stabilizes key intermediates within a narrow adsorption-energy window compatible with further hydrogenation. This review examines the fundamental and applied aspects of CoPc-mediated electrochemical CO 2 and CO reduction to methanol. The effects of ring substitution, axial ligation, and support-induced distortions on redox potentials, orbital interactions, and intermediate binding energetics were analyzed. Particular attention was devoted to solvation-coupled proton-coupled electron transfer, cation effects, and electric double-layer structure, which collectively governed CO retention and sequential hydrogenation toward CH 3 OH. Immobilization strategies on carbon nanotubes and related supports were discussed in relation to molecular dispersion, electronic coupling, and stability under flow-cell operation. Finally, scalability and sustainability are assessed through life-cycle considerations and green-chemistry metrics applied to phthalocyanine synthesis and device integration. Despite these advances, the field remains limited by catalyst deactivation, incomplete comparability among electrochemical setups and the frequent lack of standardized metrics for methanol quantification under device-relevant conditions. By connecting molecular design interfacial microenvironment, reactor architecture and sustainable catalyst synthesis, this review identifies the key directions required to move CoPc-based systems from promising molecular models toward technologically credible CO 2 -to-methanol electrolysis.
items.authors: Venanzio Raglione, Federica Palmeri, Abdolhamid Khodadadi, Gloria Zanotti, Mahmoud Zendehdel, Roberto Flammini

items.title: Advances in Multiscale Computational Modeling of 2D Nanomaterials for Solar Cells: From Interface Design to Fabrication and Stability
items.abstract: Two-dimensional (2D) nanomaterials provide a versatile platform for next-generation solar cells because their electronic structure, optical response, carrier transport, and interfacial chemistry can be engineered across multiple scales. However, photovoltaic performance and operational stability are governed not only by intrinsic material properties but also by coupled processes involving charge redistribution, interfacial recombination, ion migration, thermal transport, degradation, and fabrication-dependent microstructure. This review presents a closed-loop multiscale computational framework for the design, fabrication, and optimization of 2D-material-enabled solar cells. Density functional theory (DFT) and related quantum-mechanical methods are discussed for predicting band structure, band alignment, charge transfer, defect states, and optical properties, while molecular dynamics (MD) simulations address structural stability, ion migration, thermal effects, interfacial dynamics, and degradation. Finite element method (FEM)/COMSOL and device-scale models connect material-level descriptors to charge transport, recombination, thermal behavior, and photovoltaic metrics. Machine learning (ML) further enables high-throughput screening, property prediction, processing optimization, and inverse design. Particular emphasis is placed on bridging the simulation-to-fabrication gap by linking processing variables, including concentration, flake dimensions, functionalization, deposition, annealing, and interface formation, to realized structure and device performance. Experimental characterization and feedback are incorporated to refine computational models and guide subsequent design decisions. Overall, integrating quantum, atomistic, device-scale, data-driven, and fabrication-aware approaches provides a pathway toward efficient, stable, reproducible, and scalable 2D-material-based photovoltaic technologies.
items.authors: Iman Najafipour, Santanu Chaudhuri

items.title: Establishing Optical-Spin Interfaces in Luminescent Organic Diradicals using Spin-selective Symmetry-breaking Charge Transfer
items.abstract: Luminescent organic diradicals based on tris(2,4,6-trichlorophenyl)methyl (TTM) radicals have shown promise as optical-spin interfaces important for quantum sensing. The optically driven spin polarization mechanisms of existing TTM diradicals remain limited by non-selective singlet-triplet intersystem crossing (ISC) pathways, which restrict optically detected magnetic resonance (ODMR) contrast. Two TTM-based diradicals were prepared in which the two TTM subunits are linked at the para positions of one of their phenyls. Fully substituting the resulting biphenyl linkage between the radical centers with chlorines gives diradical 1, in which the two phenyls constituting the linkage are nearly orthogonal to one another. Subsequent replacement of the remaining four para positions of the TTM phenyls with p-tolyl groups gives diradical 2. Following photoexcitation of these diradicals to their triplet excited states, they undergo symmetry-breaking charge transfer to form a diamagnetic ion pair followed by charge recombination to form a spinpolarized triplet state. Diradical 2 shows spin-selective intersystem crossing from the triplet excited state resulting in an ODMR spectrum, while diradical 1 does not. These results show that spin-selective decay channels from the triplet excited state are a necessary requirement for establishing a spin-optical interface in TTM-based diradicals.
items.authors: Yixi Wang, Kathryn R. Peinkofer, Jonathan R. Palmer, Kyle T. Kairys, Rafael López-Arteaga, Ryan M. Young

items.title: A Biomimetic Ion-Selective Transistor-Coupled Droplet Bilayer for Integrated Chemical Sensing, Synaptic Plasticity, and Associative Learning
items.abstract: Integration of sensing, memory, and learning within a single device remains a major challenge for bioinspired electronic interfaces. Here, we report a transistor-coupled droplet bilayer (TCDB) in which selective ion transport across a biomimetic lipid membrane directly controls the electronic state of an organic electrochemical transistor (OECT). Incorporating valinomycin ionophores into the droplet interface bilayer membrane enables the selective transport of K + ions while suppressing the response to other cations. Increased concentration of valinomycin in the membrane decreases the resistance of the membrane to K + ions, producing correspondingly faster and stronger transistor gating responses. Using this membrane-mediated gating mechanism, the TCDB distinguishes K + concentrations from 3.5-20 mM through concentration-dependent response kinetics. Beyond sensing, the finite ion transport and relaxation times impart history dependence to the transistor's response, producing a ~330 mV hysteresis window, reversible analog conductance programming, paired-pulse facilitation, post-tetanic potentiation, and spike-rate- and timing-dependent plasticity. Repeated stimulation further extends the lifetime of programmed conductance states, directly linking selective ion transport dynamics to short-term memory. We further demonstrate, for the first time in a TCDB, a dual-gate architecture comprising two independently addressable lipid bilayers coupled to a shared OECT channel. The dual-gate TCDB integrates multiple ionic inputs within a common channel and enables associative learning through the temporal pairing of independent gate stimuli. Together, these results establish membrane resistance, selective ion transport, and ionic relaxation as physical parameters that simultaneously govern chemical sensing, memory, and synaptic adaptation, providing a biomimetic route toward ion-selective neuromorphic devices in which sensing and information processing arise from the same membrane-mediated ionic dynamics.
items.authors: Nawara Tanzee Minim, Essraa A Hussein, Beliz Utebay, Jonathan Rivnay, Neha Kamat, Stephen A Sarles

items.title: Ring-Conformer Ensembles Improve AutoDock Vina Docking; an Ant Colony Makes Them Affordable
items.abstract: In standard preparation, AutoDock Vina holds five-and six-membered non-aromatic rings at their input pucker, and our failure analysis of 4 509 runs against searchreachable native poses shows what that costs: with the accurate preset, the search itself fails in only 6.5% of runs, while ring conformations, ranking and the scoring function account for most of the rest. Docking up to four ring conformers per ligand and keeping the best-scoring pose repairs part of that gap for every search we tested, raising top-1 success by 5.5 to 7.4 percentage points for Vina’s Monte Carlo at exhaustiveness 1 and 8 alike and for the two presets we tested it with in the continuous ant colony optimization (ACOR) search we built into Vina; a cost-matched control that docks the input conformer K times shows that most of this gain is ring geometry rather than repeated sampling (+8.9 against +2.9 points with the accurate preset). Because the ensemble multiplies the cost of docking, its price is what limits its use, and this is where the ant colony earns its place: it reaches the pose accuracy of Vina at exhaustiveness 1 with about nine times fewer scoring evaluations, so an ensemble of up to four conformers with the accurate preset costs 8.5 s per ligand on one core and reaches 52.7% top-1 success, against 50.4% for Vina at exhaustiveness 8 (37.9 s) and 46.1% for the same ensemble driven by exhaustiveness 1. Ring ensembles with Vina’s own Monte Carlo at exhaustiveness 8 are the most accurate arm we measured (56.2%), at thirteen times that cost, so the choice between them is one of budget rather than of search.
items.authors: Suleyman Selim Cinaroglu

items.title: Access to Broad Organosulfur Chemical Space by Iron MHAT Sulfinamidation of Olefins
items.abstract: Organosulfur groups, particularly in the S(VI) oxidation state, have seen increased adoption within the medicinal chemistry community in recent years. Although certain groups such as sulfones and sulfonamides have been utilized since the advent of modern drug development, others like sulfonimidamides or sulfoximines have only recently seen utilization. These desirable functionalities provide access to new chemical space and intellectual property while enabling the optimization of key ADME properties. Herein, we disclose a new method for the construction of these key organosulfur motifs via the hydrosulfinamidation of olefins. This transformation relies upon stoichiometric, low-cost Fe(acac)3 to interconvert an olefin into an alkyl radical via MHAT, which is then trapped by a sulfinylamine (e.g. TrNSO) to deliver S(IV) species, with exclusive Markovnikov selectivity. These sulfinamides serve as diversifiable lynchpins for readily accessing their aza-S(VI) congeners. Furthermore, we demonstrate this transformation’s practicality at preparative scale ( 20-grams of product), enabling access to complex organosulfur modalities using inexpensive reagents and simple conditions.
items.authors: Sylvia Kaydos-Daniels, Zachary F. Murphy, Erik C. Vik, Noah B. Bissonnette

items.title: From Publications to Physical Knowledge Models: Transferable physical understanding for AI-native experimental science
items.abstract: Scientific communication has repeatedly accelerated when the objects used to preserve and exchange knowledge became easier to validate, search, and reuse. The scientific paper remains a human-readable compression of a richer scientific state: quantitative physical and observational models, their uncertainty and validity, and the evidence that supports or challenges them. We propose Physical Knowledge Models (PKMs) as explicit, versioned, composable, and transferable representations of this state. The intellectual object per se is not fundamentally new: expert mental models, comprehensive textbooks, and domain model repositories already integrate equations, mechanisms, observations, and validity judgments. The proposed advance is to make that integrated understanding machine-readable and directly connected to experimentation. Broad PKMs can be projected into reduced experiment-specific models; local evidence produces versioned knowledge proposals rather than silently overwriting community knowledge; and a Knowledge Integration Layer aligns partially overlapping models, evaluates evidence and beliefs, preserves competing branches, and exposes contradictions requiring further tests. Because the ontology itself can change, PKMs retain persistent links to original measurements, sample histories, and instrument and decision traces so that prior evidence can be reinterpreted under revised concepts and models. Coupled to experimental planning, this creates a structured route from shared knowledge to local experiment and back. Data, code, digital twins, and agents remain essential, but they become mechanisms for populating, interrogating, testing, and updating durable physical knowledge rather than substitutes for it.
items.authors: Sergei V. Kalinin, Boris N. Slautin, Sheryl Sanchez, Yu Liu, Mahshid Ahmadi, Mehmet Aydeniz

items.title: An Epidemic of Misbranding: Marketplace Surveillance of MGM-15 and Kratom Alkaloids in Commercially Available Tablets by QuEChERS -LCMS/MS
items.abstract: The commercial kratom market increasingly includes concentrated and semi-synthetic products, including 7-hydroxymitragynine (7-OH) and dihydro-7-hydroxymitragynine (MGM-15), whose prevalence and concentration across the marketplace remain largely uncharacterized. Kratom alkaloids, namely mitragynine (MIT) and its diastereomers, share the same molecular formula and connectivity. The product ions commonly monitored are not structurally specific, further exacerbated by the semi-synthetic derivates. Reliable identification and quantitation of the alkaloid class require chromatographic resolution in addition to mass spectrometric detection. Here, we present a validated QuEChERS extraction protocol and LC-MS/MS method for the simultaneous determination of ten kratom alkaloids in 42 commercially available pressed tablets. The method was linear from 0.05 to 2.0 μg/mL (mean R2 0.992), with limits of detection ranging from 0.0005-0.044 μg/mL, recoveries of 80-120% for seven of ten analytes, and interday precision below 12.5% for nine of ten analytes. MGM-15 was detected in 31 tablets (73.8%) at a median concentration of 6.62 mg/g. Twenty-two of 26 quantitative label claims were not met; in three products, the claimed alkaloids were nearly absent despite total alkaloid content exceeding the stated claim by more than sevenfold. Two products marketed without kratom claims contained eight and nine of the ten target alkaloids, respectively. Combining MGM-15 detection with the 7-OH:MIT ratio identified 34 of 42 products (81%) as semi-synthetically modified. These findings emphasize the need for reliable, robust, and label-independent analytical surveillance of this evolving product class.
items.authors: Ana Barovic, Mitchell L. Ellinwood, Shelby Blanchart, Alexandra E. McDevitt, Giovanni A. Ramirez, Joseph Hamilton

items.title: A Novel Mononuclear Nickel Complex as a Precatalyst for Ionomer-Dependent Oxygen Evolution Reaction Activity
items.abstract: In electrocatalytic water splitting, ionomer-catalyst interactions can significantly influence electrochemical performance. Molecular metal–organic complexes offer a tractable platform to investigate such interactions. Here we report a novel nickel–2methylimidazole complex, [Ni(2-MeIm)4(NO3)]NO3, with Ni@N4O2 coordination environment. The structure of this new material is established by single-crystal X-ray diffraction and supported by vibrational spectroscopy and thermal analysis. We evaluate the complex as an oxygen evolution reaction precatalyst in 1.0mol L−1 KOH and show that its apparent activity depends strongly on the ionomer used in the catalyst ink. With Aemion+, an anion-exchange ionomer the catalyst reaches 10mAcm−2 current density at an overpotential of 0.331V, whereas the same catalyst formulated with Nafion exhibits a markedly reduced activity with an overpotential of 0.403V. The impedance spectra recorded at 1.6V vs RHE show considerable differences in charge-transfer resistances between the two formulations, consistent with differences in interfacial charge-transfer kinetics. We propose that specific catalyst–ionomer interactions may modulate active-site accessibility and the in situ transformation of the molecular precursor into catalytically competent NiOOH.
items.authors: Neethu Kochukunnel Varghese, Serena De Negri, Pavlo Solokha, Antonio Comite

items.title: Scientific World Models: Toward Closed-Loop Scientific Intelligence
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence is moving from task-specific scientific tools toward foundation models, generative design, research agents, and autonomous laboratories. Despite this progress, most systems remain organized around isolated predictions or local workflows. They rarely maintain an evolving account of scientific objects, predict the consequences of interventions, or learn systematically from computational and experimental evidence. This article introduces scientific world models as a core paradigm for closed-loop scientific intelligence. A scientific world model reconstructs the physical state of a scientific object and its corresponding epistemic state—what is known, uncertain, or contested—from partial, multimodal, and instrument-mediated observations. It models action-conditioned state transitions, explores plausible futures under scientific constraints, and supports the selection of measurements, simulations, experiments, and process interventions according to scientific value, information gain, cost, feasibility, and risk. The new evidence then updates the state, hypotheses, and subsequent actions. On this basis, we propose a three-layer architecture of scientific perception, cognition, and action. Perception turns the physical world into traceable scientific observations and state representations. Cognition combines data-driven models with scientific laws, mechanistic knowledge, and simulation to interpret current states and reason about possible futures. Action connects model reasoning to computation, instruments, experiments, and physical processes. We further distinguish the scientific world model core from foundation models, scientific agents, digital twins, and autonomous laboratories, and outline domain instantiations, maturity levels, evaluation criteria, and open technical challenges. This framework provides a common basis for developing scientific AI systems that can observe, reason, act, and improve through evidence.
items.authors: Huan Wang, Zhenlin Zhao, Siming Dong

items.title: Substituent Effects Govern the Fidelity of Responsive Persulfide Donors
items.abstract: Persulfides (RSSH) are important intermediates in sulfur transfer and trafficking in redox biology, yet the intrinsic chemistry of these molecules complicates the design of small molecule donors that deliver persulfides on demand. Here, we investigate how specific parameters of both the persulfide payload and disulfide structure in selfimmolative donors influence persulfide release, H2S formation, and the susceptibility to degradation by biological thiols. Notably, we demonstrate that many common structures used for persulfide delivery likely do not produce the intended payloads due to a combination of unexpected thiol-disulfide exchange reactions prior to donor activation or subsequent instability of the released persulfide. Using a family of esterase-activated donor constructs, we show that geminal dimethyl substitution at the benzylic position accelerates self-immolative payload release and decreases unwanted thiol-disulfide exchange prior to donor activation. We also establish that steric protection of the release persulfide strongly influences its downstream fate, with unhindered cysteinederived persulfides generating substantially more H2S than sterically protected penicillamine-derived systems. Importantly, thiol exchange studies reveal that insufficiently protected caged disulfides can be consumed rapidly by GSH before trigger activation, thereby diminishing donor integrity. Together, these results establish that the functionality of persulfide donors is governed by steric protection, which influences the competing pathways of donor activation, thiol exchange, persulfide persistence, and H2S formation. More broadly, this work establishes design principles for high-fidelity persulfide delivery and provides a framework for interpreting biological studies in which persulfide donors may participate in competing sulfur transfer and sulfur release pathways.
items.authors: Ismail Ismail, Michael D. Pluth

items.title: From prediction to process control: a critical review of machine learning in reactive dyeing of cotton
items.abstract: Abstract Reactive exhaust dyeing of cotton uses large amounts of water, salt, alkali and heat, partly because the recipe and programme are fixed when a batch starts. This review asks whether learned models, acting on the machine during a batch, have been shown to reduce that consumption. An OpenAlex search (2003 to September 2026, 862 records) and web searching identified 27 primary studies of learned, rule-based, model-based or search-based methods, or inline monitoring, in reactive dyeing of cotton. Each was coded by setting and by how far its output reached the process. Twenty-two stop at offline prediction, three only measure the bath, one advises an operator and one acts automatically; 24 are laboratory studies. No included study documents a learned model automatically changing an outcome-level decision (dye, salt or alkali quantity or timing, temperature programme, or rinse endpoint) during a batch. The one automatic controller, a fixed rule timing alkali injection at pilot scale, is not learned. A check on 135 studies of all fibres agreed. Reported fixation spans 40 to 70%, and no study has measured how much of the shortfall control could recover. Two priorities follow: measuring that share, and a matched-batch trial of learned, rule-based and operator control.
items.authors: Sk. Mainuddin, Tinon Turja Majumder, Md Shajjad Khan Faisal

items.title: Detection of Molecular Oxidation States in Dye Sensitized Solar Cells-Relevant Organic Dyes Eosin Y Through Optical UV/Vis Absorption Spectrum Changes
items.abstract: This study investigates oxidative degradation mechanisms of the non-metallic organic dye Eosin Y in order to examine precisely how they influence the light-harvesting efficiency (LHE) of Dye-Sensitized Solar Cells (DSSCs). Density Functional Theory (DFT) and Time-Dependent DFT (TD-DFT) computations with ABINIT are used to construct the molecular geometry and electronic configuration of the dye in its neutral form, oxidized adduct state , and oxidized state with excited electron. From the basic Highest Occupied Molecular Orbital (HOMO) to its Lowest Unoccupied Molecular Orbital (LUMO) energy gaps and Ultraviolet-Visible (UV/Vis) absorbance spectra obtained from the computations, it is evident that both photo-oxidation and oxygen addition render the molecule inactive, resulting in up to 90% reduction in extinction coefficient and near disappearance of the visible absorption spectrum. In summary, this project provides a molecular-level interpretation of the efficiency reduction experienced in organic DSSCs due to oxidative degradation.
items.authors: Alibek Kadralinov

items.title: Mean First-Passage-Time-Directed Bias Optimization with Gaussian-Kernel Markov Models
items.abstract: Rare transitions limit the direct simulation of molecular kinetics and complicate the design of enhanced-sampling biases that accelerate specific events without obscuring their mechanism. We develop a data-driven framework in which biased trajectory data are combined using dynamic histogram analysis and represented by either conventional grids or normalized kernel-anchor memberships to construct finite row-stochastic kinetic models. These models are used to adapt a bounded bias by directly minimizing an absorbing mean first-passage time (MFPT) objective, while reactive-current diagnostics independently assess whether accelerated trajectories preserve the reference transition mechanism. We first test the kernel-induced representation in equilibrium free-energy reconstruction and then apply the kinetic optimization framework to progressively more challenging rareevent problems, including membrane permeation, multidimensional barrier crossing, and a metastable molecular rearrangement. The benchmark calculations show that MFPT-directed biasing can efficiently promote target arrival and that soft kernel states provide a flexible alternative to rigid spatial discretization. At the same time, pathway analysis shows that faster arrival does not imply preservation of the underlying transition mechanism. A confounded high-dimensional stress test further exposes the limitations of projected kinetic models when the relevant dynamical coordinates are unresolved.
items.authors: Qingying Wang, Tingyue Zhou, Baowen Li, Christian Jorgensen, Edina Rosta

items.title: RealBind: a leakage-controlled benchmark for experimental PXRD and Raman structure retrieval
items.abstract: We present RealBind, a benchmark for retrieving crystal structures from experimental powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD) and Raman spectra. It contains 3,288 curated candidate structures, of which 1,468 have linked measured PXRD patterns, and 16,005 experimental Raman spectra, of which 10,547 are linked to structures. We provide quality-control records, prototype-held-out and composition-held-out splits, and evaluation protocols that state candidate-library size and the chemical information available at retrieval time. On a 492-candidate prototype-held-out library, a contrastive model trained on simulated PXRD reaches 78.5% Recall@10 on simulated queries but 5.3% on measured queries; physics-inspired corruption raises measured-query Recall@10 to 34.4%. A model-free correlation against simulated candidate patterns, with no preprocessing beyond the common Q-grid resampling and the measuredwindow mask, achieves 82.8% Recall@10 on the same test library. In a separate split comparison, 44% of random-split test structures have a structure-matched training counterpart; measured-query Recall@10 is 59.1% on that split versus 20.7% on the prototype-held-out split, although test populations and libraries also differ. Holding the trained model and 420 queries fixed, restricting the candidate library and pre-screening candidates by the ground-truth element set of the query’s structure, used as an oracle chemistry-conditioned diagnostic, raises Recall@10 from 27.1% to 99.1%; 37.6% of filtered queries have a single candidate. A Raman-to-structure baseline reaches 34.7% Recall@10 on heldout mineral spectra against 979 candidates in the pooled evaluation and 45.7% on the 485-candidate test-only library, which includes no validation structures. RealBind provides an experimental test bed for comparing learned methods with simple simulation-based matching under explicit, leakage-aware protocols.
items.authors: Preyansh Srivastava

items.title: Bridging Azahelicene Enables Circularly Polarized Luminescence in a Dinuclear Ytterbium(III) Single-Molecule Magnet
items.abstract: Modern coordination chemistry employs increasingly sophisticated building blocks to design compounds and molecule-based materials with unusual combinations of properties relevant to emerging technologies. A notable example is the incorporation of helicenes as chiral ligands in luminescent and magnetic lanthanide complexes, which can give rise to circularly polarized luminescence (CPL) or magneto-chiral dichroism (MChD). Lanthanides are particularly wellsuited for CPL owing to their intraconfigurational 4 f -4 f transitions with long excited-state lifetimes and sharp, well-defined emission bands. Herein we present a new low-coordinate Yb III dinuclear complex [{Yb(BHT) 3 } 2 (azahelicene)] (BHT = 2,6-di-tert-butyl-4-methylphenolate; azahelicene = benzo[4,5]imidazo[1,2-a]benzo[4,5]imidazo[2,1-k][1,10]phenanthroline), where the two Yb III luminophores are bridged by the optically pure azahelicene ligand as the source of chirality. Additionally, the reported compound is a single-molecule magnet (SMM) thanks to the synthetic strategy that enables control of the coordination sphere around the Yb III ion. The combined experimental and theoretical magneto-optical studies conducted for both enantiomers of [{Yb(BHT) 3 } 2 (azahelicene)] reveal a direct link between the crystal structure, the related crystalfield splitting, and the observed magnetic and chiroptical properties. First of all, the introduction of the azahelicene into the coordination sphere of the achiral luminescent Yb(BHT) 3 parent compound was achieved with the retention of its SMM behavior. Most importantly, however, its incorporation as an integral component of the molecule enabled the observation of circularly polarized near-infrared (NIR) emission from Yb III . Three CPL bands were detected in the NIR, including the most intense signal at 978 nm with the luminescence dissymmetry factor glum = |0.035|, as well as a rare CPL emission above 1050 nm.
items.authors: Gabriela Handzlik, Salauat R. Kiraev, Mathieu Gascoin, Maxime Grasser, Stephan Guy, Bruno Baguenard

items.title: Precision of Gaussian, Lorentzian, and pseudo-Voigt peak fitting under Gaussian noise
items.abstract: Discriminating subtle differences in measured signals is essential to scientific discovery. Knowledge of the attainable precision limits of fitted peak parameters and the physical and statistical factors that determine them provides a rational basis for improving this capability. However, without a common framework for comparing peak shapes and noise statistics, universal features of peak-parameter precision remain difficult to distinguish from those specific to a profile or noise regime, thereby hindering the development of general guidance for peak fitting and measurement design. Here we analyze Gaussian, Lorentzian, and pseudo-Voigt profiles in the Gaussian-noise (GN) limit using the same information-theoretic parameterization established for the Poisson-noise (PN) limit, enabling direct comparisons across peak shapes and noise regimes. Using the Fisher information matrix and the Cramér–Rao inequality, we derive analytical lower bounds on the standard deviations of peak intensity (I), center (ωc), full width at half maximum (Γ), area (A), and mixing parameter (η) and validate them against numerical calculations and Monte Carlo simulations. This unified framework addresses a long-standing question in peak analysis: whether intensity ratios or area ratios can be estimated more precisely. Whereas PN-limit theory predicts greater precision for area ratios across all three profiles, our GN-limit analysis shows that this advantage disappears for Gaussian and Lorentzian profiles and reverses for a pseudo-Voigt model with free η. Thus, neither I- nor A-based quantification is intrinsically more precise; their relative precision is governed by peak shape, parameter covariance, and noise statistics. This helps explain why experimental comparisons have not yielded a unique answer and provides a principled basis for selecting the more precise quantity. Fisher-information densities further show that information on I is concentrated in the peak core, information on ωc is concentrated on the flanks, and information on Γ and η extends into the wings. This indicates that precise estimation of Γ and η requires the fitting range to extend sufficiently into the peak wings. Finally, using Raman spectroscopy as an example, we combine the theory with detector-noise models to predict attainable precision before data acquisition and quantify how measurement conditions and instrument performance affect precision. The framework supports quantitative optimization of measurement conditions and instrument design to improve analytical precision across diverse signal-analysis applications.
items.authors: Yuuki Hagiwara, Tatsu Kuwatani

items.title: Comprehensive Quantum Chemical Interaction Analysis of Whole Protein–Ligand Structures in BindingDB Using the Fragment Molecular Orbital Method
items.abstract: Understanding protein–ligand interactions based on their electronic states is important for elucidating molecular recognition and supporting structure-based drug discovery. In this study, we performed fragment molecular orbital (FMO) calculations, a quantum chemical approach, for a comprehensive set of experimentally determined protein–ligand complexes derived from BindingDB. Ligand–amino acid residue interactions were quantitatively characterized using inter-fragment interaction energies (IFIEs) and pair interaction energy decomposition analysis (PIEDA), and were compared with molecular mechanics (MM) interaction energies. The comparison revealed residue- and interaction-dependent differences between the FMO and MM descriptions, with particularly distinct behavior for interactions involving aromatic residues. Comprehensive IFIE/PIEDA analysis further revealed characteristic energetic contributions associated with amino acid residue type and ligand charge, including dispersion contributions involving aromatic residues and charge-transfer contributions associated with hydrogen-bonding interactions. A case study of MAPK14 demonstrated that the resulting dataset can identify residue regions commonly involved in ligand recognition and distinguish residue-level interaction patterns among individual ligands. These results provide a systematic quantum chemical perspective on diverse protein–ligand interactions and establish a quantum chemical resource for complementing structural, experimental, and conventional MM-based analyses.
items.authors: Shuhei Miyakawa, Naoko Konami, Ruri Mihata, Rikuto Osaki, Ayaka Masuda, Tomoka Taguchi

items.title: Screening Protein Conformational Responses by Molecular Friction Sensing
items.abstract: Small-molecule drugs often act by stabilizing specific protein conformations, yet most biophysical screening platforms report binding affinity or kinetics without directly capturing structural response. Here we introduce molecular friction sensing (MFS), a screening-compatible approach that detects ligand-induced changes in protein conformation through changes in hydrodynamic drag exerted on electrically switchable DNA origami nanolevers. Across a diverse protein panel and under physiological conditions, the method quantitatively reports protein size and resolves ligand-dependent conformational shifts with sub-Angström sensitivity. In maltodextrin-binding protein, cognate and non-cognate maltodextrins produced distinct friction signatures that mirrored their biological roles. In a carbonic anhydrase screen, molecular friction sensing identified compound-dependent conformational responses among SPR-validated binders, revealing that affinity and kinetics do not predict structural outcome. Molecular friction sensing therefore adds a structural dimension to interaction analysis and provides a route to prioritize drug candidates by the conformations they induce.
items.authors: Pablo Porragas Paseiro, Lukas Aufinger, Alfred Kick, Tereza Jahodová, Veronica Hamer, Ulrich Rant

items.title: Tautomeric Diversity in the Baicalein Radical Cation: EPR Fingerprints of a Traditional Chinese Medicine Antioxidant
items.abstract: The radical cation of baicalein, the principal bioactive flavonoid of the Traditional Chinese Medicine herb Scutellaria baicalensis, has been predicted to undergo an intramolecular proton transfer from the 5-hydroxyl to the 4carbonyl oxygen. This tautomerization produces two distinct electronic configurations, denoted C1 (canonical) and C2 (proton-transferred), whose relative populations and reactivities may determine the antioxidant behavior of the molecule within the single-electron-transfer–proton-transfer (SET-PT) pathway. The two tautomers have not, however, been distinguished experimentally; their UV-Vis signatures differ only subtly. Here we report the first EPR hyperfine fingerprints of the two tautomers, computed at the DFT/UM06-2X/EPR-III level across fourteen media. Three qualitatively distinct signatures separate C1 from C2 (values in water): a near-doubling of the isotropic coupling at the 5-hydroxyl oxygen O5 (from −5.88 to −11.77 G), a sign reversal at the aromatic carbon C5 (from +4.83 to −5.77 G), and the disappearance of the mobile proton’s coupling (from −3.49 to +0.30 G). All three qualitative signatures are preserved across dielectric constants from 1 to 78, making them robust diagnostics of the tautomeric state in a wide range of environments. Because EPR hyperfine couplings report directly on spin density rather than on electronic transitions, they provide an unambiguous experimental handle for detecting the tautomeric diversity of the baicalein radical cation.
items.authors: Ioan Bâldea, Ioan Baldea

items.title: The Oxidation of Drug Molecules Using the Peroxygenase Activity of a Bacterial Family of Cytochrome P450 Enzymes
items.abstract: Cytochrome P450 (CYP) enzymes with peroxygenase activity can use H2O2 as the sole oxidant which is beneficial for biocatalytic applications. We investigated the peroxygenase activity of CYP105D18 from Streptomyces laurentii. The modification of the acid-alcohol pair in the I-helix through protein engineering reduced the peroxygenase activity for papaverine oxidation by 6-fold compared to the wild-type (WT) enzyme. We identified the oxidation metabolites as papaverine N-oxide, and two newly identified metabolites that arise from O-demethylation. The major O-demethylation metabolite was characterized as 6-O-desmethyl papaverine. Given the higher peroxygenase activity of the unmodified CYP105D18 enzyme we explored if another enzyme from the same CYP subfamily had similar activity.
