Nocturnal warming is accompanied by a significant rise in near-surface water vapor pressure (+0.15 hPa per decade), whose detrended interannual variability correlates strongly with TN90p (r = 0.59), identifying the water-vapor greenhouse effect as a key driver of the faster warming of nights than days. Precipitation shows no significant national trend, except for very wet days (R90p, percentage of days with precipitation above the 90th percentile of wet days, +2.18% per decade) and a decline in rainy days (RR1, number of days with precipitation ≥ 1 mm, –4 days per decade). These results provide the first country-wide baseline of temperature and precipitation extremes for climate-risk assessment in Haiti.
items.authors: Armand Pierre, Carlo Destouches, Ralph Bathelemy, Dominique Boisson, Kelly Guerrier, Élisée Villiard

items.title: A Reproducible Typesetting Solution for Zsigmondy–Palmer Dental Notation
items.abstract: Zsigmondy–Palmer dental notation, still used in dentistry and dental education, has a two-dimensional, quadrant-based structure that is difficult to reproduce consistently in modern digital documents. Earlier digital approaches enabled symbol entry or rendering through specialized fonts, keyboard approximations, and character encoding, but the approaches reviewed here did not formalize quadrant-addressed content separately from document-level composition. This study aimed to define a structured representation that separates quadrant content from its two-dimensional placement, and to implement and technically validate it. We developed palmer.sty, a LaTeX package that arranges tooth identifiers and quadrant lines automatically from that structured input, so the notation can be edited and reused directly in the document source. We additionally developed palmer-type, a companion graphical user interface application that renders the same notation as reusable image output for word-processing and presentation software. Defined rendering and diagnostic checks support package operation across three LaTeX engines, and source-level functional tests support image export and Word conversion with experimental alternative text. The evidence presented here is limited to functional validation; usability, workflow efficiency, and comparative task performance were not evaluated. These tools complement the standardized Fédération Dentaire Internationale (FDI) system by supporting the consistent digital representation of Zsigmondy–Palmer notation in documents where it continues to be used.
items.authors: Yosuke Yamazaki, Saya Imaoka, Maki Yuguchi

items.title: Engineering Data Analysis Beyond Statistics vs. Machine Learning: A Review of Explanation, Prediction, Hybrid Modeling, and Responsible Decision Support
items.abstract: This structured narrative review explores how engineers select and evaluate traditional statistical, machine learning, mechanistic, and hybrid methods for explanation, prediction, and responsible decision support. We identified representative literature available through 2025 via iterative searches of Web of Science, Scopus, ScienceDirect, and Google Scholar, and conducted a thematic synthesis. We qualitatively assessed the credibility and relevance of the literature sources. Application areas covered include manufacturing, semiconductor processing, mechanical and materials systems, civil infrastructure, chemical processes, energy and construction, robotics, and greenhouse engineering (excluding healthcare). Comparisons included analytical objectives, data characteristics, hypotheses, interpretability, uncertainty, causality, physical consistency, validation, and deployment. The synthesis yielded three recurring conclusions. First, a method’s applicability depends on information content, dependency structure, operating conditions, and decision consequences, not dataset size or method labels. Second, statistical significance and predictive accuracy do not independently demonstrate causal validity, physical plausibility, or operational effectiveness. Reliable evaluation combines internal validation, feasible external testing, repeatable benchmarking against meaningful benchmarks, and deployment evaluation to address issues such as data leakage, distribution shift, and uneven error costs. Third, hybrid models are appropriate when complementary functionality is required, but the increased computational, validation, and maintenance burden must be justified; simpler, validated models may suffice. Physics-informed machine learning, gray-box models, and digital twins differ in their functional and integration requirements. This paper’s main contribution is a cross-domain decision-making architecture and practical selection guidelines that link engineering goals to modeling choices, validation requirements, decision thresholds, and operational measures. This framework does not rank algorithms or prescribe general workflows; instead, it supports domain-specific judgments about model suitability, uncertainty, security, cost, and human oversight.
items.authors: Hsuan-Yu Chen, Chiachung Chen

items.title: Competing Roles of Hollow-Particle Ascent and Smectite Structure Formation in Drying Patterns of Aqueous Sessile Droplets
items.abstract: This study examined how the volume fraction of fluorinated hectorite (Ht-F) and NaCl concentration affect the drying patterns of sessile droplets containing aluminosilicate hollow particles. Ht-F-only droplets formed low peripheral rings, whereas higher Ht-F fractions or NaCl concentrations promoted bump-like patterns. Hollow-particle-only droplets formed a well-defined core coffee-eye and a narrow peripheral ring. Ht-F addition produced extended coffee-eyes and wider rings. Hollow-particle ascent in water, observed in previous studies, provides a physical basis for interpreting central accumulation; individual vertical particle trajectories were not measured in the present drying droplets. Comparison using the apparent normalized ascent distance, Λapp, based on Stokes’ law indicated that the estimated increase in viscosity decreased Λapp and that ascent could become more influential with increasing particle size. DLVO analysis showed that increasing NaCl shortened the range of electrostatic repulsion. The core coffee-eye diameter varied nonmonotonically with NaCl concentration, suggesting that competition between interparticle interactions and particle transport may influence the extent of central accumulation. Without added NaCl, trace Ht-F was associated with a temporary coffee-eye that collapsed into a volcano-like pattern late in drying. The observed drying patterns are interpreted in terms of hollow-particle ascent, evaporation-induced outward transport, and Ht-F-induced viscosity increase and network formation. Transport and interaction calculations were used for semi-quantitative comparison based on initial conditions and simplified models.
items.authors: Hiroshi Kimura

items.title: Semiparametric Panel Generalized Additive Models for Separate Forecasting of GDP Growth and Inflation in African Economies
items.abstract: Reliable forecasts of GDP growth and price dynamics support macroeconomic monitoring and economic planning, particularly in heterogeneous African economies where macroeconomic relationships may vary across economic conditions. This study develops and evaluates separate semiparametric Panel Generalized Additive Models (Panel GAMs) to examine nonlinear conditional associations and forecast GDP growth and the inverse hyperbolic sine-transformed Consumer Price Index (IHS-CPI). We analyse quarterly panel data for 53 African economies covering 2005Q1–2025Q4. The models represent the effects of exchange rate, money supply, interest rate, and time using smooth functions while accounting for country-specific heterogeneity through country-level random effects. We evaluate out-of-sample forecasting performance against a Linear Mixed Model. The estimated smooth terms provide evidence of statistically significant nonlinear conditional associations for both GDP growth and IHS-CPI. The Panel GAM achieves adjusted R2 values of 0.230 for GDP growth and 0.709 for IHS-CPI, indicating stronger in-sample fit for IHS-CPI. For out-of-sample forecasting, the Panel GAM produces RMSE and MAE values of 3.465 and 2.027 for GDP growth and 1.669 and 1.211 for IHS-CPI, respectively, compared with 3.368 and 1.931 for GDP growth and 1.632 and 1.192 for IHS-CPI from the Linear Mixed Model. Thus, the Panel GAM does not achieve superior out-of-sample point-forecast accuracy relative to the Linear Mixed Model, although it provides a flexible framework for representing nonlinear conditional associations and country-specific heterogeneity.
items.authors: Ben Magabashele Malope, Retius Chifurira, Temesgen Zewotir, Knowledge Chinhamu

items.title: Biomarker Integration in the Perioperative Management of Early-Stage Non-Small-Cell Lung Cancer
items.abstract: The concept of personalized medicine has tremendous appeal—tailoring diagnosis and treatment to an individual, rather than a “one-size-fits-all” approach. The management of non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) has rapidly evolved toward strategies increasingly guided by tumor biology and precision oncology. The safety and significant efficacy of biomarker-directed therapies in metastatic disease have fueled interest in applying precision oncology to early-stage, operable NSCLC. Advances in molecular profiling have revealed that a substantial proportion of resected NSCLC harbor actionable driver mutations, enabling the integration of targeted therapies into the perioperative setting. The success of adjuvant epidermal growth factor receptor and anaplastic lymphoma kinase inhibition established a framework for biomarker-driven therapy and highlights the importance of comprehensive molecular testing at diagnosis. In parallel, perioperative immune checkpoint inhibitor-based strategies have expanded treatment options for appropriately selected patients, further emphasizing the importance of molecular profiling. Significant implementation gaps remain, including incomplete molecular testing, delayed results, inadequate tissue sampling, fragmented workflows, and disparities in access. Beyond clinically actionable driver mutations, emerging research highlights radiogenomics and advances in the use of circulating tumor DNA for minimal residual disease detection, with important implications for early recurrence detection and patient prognostication, although these technologies differ in clinical maturity. Collectively, these developments emphasize the molecular heterogeneity underlying early-stage NSCLC and the expanding role of biomarkers in guiding clinical decision-making. Integrating genomic, radiographic, and biologic markers into clinical workflows will be essential to refine risk stratification, personalize perioperative treatment strategies, and ultimately improve long-term oncologic outcomes.
items.authors: Emily P. Rabinovich, Linda W. Martin
items.title_zh: 早期非小细胞肺癌围手术期生物标志物整合管理
items.summary_zh: 个性化医学的理念在非小细胞肺癌（NSCLC）管理中逐渐得到应用，尤其是通过肿瘤生物学和精准肿瘤学指导的策略。研究表明，许多切除的NSCLC肿瘤中存在可靶向的驱动突变，这为围手术期整合靶向治疗提供了可能。辅助表皮生长因子受体和间变性淋巴瘤激酶抑制剂的成功应用，确立了生物标志物驱动治疗的框架，并强调了诊断时进行全面分子检测的重要性。同时，围手术期免疫检查点抑制剂的策略为适当选择的患者扩展了治疗选择，进一步突显了分子分析的重要性。然而，实施过程中仍存在分子检测不完整、结果延迟、组织取样不足、工作流程碎片化及获取资源不平等等问题。
items.l1_lead: 个性化医学在非小细胞肺癌的围手术期管理中逐渐应用，强调全面分子检测的重要性，以指导靶向治疗和免疫治疗的选择。
items.l2_summary:
个性化医学在非小细胞肺癌（NSCLC）管理中的应用日益受到重视，特别是在围手术期生物标志物整合管理方面。研究表明，许多切除的NSCLC肿瘤中存在可靶向的驱动突变，这为围手术期的靶向治疗提供了新的可能性。辅助表皮生长因子受体（EGFR）和间变性淋巴瘤激酶（ALK）抑制剂的成功应用，确立了生物标志物驱动治疗的框架，强调了在诊断时进行全面分子检测的重要性。这种检测不仅能够识别潜在的靶向治疗机会，还能帮助医生为患者制定更为个性化的治疗方案。

此外，围手术期免疫检查点抑制剂的应用为适合的患者提供了更多的治疗选择，进一步突显了分子分析在治疗决策中的重要性。然而，在实际实施过程中，仍然面临着一些挑战，包括分子检测的不完整性、结果的延迟、组织取样的不足、工作流程的碎片化以及资源获取的不平等。这些问题可能影响到患者的治疗效果和预后，因此亟需在临床实践中加以解决，以确保每位患者都能获得最佳的治疗方案。

总的来说，围手术期生物标志物整合管理在非小细胞肺癌的个性化治疗中具有重要的潜力，但要实现这一潜力，需要克服现有的实施障碍，确保分子检测的全面性和及时性，以便为患者提供更为精准和有效的治疗。

items.title: Potential to Fine-Tune the Requirements for Amino Acids, Copper, Zinc, and Manganese to Optimise Growth Performance in Broiler Chickens
items.abstract: Chicken meat is the most widely consumed meat globally, with Australia alone reporting a per capita consumption of 53 kg/person/year. Amino acids and microminerals are essential to poultry nutrition, supporting growth performance and health in broiler chickens, partly mediated by their interaction with the gut microbiota. However, imprecise or excessive supply increases nutrient excretion, raising environmental concerns and adding unnecessary feed costs, emphasising the need for precision nutrition. This review examines the impacts of amino acid and micromineral nutrition, including their role in shaping the gut microbiota, and explores how precision feeding can reduce nutrient waste, environmental impact, and cost. Precision nutrition seeks to improve growth performance, feed efficiency, gut health and nutrient absorption, by delivering the right nutrients, in the right amounts, at the right time. Across the literature, organic microminerals consistently show greater bioavailability and overall performance than inorganic forms at lower inclusion levels; likewise, split (AM/PM) feeding has improved performance in laying hens, though its circadian-informed application to amino acid and micromineral feeding remains largely unexplored in broilers. This review discusses the potential to fine-tune amino acid and micromineral (copper, zinc, and manganese) requirements together with their microbiota-mediated effects to optimise feed efficiency and growth performance in broilers.
items.authors: Birendra Dhakal, Thi Hiep Dao, Amy F. Moss

items.title: Influence of Friction Stir Welding and Post-Weld Aging on Corrosion Behavior of LPBF A20X Alloy
items.abstract: Laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) enables the production of high-strength A20X aluminum components with complex geometries for aerospace applications. However, the limited build volume of LPBF systems often requires separately manufactured parts to be joined. This study compares the microstructure and corrosion behavior of LPBF A20X under four material conditions: base material (BM), as-welded stir zone (SZ), solution-treated and peak-aged base material (BM–PA), and solution-treated and peak-aged stir zone (SZ–PA). Microstructural evolution was assessed using electron microscopy and X-ray diffraction, while corrosion behavior was evaluated by electrochemical impedance spectroscopy and potentiodynamic polarization in 3.5 wt.% NaCl solution. Among the tested specimens, BM exhibited the lowest corrosion current density (0.703 μA/cm2), followed by SZ (0.966 μA/cm2), BM–PA (2.257 μA/cm2), and SZ–PA (3.181 μA/cm2). The impedance response and post-polarization SEM observations indicated lower corrosion resistance after solution treatment and aging, particularly in SZ–PA. These findings are consistent with a possible contribution from micro-galvanic interactions involving redistributed and precipitated Cu-rich constituents, TiB2 particles, and the Al matrix. Under the tested conditions, post-weld heat treatment reduced corrosion resistance compared to FSW alone. This underlines the need to optimize welding and heat-treatment parameters for LPBF A20X components.
items.authors: Mohammad Abankar, Paolo Matteis, Pasquale Russo Spena

items.title: Optimization of the Performance of Zirconia-Toughened and Mixed-Alumina Ceramic Tools in CNC Turning of 42CrMo4 Steel
items.abstract: This article presents the results of a comprehensive study of the performance of zirconia-toughened and mixed-alumina ceramic tools in CNC turning of 42CrMo4 steel with hardnesses of 35, 40, and 45 HRC. Empirical models have been developed for the cutting tool lifetime and the surface roughness of the machined surfaces as a function of cutting speed and hardness of the machined material. Through multi-objective compromise optimization via two approaches (the optimal compromise region and the generalized arithmetic mean utility function with weighting coefficients) and the application of a genetic algorithm, the optimal conditions for performing the CNC turning process were determined when using tools made of different mineral ceramics for steel with varying hardness. These conditions provide a tool lifetime exceeding 8 min and a high machined surface quality with a roughness below 1.7 µm.
items.authors: Irina Aleksandrova, Hristo Metev, Hristian Mitev, Trayan Hristov, Simona Tsaneva

items.title: A Generalized Analytical Framework for Prediction of Self-Excited Backward Whirl in Geometrically Nonlinear Rotor/Stator Rubbing Systems
items.abstract: Traditional analytical models for dry friction backward whirl predominantly rely on linear shaft assumptions, failing to capture amplitude-dependent frequency shifts and nonlinear response dynamics. For the geometrically nonlinear rotor/stator rubbing systems characterized by isotropic, smooth odd-polynomial restoring forces with arbitrary truncation orders, a generalized analytical framework for prediction of self-excited backward whirl is presented in this paper. By expanding the restoring force via a Taylor series with an arbitrary truncation order, a response decomposition strategy is established to treat the steady-state response as a superposition of a synchronous forced forward response and a self-excited backward whirl. A harmonic balance procedure is subsequently employed to decouple these components, yielding closed-form analytical solutions for both stability thresholds and orbital topologies. With the aid of numerical simulations, the proposed framework is validated across multiple degrees of nonlinearity, demonstrating excellent agreement with low root-mean-square errors when the relative sliding duration ratio exceeds 0.7. Crucially, compared with traditional linear rotors, geometric nonlinearity introduces a strong stiffness-hardening effect, resulting in reduced, self-limiting whirl amplitudes and pronounced upward frequency shifts. Furthermore, the instability boundaries of dry friction backward whirl and backward full-annular quasi-periodic rub are revealed to be governed by a nonlinear synergistic excitation driven by the dynamic coupling of dry friction, unbalance forces and geometric nonlinearity. This study provides a computationally efficient analytical tool capable of evaluating the physical qualitative trends and quantitative boundaries of nonlinear rotors for the stability assessment and vibration control of modern nonlinear rotor systems.
items.authors: Shunzeng Wang, Zhenduo Zhang, Xiaoming Liu, Ling Hong, Jun Jiang

items.title: Ferrocene-Branched Polymers via a Ugi Multicomponent Reaction for an Integrated and Reagentless Amperometric Glucose Biosensor
items.abstract: A Ugi multicomponent reaction was employed to synthesize a ferrocene (Fc)-branched polyethyleneimine derivative. This polymer was evaluated as a redox-active matrix for the fabrication of an electroanalytical disposable glucose biosensor based on a carbon PE-printed electrode functionalized with glucose oxidase as a biorecognition element. The resulting biosensor displayed a linear response up to 35 mM glucose at pH 6.5, with a limit of detection of 33 µM. The enzyme biosensor reached 95% of the steady-state current within approximately 50 s and showed a sensitivity of 0.92 µA/mM. In addition, this analytical device exhibited high selectivity, good reproducibility, and excellent storage stability, retaining strong analytical performance after 45 days at 4 °C. The proposed electrochemical biosensor was successfully applied to glucose determination in red and white wine samples.
items.authors: Jorge Urraca, Isabel Zurita, Marija Krznaric, Tatiana Martínez, Alfredo Sánchez, Diana Vilela

items.title: 5D Printing in Additive Manufacturing: Current Status, Applications, and Future Perspectives
items.abstract: Since the late 1980s, additive manufacturing (AM) has emerged as a prominent fabrication technology, experiencing significant advancements over the past decades. Even with its rapid development, this technology still faces many manufacturing challenges. Driven by the development of AM, 5D printing evolved from conventional 3D printing by incorporating five controlled degrees of freedom (three translational and two rotational axes) to enable non-planar deposition, curved-layer fabrication, and improved control of deposition orientation. This review critically analyses and summarizes 5D printing technology, detailing its development, material innovations, applications, and future outlook. The study starts with the evolution of printing from 1D printing, through 2D printing, to 3D printing, detailing its limitations and the paradigm shift to 5D printing. Further insights are also discussed regarding material selection, which plays a crucial role in determining the functionality and performance of 5D printing. Moreover, various applications of 5D printing across the aerospace, automotive, biomedical, jewelry, and food industries have been discussed, highlighting its potential for lightweight, high-strength, and tailored components. Furthermore, a detailed SWOT analysis of 5D printing has been presented to evaluate the strength, weaknesses, opportunities and threats of the technology, providing a strategic perspective of 5D printing in the industry. Lastly, future prospects for multi-material integration, AI-optimized printing and hybrid manufacturing methods are discussed.

items.title: Posttraumatic Stress Symptoms, Hopelessness, and Suicidal Ideation in Public Safety Personnel: A Network Analysis
items.abstract: Objective. Public safety personnel (PSP; e.g., police, firefighters, paramedics, correctional workers, and communications officials) face elevated risks of mental health concerns, including suicidal ideation and behaviours. Well-validated cognitive and interpersonal theories of suicide emphasize the roles of hopelessness, belongingness, traumatic exposures, and burdensomeness; however, the integration with symptom-level processes of posttraumatic stress remains limited. This study examined the relationships between posttraumatic stress symptoms (PTSSs), hopelessness, and suicidal ideation in relation to suicidal contemplation in a large sample of PSP. Method. Data were collected between September 2016 and January 2017 from 1259 Canadian public safety personnel, including 623 who endorsed suicidal contemplation and 636 who did not. Participants completed validated self-report measures of posttraumatic stress symptoms (PCL-5), depression symptoms, including hopelessness and suicidal ideation (PHQ-9), and trauma exposure (LEC-5). Separate partial correlation networks were estimated for personnel with and without suicidal thoughts using regularized graphical models. Centrality was assessed with expected influence, networks were compared using the Network Comparison Test, and a directed acyclic graph was constructed to examine conditional dependency patterns. Results. Networks for personnel with suicidal contemplation showed greater overall connectivity. Comparison tests indicated that network structure and centrality differences were not statistically significant between groups. Descriptively, several trauma-related symptoms appeared somewhat more central in the contemplation network, although centrality differences were not statistically significant. Directed acyclic graph modelling identified conditional dependence patterns linking hopelessness and suicidal ideation, with PTSSs such as upsetting reminders and detachment also appearing in the model. Conclusions. Findings align with elements of cognitive and interpersonal theories of suicide while extending them to posttraumatic stress processes in PSP. The results provide exploratory hypotheses concerning hopelessness and trauma-related symptoms for future longitudinal and intervention research, while recognizing that the findings reflect cross-sectional, pre-pandemic associations.
items.authors: Blake A. E. Boehme, Holden J. Norrie, R. Nicholas Carleton, Gordon J. G. Asmundson

items.title: The Torres Agentic Learning Method: Personalized Embodied Learning Strategies to Evoke Autonomous Volitional Motor Control in Autistic and Neurotypical Children
items.abstract: Background: Learning often occurs under instruction. In the neuromotor domain, this entails moving with intent to accomplish the instructed goal, repeatedly, building an expectation and predicting future events. In autism, however, neuromotor development is delayed and their sense of kinesthetic reafference affected by random noise in the returning motor stream. This impedes fluid, moment-to-moment predictive control, creating a gap between mental intent and physical volition. However, our lab discovered that uninstructed, goal-less spontaneous movements, typically embedded in purposeful actions, are spared and plastic across the autism spectrum. How can we leverage these motions’ unintended consequences, to help autistics self-discover a goal and fluidly complete actions on their own volition? Methods: We built a closed-loop interactive assay: the Torres Agentic Learning (TAL) task. In this task, without instructions, 33 children had to self-discover the goal and complete the action of watching movies under their own volitional control. We continuously recorded their hand motions as they caused media to play, first through naïve wondering and spontaneous unintended consequences from surprising events and then, learning through deliberate error-correction relative to the self-discovered goal. Results: All participants learned through the TAL paradigm. They self-discovered the goal and gained prediction of their motor code, lowering the entropy and enhancing the signal-to-noise ratio of their hand speed temporal streams. Conclusions: Uninstructed goal-less agentic learning mediated by spontaneous motions and surprises is feasible in both autistics and typically developing children. This work offers both an assay and biometrics to track the effectiveness of the agentic learning progression.
items.authors: Elizabeth B. Torres

items.title: The Next Language of Biology May Not Be Human
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence is changing how cancer biology is read, searched, modeled, and turned into hypotheses. But scientific AI does not meet biology directly. Much of what it learns has already passed through English, abstracts, pathway labels, database entries, and text-mined relations. New foundation models create a second translation problem. They can learn from molecular structures, single-cell profiles, perturbation data, and clinical trajectories without first converting those relations into human-readable explanations. This could expand biological and biomedical discovery, but it also changes the burden of proof. If a model proposes a target, biomarker, stratification, or perturbation that is reproducible but only partly interpretable, what evidence should be required before researchers or clinicians act on it? We argue that interpretability is not only an engineering problem. It is a translation problem. When the internal language of a model is difficult to read, the external evidence must become stronger: clear provenance, experimental challenge, cross-population validation, reproducibility, and accountable human judgment.
items.authors: Helder I. Nakaya, Bruno B. Andrade

items.title: Assessment of TLR3-TRIF-NF-κB Innate Immune Signaling Pathway Induced by Newcastle Disease Virus and Construction of TLR3-Deficient BHK-21 Cells
items.abstract: The innate immune system plays a significant role in inhibiting viral infection and proliferation. To explore the signaling pathway of the innate immune response induced by Newcastle disease virus (NDV) in BHK-21 cells, the mRNA expression levels of pattern recognition receptors such as TLR3, TLR7, TLR8, and NOD2, as well as those of cytokines including TNF-α, IL-6, IL-1β, IL-10, IL-17, TRIF, TRAF3, and NF-κB were determined by transcriptome sequencing, qRT-PCR, and ELISA. All these results indicated that the NDV LaSota strain primarily induces the TLR3-TRIF-NF-κB signaling pathway in BHK-21 cells. Subsequently, an NF-κB inhibitor, a TLR3 inhibitor, and a TRAF3 inhibitor were separately used, and the viral titer was measured during the NDV LaSota strain infection of BHK-21 cells. The results displayed that the inhibition of TLR3 or NF-κB effectively increased the viral titer of NDV. Hence, the CRISPR/Cas9 system was used to create a BHK-TLR3—cell clone in which TLR3 was knocked out, and the cells were assessed for morphology, cell density, cell viability, and genetic stability. Finally, the cells were infected with the NDV LaSota strain. The results showed that the BHK-TLR3—cell line is a stable cell line with markedly enhanced NDV LaSota strain production. Furthermore, the knockout of the TLR3 gene significantly inhibited the expression of IFN-α, IFN-β, IL-1β, and TNF-α, especially that of IL-1β and TNF-α. In summary, the present research revealed the main signaling pathway of the innate immune response induced by the NDV LaSota strain and provides a promising basis for NDV production.
items.authors: Bingmei Dong, Jing Cai, Haiqi Zhao, Pengyan Gao, Qingqing Xu, Weiqin Meng
items.title_zh: 评估新城疫病毒诱导的TLR3-TRIF-NF-κB免疫信号通路及构建TLR3缺失BHK-21细胞
items.summary_zh: 先天免疫系统在抑制病毒感染和增殖中发挥重要作用。为探讨新城疫病毒（NDV）在BHK-21细胞中诱导的先天免疫反应信号通路，通过转录组测序、qRT-PCR和ELISA检测了TLR3、TLR7、TLR8、NOD2等模式识别受体及TNF-α、IL-6、IL-1β、IL-10、IL-17、TRIF、TRAF3和NF-κB等细胞因子的mRNA表达水平。结果表明，NDV LaSota株主要诱导BHK-21细胞中的TLR3-TRIF-NF-κB信号通路。随后使用NF-κB抑制剂、TLR3抑制剂和TRAF3抑制剂，测定了感染NDV LaSota株的病毒滴度，结果显示抑制TLR3或NF-κB有效增加了NDV的病毒滴度。利用CRISPR/Cas9系统构建了TLR3缺失的BHK-TLR3—细胞克隆，评估了细胞形态、密度、活力和遗传稳定性。最终，感染NDV LaSota株的结果显示，BHK-TLR3—细胞系是一个稳定的细胞系，显著增强了NDV LaSota株的产量。此外，TLR3基因的敲除显著抑制了IFN-α、IFN-β、IL-1β和TNF-α的表达。
items.l1_lead: 新城疫病毒通过TLR3-TRIF-NF-κB信号通路诱导BHK-21细胞的免疫反应，TLR3缺失显著提高病毒产量并抑制多种细胞因子的表达。
items.l2_summary:
本研究旨在评估新城疫病毒（NDV）在BHK-21细胞中诱导的先天免疫反应信号通路，特别是TLR3-TRIF-NF-κB信号通路的作用。研究通过转录组测序、qRT-PCR和ELISA等方法检测了多种模式识别受体（如TLR3、TLR7、TLR8、NOD2）及细胞因子（包括TNF-α、IL-6、IL-1β、IL-10、IL-17、TRIF、TRAF3和NF-κB）的mRNA表达水平。结果显示，NDV LaSota株主要诱导了BHK-21细胞中的TLR3-TRIF-NF-κB信号通路的激活。

为进一步探讨该信号通路的功能，研究者使用了NF-κB抑制剂、TLR3抑制剂和TRAF3抑制剂，测定了感染NDV LaSota株后的病毒滴度。结果表明，抑制TLR3或NF-κB的活性显著增加了NDV的病毒滴度，提示TLR3-TRIF-NF-κB信号通路在抑制病毒增殖中发挥了重要作用。

此外，研究还利用CRISPR/Cas9系统构建了TLR3缺失的BHK-TLR3—细胞克隆，并对其细胞形态、密度、活力和遗传稳定性进行了评估。最终结果显示，BHK-TLR3—细胞系在感染NDV LaSota株后表现出显著增强的病毒产量，且TLR3基因的敲除显著抑制了IFN-α、IFN-β、IL-1β和TNF-α的表达。这些结果表明，TLR3在NDV感染中的作用至关重要，且构建的TLR3缺失细胞系为进一步研究NDV的免疫机制提供了有价值的工具。

items.title: From E-Waste to Environmental Sensors: An Evidence-Based Recovery-to-Sensor Framework for Recycled Ag, Au, and Cu Functional Materials
items.abstract: Electronic waste is a concentrated secondary source of Ag, Au, and Cu. Still, its suitability for environmental sensing depends not only on extraction efficiency but also on material quality, processability, reproducibility, and demonstrated analytical performance. This review evaluates the recovery-to-sensor pathway using an evidence-based framework that distinguishes genuinely recycled-metal materials from waste-assisted syntheses, reused components, and commercial-precursor benchmarks. Recovery and purification routes are assessed according to material attributes relevant to sensing and printing, including elemental purity, residual lixiviants, phase composition, oxidation state, particle-size distribution, surface chemistry, colloidal stability, and batch reproducibility. The final evidence inventory comprised 88 publications and was classified by material provenance (P1–P6) and evidence level (E1–E6), from recovery-only studies to integrated pathways incorporating device fabrication, real-sample validation, sustainability metrics, and end-of-life management. Direct evidence is strongest for Cu-based systems, including NiO-doped CuO nanoflakes obtained from flexible printed circuit boards for room-temperature ammonia sensing, Cu2O recovered from waste electric cables for electrochemical sensing, Cu2O/CuO nano-skeletons produced from waste printed circuit boards, and recycled Cu electrodes and Cu(OH)2 nanostructures derived from spent lithium-ion batteries. Au recovered from discarded electronic components has also been converted into functional nanoparticles, while commercial-AuNP studies provide transferable evidence for recyclable colorimetric sensing. The review identifies major gaps in direct recycled-versus-virgin comparisons, ink rheology, multi-batch reproducibility, harmonized limits of detection, real-matrix validation, quantitative life-cycle data and recovery of used sensors. A circular-sensor assessment framework is proposed based on material yields, recycled content, process mass intensity, energy and water use, device lifetime, valid measurements per device and end-of-life recovery. None of the studies included in the final evidence inventory met all E6 criteria required for a fully validated circular-sensor claim.
items.authors: Norica Godja, Michael Kitzmantel, Florentina-Daniela Munteanu

items.title: Serial Optical Coherence Tomography Findings After Lesion-Preparation Incorporating the ShockFast™ Intravascular Lithotripsy: A Prospective Single-Center Imaging Sub-Study
items.abstract: Background: Intravascular lithotripsy (IVL) is an established calcium modification strategy for severely calcified coronary lesions. The Shunmei ShockFast™ IVL system is a novel device that appeared safe and feasible in an initial clinical experience. However, its calcium fracture typology, depth distribution, and quantitative stent optimization characteristics have not been characterized by serial optical coherence tomography (OCT). Objectives: To provide the first dedicated serial OCT sub-study of calcium modification patterns and stent optimization metrics achieved with the ShockFast™ IVL system in a cohort of patients with severely calcified de novo coronary lesions. Methods: This is a prospective, single-center OCT imaging sub-study nested within the Cardio-FR registry (NCT04185285). We included 14 patients with OCT assessment performed at three mandatory time points—baseline (before any device delivery), post-IVL, and post-stenting–who underwent PCI with the ShockFast™ IVL system between June 2025 and April 2026. The primary endpoint was OCT-confirmed calcium fracture rate following IVL treatment. Secondary endpoints included calcium fractures ≥2 and type, post-lesion-preparation lumen gain, minimum stent area (MSA), stent expansion (SE), malapposition, and edge dissection rates. Exploratory correlative analyses between baseline calcium morphology and post-IVL stent optimization outcomes were performed. Results: Median baseline OCT MLA was 2.22 mm2 (IQR 1.4–3.61). Calcium fractures were identified in 10 of 14 lesions (71%, 95% CI 45–88%) following a lesion-preparation strategy incorporating ShockFast™ IVL, with ≥2 fractures in 43%. Fractures were classified as partial-thickness (non-transmural) in 30% and full-thickness (transmural) in 70% of cases. Median post-lesion-preparation lumen gain was 0.53 mm2 (IQR 0.3–0.84). Median final MSA was 4.77 mm2 (IQR 3.59–5.34) and median SE was 89.5% (IQR 85–94), with SE 80% achieved in 100% of lesions. No major malapposition or medial edge dissections were recorded. Conclusions: Applied as the central calcium-modification component of a comprehensive lesion-preparation strategy, the ShockFast™ IVL system was associated with OCT-confirmed calcium fractures in the majority of the lesions, with favorable stent expansion and optimization metrics in the absence of major malapposition or edge dissections. These findings provide the first dedicated serial OCT sub-study of calcium modification mediated by a lesion-preparation strategy incorporating ShockFast™ IVL, consistent with feasibility as a novel IVL platform suitable for further investigation in adequately powered comparative studies.
items.authors: Giacomo Maria Cioffi, Ioannis Skalidis, Julius Jonas Jelisejevas, Yannick Faucherre, Peter Wenaweser, Pascal Meier

items.title: Asynchronous Land-Use Change and Surface Thermal Variability in Nepal, 2000–2023: Drivers and Implications for Himalayan Mountain System Resilience
items.abstract: The vertical redistribution of human activities and surface thermal changes poses challenges to Himalayan resilience. Using Nepal’s 77 districts, this study integrates land-use maps for 2000, 2020, and 2023 with annual MODIS land surface temperature (LST) data for 2000–2023. Trend analysis, fixed thermal thresholds, displacement correspondence tests, lag analysis, and GeoDetector were employed to examine land-use restructuring, thermal variability, and their spatial associations. Results show that: (1) Built-up land expanded from 527 to 1817 km2, with its mean elevation increasing from 412 to 617 m. However, national mean LST, fixed-threshold hot-area extent, and hot-area mean elevation exhibited no significant monotonic trends. (2) Land-use and thermal displacements showed no consistent spatial correspondence or stable temporal lag, indicating regional vertical decoupling rather than delayed thermal migration. (3) Built-up expansion was positively associated with local LST trends. (4) Spatial associations between thermal heterogeneity and elevation, built-up land proportion, and population density, highlighting the spatial heterogeneity of topographic conditions and human activities in relation to regional thermal changes. These asynchronous vertical responses highlight potential development and ecological pressures in mid-elevation transition zones, suggesting a shift from predominantly horizontal spatial regulation toward elevation-sensitive, vertically adaptive planning for Himalayan resilience.
items.authors: Xuejiao Qian, Meimei Wang, Xiaoling Xie

items.title: Students’ Generative AI Use in Studio-Based Design Education: Selective Use, Design Judgment, and Studio Context
items.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly reshaping studio-based design education, yet relatively little is known about how students decide when and how AI should support their design process. This study examined students’ use, adaptation, and perceptions of generative AI, with particular attention to task-specific use, contextual adaptation, and factors associated with AI-related decision-making. An online survey of 112 undergraduate and graduate design students combined structured questionnaire items with optional open-ended responses to examine AI use across studio tasks, project stages, and learning contexts. Students reported higher AI use for concept development, research, and written articulation than for visual refinement, technical documentation, and later stages of design development. Students also reported becoming more selective in their AI use as projects progressed, while instructor expectations, peer influence, and concern about negative judgment were associated with students’ AI-related decisions. Qualitative responses further highlighted authorship, learning, and professional responsibility as important considerations. Together, these findings suggest that students’ selective and context-dependent AI use can be interpreted as boundary-setting around when and how AI participates in the design process. Rather than viewing AI use simply as technology adoption, the findings suggest value in a judgment-centered, process-based approach to AI pedagogy that emphasizes accountability and reflective decision-making.
items.authors: Michelle Boyoung Huh, Alp Tural, Elif Tural

items.title: Serum Corticosterone Concentrations and Granulocyte-to-Lymphocyte Ratios in Slaughter Geese Across Transport-Distance Categories: An Exploratory Descriptive Field Study
items.abstract: Transport exposes poultry to multiple stressors. The declining number of slaughterhouses in the European Union can increase transport distances to slaughter facilities. Transport-related stress responses are documented in chickens and ducks but remain poorly characterized in geese. This exploratory descriptive field study characterized serum corticosterone (CORT) concentrations and the granulocyte-to-lymphocyte (G/L) ratio in pooled blood samples representing 292 slaughter geese from six flocks: one non-transported flock slaughtered on a farm and five commercial flocks transported 1–100, 101–200, 201–300, 301–400, or 400 km. Exploratory pool-level comparisons indicated overall differences in G/L ratios among the five evaluable flocks (p = 0.035), but no pairwise difference remained significant after Bonferroni adjustment. Corticosterone was lower in pooled serum samples from the non-transported flock than in those from the 1–100, 201–300, and 400 km flocks (p 0.001). However, one flock and one journey per distance category prevented separation of distance effects from flock-, farm-, age- or journey-specific influences. These observations provide important descriptive field data but do not permit conclusions about an independent effect of transport distance. Studies with multiple independent flocks and journeys per distance category are required.
items.authors: Benedikt Sauer, Ella Fischer, Isabelle Ruhnke, Eva-Maria Saliu

items.title: Numerical Study of Wave-Induced Responses of a Moored LNG Carrier
items.abstract: Large LNG carriers are sensitive to wave-induced motions at berth, where excessive motions and mooring-line loads compromise operations and safety. This study investigates the wave-induced responses of a fully loaded 177,000 m3 LNG carrier using the time-domain program SHIP-MOORINGS, examining the effects of significant wave height, peak period, wave direction, spectral peak enhancement factor and directional spreading on the six-degree-of-freedom motions and mooring-line forces. The model is validated against two physical model tests (172,000 m3 carrier in ballast, beam waves, Tp = 8.4 s), with maximum-motion differences within 0.05 m (0.05°), line-force differences below 10% and the same spectral content; results beyond this range, obtained from a single irregular-wave realization, indicate trends. Significant wave height scales the responses in approximate proportion without altering their pattern, whereas peak period and wave direction govern both their magnitude and the dominant motion patterns and mooring-load distribution. Under long-period waves, the dominant frequencies of heave, roll and pitch approach their natural frequencies, while surge is dominated by low-frequency motion. The peak enhancement factor changes the maximum motions by no more than 5%, whereas directional spreading produces larger, component-dependent variations. The critical wave direction for the mooring system is the oblique heading of 75°, at which Line 4 is the critical line; sway governs the loss of motion-based operability.
items.authors: Bo Yang, Yusheng Shen, Zhongbin Sun
items.category_raw: Journal of Marine Science and Engineering

items.title: Aerial Phenotyping of Coffee Flowering Using Deep Learning for Early Yield Prediction
items.abstract: Early yield estimation is important for improving decision-making and management practices in coffee production systems. However, approaches that use aerial imagery to characterize flowering and relate it to subsequent yield remain limited. This study evaluated the potential of RGB imagery acquired by remotely piloted aircraft (RPA) combined with Deep Learning techniques to classify coffee plants according to three levels of a flowering proxy and to investigate its relationship with yield. A dataset comprising 1593 segmented RGB images was classified into Low, Medium, and High flowering levels using a custom convolutional neural network and three transfer learning architectures: VGG16, ResNet50V2, and MobileNetV2. ResNet50V2 was selected for final evaluation based on its validation performance and achieved 92.12% accuracy, 92.40% macro-precision, 91.81% macro-recall, and 92.06% macro-F1 on the test dataset. The flowering proxy showed a positive association with field-observed yield, with Spearman’s ρ = 0.701 (p 0.001) and R2 = 0.528 for the combined dataset of Arara and Mundo Novo. In consolidated out-of-sample predictions, the model achieved R2 = 0.489, MAE = 1.03 kg plant−1, and RMSE = 1.18 kg plant−1. Performance differed between cultivars, with consolidated R2 values of 0.567 for Arara and 0.329 for Mundo Novo. Spatial analysis also showed correspondence between the distribution of flowering levels derived from RGB imagery and the subsequent spatial distribution of yield. These findings indicate that RPA-based RGB imagery and Deep Learning can provide spatialized information related to coffee flowering and its productive performance, with potential applications in precision agriculture. Further evaluation across production cycles, cultivars, and environmental conditions is needed to assess the robustness and generalization of the approach.
items.authors: Elias Horácio Zavala, Gabriel Araújo e Silva Ferraz, Felipe Andrés Obando Vega, Mirian de Lourdes Oliveira, Milene Alves de Figueiredo Carvalho, Samuel Henrique Braga da Cunha

items.title: Saccharopine and α-Aminoadipic Acid as Potential Biomarkers for Mitochondrial Stress in Neurons
items.abstract: Redox stress and subsequent metabolic reprogramming are well-known consequences of neuronal exposure to mitochondrial toxicants. Here, we investigated, using human neuronal cultures, how such changes are quantitatively reflected in the patterns of cellular and extracellular amino acids. We asked whether these alterations may yield a mechanistically anchored biomarker for the type of neurotoxicity resulting from the impairment of the respiratory chain. Using a targeted metabolomics approach, we quantified intra- and extracellular amino acid pools and their temporal dynamics. Data were obtained from differentiated LUHMES neurons exposed to the complex I inhibitors berberine, 1-methyl-4-phenylpyridinium (MPP+), and tebufenpyrad, as well as to the non-mitochondrial toxicants MG-132 (proteasome inhibitor), RSL3 (glutathione peroxidase 4 inhibitor), and aerugine (fungal oxidative toxicant). The reductive stress, caused by mitochondrial inhibitors, was reflected in a characteristic and specific re-routing of amino acid metabolism, including increased Asn/Asp and Gln/Glu ratios and an upregulation of the electron acceptor Pro in neurons. Most conspicuous were the pronounced and reproducible increases in the lysine catabolites saccharopine (sacc) and α-aminoadipic acid (α-AAA). These two potential biomarkers of neuronal mitotoxicity were not altered by other types of toxicants. Moreover, the extent of concentration changes in sacc and α-AAA roughly correlated with the damaging effects of mitotoxicants, when assay conditions were (exposure period and exposure concentration). Our data provide an exemplary reference map of absolute amino acid concentrations in human cells and their culture medium. Moreover, sacch and α-AAA emerge as candidate biomarkers for neuroactive mitotoxicants and potentially for pathologies associated with impaired neuronal mitochondrial function.
items.authors: Anna-Katharina Ückert, Anja Land, Regina Pape, Mahshid Alimohammadi, Ivano Amelio, Marcel Leist
items.title_zh: 作为线粒体压力潜在生物标志物的糖醇和α-氨基己二酸
items.summary_zh: 红氧化应激及随后的代谢重编程是神经元暴露于线粒体毒素的已知后果。本研究使用人类神经元培养，定量分析细胞内外氨基酸的变化模式，以探讨这些变化是否能作为呼吸链损伤引起的神经毒性机制的生物标志物。采用靶向代谢组学方法，量化了氨基酸池及其时间动态。数据来自于暴露于复合物I抑制剂（如小檗碱、1-甲基-4-苯基吡啶（MPP+）和特布芬脲）及非线粒体毒素（如MG-132、RSL3和青霉素）的LUHMES分化神经元。线粒体抑制引起的还原应激在氨基酸代谢的特征性重定向中得以体现，包括Asn/Asp和Gln/Glu比率的增加，以及神经元中电子受体脯氨酸的上调。最显著的是赖氨酸代谢物糖醇（sacc）和α-氨基己二酸（α-AAA）的显著增加，这两个潜在的神经元线粒体毒性生物标志物未受到其他类型毒素的影响。
items.l1_lead: 本研究发现糖醇和α-氨基己二酸在神经元暴露于线粒体毒素时显著增加，可能作为线粒体压力的生物标志物。
items.l2_summary:
本研究探讨了线粒体压力对神经元的影响，特别是通过分析氨基酸的变化模式，寻找潜在的生物标志物以揭示呼吸链损伤引起的神经毒性机制。研究采用人类神经元培养（LUHMES分化神经元），通过靶向代谢组学方法定量分析细胞内外的氨基酸变化。实验中，神经元暴露于复合物I抑制剂（如小檗碱、1-甲基-4-苯基吡啶（MPP+）和特布芬脲）以及非线粒体毒素（如MG-132、RSL3和青霉素），以观察不同毒素对氨基酸代谢的影响。

结果显示，线粒体抑制引起的还原应激在氨基酸代谢中表现出特征性重定向，具体体现在Asn/Asp和Gln/Glu比率的增加，以及电子受体脯氨酸的上调。这些变化表明，线粒体功能障碍可能导致氨基酸代谢的显著改变。最为显著的是，赖氨酸代谢物糖醇（sacc）和α-氨基己二酸（α-AAA）的浓度显著增加，这两个代谢物被认为是潜在的神经元线粒体毒性生物标志物，且未受到其他类型毒素的影响。

综上所述，本研究通过定量分析氨基酸的变化，揭示了线粒体压力对神经元的影响，并提出糖醇和α-氨基己二酸作为新的生物标志物，可能为理解线粒体毒性机制提供新的视角。这些发现为未来的神经退行性疾病研究提供了重要的线索，尤其是在寻找早期诊断和治疗靶点方面。

items.title: Dynamic Assessment and Synergistic Reconfiguration of Rural Territorial System Resilience: A Case Study of Quzhou County, China
items.abstract: Rapid urbanization is widely regarded as a major pathway to rural development through improved market accessibility, infrastructure provision, and urban–rural functional linkages. Yet long-term empirical evidence has not sufficiently tested whether urban proximity enhances or erodes the resilience of rural territorial systems. Drawing on multisource remote sensing imagery, a harmonized nighttime light series, socioeconomic statistics, and key informant interviews spanning 1985–2025, this study reconstructs the spatiotemporal evolution of rural territorial system resilience in Quzhou County, a representative agricultural county on the North China Plain. An integrated element–structure–function framework conceptualizes rural resilience along three dimensions—element support capacity, structural resistance, and functional adaptability—extending the analytical focus from assessing system states to examining underlying mechanisms. The results show that the county-wide mean resilience index declined from 0.4832 to 0.2897, a cumulative decrease of 40%, with a 26.7% decline during 2015–2025 alone. The coefficient of variation across townships followed a nonlinear rise–fall–rise trajectory, indicating widening disparities, brief convergence, and renewed divergence, and reached a study-period maximum of 0.3859 in 2025. The combined area share of the low and relatively low resilience classes increased from 10.89% to 79.27%, whereas that of the high resilience class contracted from 17.50% to 7.82%, remained low, and ultimately fell to zero in 2025. Spatially, townships surrounding the county seat experienced the sharpest declines, contrary to the conventional expectation that proximity to urban centers strengthens rural resilience. Policy interventions yielded only temporary rebounds, and no township achieved systemic recovery during the study period. Instead, the system exhibited interconnected deterioration characterized by resource depletion, structural fragmentation, and functional homogenization. These findings motivate a “proximity paradox” hypothesis in urban–rural integration: when urban expansion erodes the resource base of surrounding rural areas, disrupts their spatial organization, and reduces their functional redundancy, geographical proximity to cities may shift from an enabling condition for resilience to a source of resilience loss. Accordingly, this study proposes a coordinated governance approach integrating the conservation of critical resources, the restructuring of settlements into a three-tier hierarchy, and spatial zoning into four functional categories. This approach provides an empirical basis for overcoming persistent rural decline and implementing differentiated spatial governance in agricultural plains undergoing rapid urbanization.
items.authors: Yibin Zhang, Limeng Jia, Xin Zhang, Yahui Duan, Mu Li, Qiangqiang Sun

items.title: From In Vitro Screening to In Vivo Evaluation of Essential-Oil-Based Formulation Against Avian Pathogenic Escherichia coli
items.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance in avian pathogenic Escherichia coli (APEC) poses a significant challenge to poultry production, highlighting the need for effective alternatives to conventional antimicrobials. This study aimed to evaluate the antibacterial activity of selected essential oils (EOs) against multidrug-resistant APEC isolates and assess the in vivo effects of an oregano–thyme EO-based formulation in experimentally infected broilers. Six EOs were screened in vitro using the broth microdilution method, and oregano and thyme EOs, showing the strongest activity (MIC 0.003% and 0.003–0.007%, respectively), were further evaluated in two combinations. The more active combination was formulated for administration via drinking water and tested in 420 Ross 308 broilers experimentally challenged with APEC. Birds were allocated to untreated control, infected untreated, EO-treated, enrofloxacin-treated, and enrofloxacin + reduced-dose EO formulation groups. Mortality did not differ significantly among groups. A binomial GLMM identified significant differences in faecal consistency among experimental groups (likelihood-ratio χ2 = 32.90, df = 4, p 0.001), while no significant differences were observed in body weight, feed intake, or overall FCR. Significant differences were detected in AST, glucose, total bilirubin, and calcium concentrations. Overall, the EO-based formulation demonstrated antibacterial activity in vitro and was associated with changes in intestinal status following APEC challenge, while no consistent improvement in productive performance was observed. These findings support further investigation of EO-based formulations as potential non-antibiotic approaches for managing APEC-associated intestinal disturbances in broiler chickens.
items.authors: Milenko Rikić, Zoran Ružić, Marko Pajić, Dalibor Todorović, Slobodan Knežević, Nebojša Kladar

items.title: Strongly Nonlinear Responses in Coupled Duffing Oscillators: Homotopy-Enriched Multiple Scales and Branch-Resolved Continuation Benchmarking
items.abstract: First-order classical multiple scales (MMS) linearizes frequency detuning and discards a quadratic correction that grows away from resonance. Homotopy-enriched multiple scales (EMMS) uses the forcing-frequency carrier and retains the full squared-frequency mismatch. We derive coupled modulation equations and explicit stability Jacobians for a two-degree-of-freedom Duffing system with a general cubic modal tensor, and compare its algebraic responses with AUTO2000 periodic-orbit continuation. The principal benchmark is a large-detuning stress test. On the 107 reference cells matched by both methods, the median amplitude errors are 1.28% for EMMS and 10.89% for classical MMS. EMMS matches 186 of 201 reference cells, and classical MMS 107. The lower-fold frequency errors are 0.011% and 0.503%, respectively; the EMMS and reference lower-fold frequencies both round to 1.108. Both methods recover a separate weak small-detuning control. Shooting of the full equations of motion shows that the maximum sampled peak–fundamental difference increases from 3.55% to 4.28% with forcing. Classical MMS predicts both secondary-lobe stability boundaries more closely, while EMMS predicts the interval width more closely. The symmetric coupling sweep tests consistency because the direct coupling cubic term cancels from the first modal equation; an asymmetric benchmark exercises the additional odd tensor coefficients.
items.authors: Hussain Al-Qahtani

items.title: Driving Customer Retention Intention in the Indonesian Digital Economy: The Interplay of Multidimensional Values, Perceived Risk, and Trust
items.abstract: High churn rates and the inherent anonymity of digital marketplaces make customer retention a complex strategic imperative. To understand the psychological mechanics associated with consumer continuance intention, this research examines the interplay of multidimensional values (utilitarian, hedonic, and social) and perceived risk through the lens of the Stimulus–Organism–Response (S-O-R) paradigm. Responses gathered from a purposively recruited sample of 270 active e-commerce shoppers in Indonesia were evaluated using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). The analysis reveals a complex partial mediation structure. While utilitarian value and perceived risk operate strictly through internal psychological states, hedonic and social values exhibit significant direct and indirect effects on retention intention. Both relational trust and transactional satisfaction emerge as paramount predictors of retention intention. By mapping the sequential and direct associations of marketing stimuli with continuance intention, this study broadens the applicability of the S-O-R framework in emerging digital economies. The findings suggest that platform strategies prioritizing experiential engagement—such as gamification—and visible risk mitigation policies may offer valuable approaches for supporting long-term consumer relationships.
items.authors: Tri Yulistyawati Evelina, Ludfi Djajanto
items.category_raw: Journal of Theoretical and Applied Electronic Commerce Research

items.title: Breeding in the City: Non-Linear Associations of Urbanization, Tree Cover, and Human Disturbance with Eurasian Tree Sparrows (Passer montanus) Breeding Performance
items.abstract: Urbanization can alter habitat structure and disturbance regimes, with consequences for bird reproduction. We used 13 years of nest-box monitoring data from 15 urban green spaces in Madrid, Spain, with an average of 866 nest boxes monitored annually, to assess how urbanization, tree cover, building height, road infrastructure, noise, and pedestrian intensity were associated with Eurasian Tree Sparrow (Passer montanus) breeding performance. Nest-box occupancy, eggs and hatched chicks per box, nestlings reaching ringing age, and mean number of clutches showed non-linear associations with urbanization, with the highest values generally recorded in partially urbanized areas. Occupancy was 66.9% in these areas, compared with 17.5% in urbanized areas. Tree cover was positively associated with productivity in highly urbanized areas, suggesting that vegetation may be particularly relevant to productivity under highly urbanized conditions. In contrast, greater building height was associated with lower occupancy and reproductive performance. Pedestrian intensity was negatively related to nest-box use and reproductive output, whereas road infrastructure and noise mainly affected later reproductive stages. Overall, breeding performance was associated with the combined characteristics of vegetation, urban structure, and human disturbance. Maintaining partially urbanized green spaces and increasing tree cover in densely built areas may be associated with more favourable breeding conditions for Eurasian Tree Sparrows.
items.authors: Igor Irazusta-Peco, Beatriz Martínez-Miranzo, José I. Aguirre, Eva Banda

items.title: Visitor-Centric Public Space Network Analysis: A Revised Node Efficiency Model for Spatial Intervention
items.abstract: Conventional spatial network analysis relies on topological metrics that neglect visitor behavioral dimensions, leading to systematic mismatches between structural centrality and actual spatial vitality. This study proposed a revised node efficiency model that incorporated three visitor-centric parameters: space attractiveness, quantified by the type, frequency, and duration of on-site activities; a visitor inflow coefficient reflecting dynamic crowd aggregation; and path attraction impedance, accounting for the flow-retention effects along pedestrian routes. The model was validated using field observation data from 20 public space nodes at Xi’an Banpo International Art District. Comparative analysis against conventional node efficiency and degree centrality metrics revealed substantial discrepancies between topologically critical nodes and those that actually sustain visitor vitality. Two distinct types of supply-demand mismatches were identified, namely network-oriented potential spaces and activity-oriented potential spaces, and differentiated intervention strategies were proposed. These findings demonstrate that incorporating visitor activity characteristics reshapes the assessment of node importance, offering a human-centered diagnostic lens for public space analysis. This approach provides a methodological framework for evidence-based spatial intervention, with empirical validation in the context of industrial heritage renewal, and suggests promising directions for further testing in other urban public space typologies.
items.authors: Xin Xu, Jinting Yu, Qing-Chang Lu, Zhichao Zhang

items.title: Hyperautomated Hazard Mitigation Using Integrated, Scalable, and Sustainable Robotics and UAV Systems
items.abstract: Natural and anthropogenic disasters are rising in frequency and severity, and reactive, single-technology response models are now the principal bottleneck in safeguarding planetary health. This article develops Hyperautomated Hazard Mitigation (HHM), in which robots, unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), and artificial intelligence (AI) services operate as one integrated, self-optimizing system rather than as isolated tools. Hazard mitigation is treated as a specific resilience behavior of a multi-agent engineering system, building on established proactive-resilience theory rather than presenting that framing as new. This framework-oriented review synthesizes evidence and proposes an architecture. It reports no new experimental validation. It maps hazard-mitigation functions onto the six layers of the Reference Architectural Model Industrie 4.0 (RAMI 4.0) with the standards and interfaces that realize each layer; classifies robotic and UAV functions across natural and anthropogenic hazards using one set of four capability classes; expresses ethical and regulatory requirements as quantified engineering constraints; operationalizes health- centered evaluation metrics; and appraises the maturity of the evidence in each hazard domain. It concludes that the architecture is tractable with existing standards, that the actuation stage is the least mature and least evaluated, and that the decisive gap is evaluative: the field has no shared benchmark and rarely reports health outcomes.
items.authors: Ronnie Concepcion, Jeanette Pao, Rhen Anjerome Bedruz, Ronnel Agulto, Jared Jan Abayan, Edza Aria Wikurendra

items.title: Pooled Information and Model Flexibility: Decomposing Machine-Learning Gains in Corporate Budgeting and Forecasting
items.abstract: Corporate financial planning and analysis (FP A) is being reorganised around machine learning, yet the supporting evidence consists largely of vendor case reports using undefined accuracy measures. This study decomposes the machine-learning advantage into components that prior work bundles together—information recency versus model re-estimation, and pooled estimation versus learner flexibility—measured on corporate income-statement data rather than retail or equity series. An open benchmark from SEC XBRL data covering 2599 non-financial US filers and 118,406 firm-quarters, from 2011 to 2025, evaluates five pre-registered hypotheses under rolling-origin validation with clustered inference. First, the advantage of continuous re-forecasting over annual budgeting derives from information recency rather than parameter updating: supplying current quarterly actuals to a model estimated once at fiscal year start recovers 27 to 58 percent of forecast error, whereas quarterly re-estimation produces no detectable improvement (p = 0.82), a result that holds across the COVID-19 and 2022 inflation regimes. Second, the advantage is an interaction rather than a main effect: a pooled linear model modestly outperforms a Theta benchmark, a flexible learner fitted per firm underperforms it, and a foundation model pooled across unrelated domains underperforms further; only pooling across comparable firms combined with a flexible learner realises the full gain. Third, model ranking reverses under asymmetric budget-variance cost.
items.authors: Muteb Ahmed Almihbash
items.category_raw: Journal of Risk and Financial Management

items.title: On (N1)-Tuple Riccati Stability+
items.abstract: In this paper, we introduce the notion of tuple Riccati stability, which extends the classical concept of Riccati stability from a pair of matrices to an arbitrary finite collection of matrices. We establish an equivalent linear matrix inequality characterization and investigate several fundamental properties of the proposed notion, including hereditary, invariance, robustness, and convexity properties. As an application, we show that tuple Riccati stability provides a sufficient condition for the delay-independent asymptotic stability of linear systems with multiple constant delays by means of a Lyapunov–Krasovskii approach. We also establish a joint Schur–Cohn stability result that extends the classical spectral condition for Riccati-stable pairs to simultaneous combinations of multiple feedback matrices. Several consequences of this result are derived, illustrating how the proposed framework treats multiple feedback channels simultaneously. The results presented here generalize several well-known properties of classical Riccati stability and provide a unified framework for the analysis of systems with multiple delayed feedbacks.
items.authors: Mohamed Abdel Aziz Abdellahi, Ali Algefary

items.title: Mechanical Response and Stability Assessment of Deteriorated Tunnel Linings Under Prescribed Cyclic Stress Changes
items.abstract: This study investigates how initial material deterioration and repeated stress changes affect the response of lining–rock systems during tunnel reconstruction and expansion. Monotonic uniaxial compression tests on limestone specimens with gypsum linings were monitored using digital image correlation. A corresponding numerical model was compared with the monotonic test response and used for incremental–static cyclic loading simulations. The numerical series examined cyclic stress amplitude, initial lining deterioration and initial surrounding-rock deterioration separately. Higher cyclic stress amplitudes produced greater convergence and more extensive plastic-zone development. The lining plastic-zone fraction increased more markedly between surrounding-rock deterioration levels of 20% and 30% than across the lower sampled levels, indicating a possible transition within the investigated range. Axial work-density changes depended on the parameter series and were not uniformly monotonic. A weighted five-indicator framework with prescribed engineering weights combines convergence, plastic-zone fractions and lining cohesion loss for relative comparison of the simulated cases. The findings identify regions and material conditions that warrant attention when assessing deteriorated linings and planning tunnel reconstruction and expansion.
items.authors: Xiaogang Ren, Xinjie Zhu, Guangbin Shang, Minghui Hu, Shengxu Wang, Xiaoliang Dong

items.title: Population PK/PD Modeling and Simulation to Predict the Comparative Long-Term Efficacy of Olokizumab in Rheumatoid Arthritis Patients
items.abstract: Background/Objectives: Olokizumab (OKZ) is a humanized monoclonal antibody targeting interleukin-6 (IL-6). OKZ demonstrated efficacy in subjects with active rheumatoid arthritis (RA) in randomized controlled trials versus adalimumab (ADLM) and placebo over 24 weeks, with sustained efficacy confirmed through 106 weeks in an open-label single-arm extension study (OLE). This analysis aimed to predict 1-year efficacy of OKZ 64 mg administered every two weeks (q2w) and every four weeks (q4w) compared with ADLM and placebo through virtual clinical trial simulations based on population pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) models. Methods: Nonlinear mixed-effects models were developed using pooled data from phase III studies. Turnover models with a maximum inhibition Imax-type relationship between OKZ concentrations and clinical scores were applied. Simulated clinical trials were performed to estimate 52-week response rates, defined as proportions of patients achieving low disease activity (DAS28-CRP ≤ 3.2) and remission (CDAI ≤ 2.8). The reliability of the simulated extrapolations was validated against published data. Results: Log-transformed C-reactive protein (CRP) baseline levels and region were identified as significant covariates, influencing the dynamics of RA activity scores. OKZ and ADLM showed comparable predicted efficacy profiles, with overlapping 95% prediction intervals, and both were superior to placebo. Model predictions showed strong agreement with published long-term data for ADLM and placebo and closely reproduced the actual 1-year response profiles from the OKZ OLE. Conclusions: The developed PK/PD models showed good agreement with observed long-term efficacy outcomes for OKZ, ADLM, and placebo in MTX-IR RA patients. Both OKZ dosing regimens sustained low disease activity and remission rates comparable with those for ADLM over 52 weeks, supporting their use as effective treatment options.
items.authors: Yuri Kosinsky, Ivan Azarov, Kirill Zhudenkov, Kirill Peskov, Sergey Grishin, Alina Egorova
items.title_zh: 基于人群PK/PD模型预测Olokizumab在RA患者中的长期疗效
items.summary_zh: 背景/目的：Olokizumab（OKZ）是一种针对白介素-6（IL-6）的人源化单克隆抗体。在随机对照试验中，OKZ在活跃性类风湿关节炎（RA）患者中显示出相较于阿达木单抗（ADLM）和安慰剂的疗效，且在开放标签单臂扩展研究中确认了其在106周内的持续疗效。本分析旨在通过基于人群药代动力学/药效学（PK/PD）模型的虚拟临床试验模拟，预测每两周（q2w）和每四周（q4w）给药的OKZ 64 mg与ADLM和安慰剂的1年疗效。方法：使用III期研究的汇总数据开发非线性混合效应模型，应用最大抑制Imax型关系的周转模型。模拟临床试验用于估算52周的反应率，定义为达到低疾病活动性（DAS28-CRP ≤ 3.2）和缓解（CDAI ≤ 2.8）的患者比例。结果：对数转化的C反应蛋白（CRP）基线水平和地区被确定为显著协变量，影响RA活动评分的动态。OKZ和ADLM的预测疗效曲线相似，95%预测区间重叠。
items.l1_lead: 基于人群PK/PD模型的研究表明，Olokizumab在类风湿关节炎患者中的长期疗效与阿达木单抗相似，且在不同给药频率下均能有效降低疾病活动性。
items.l2_summary:
Olokizumab（OKZ）是一种针对白介素-6（IL-6）的人源化单克隆抗体，近年来在活跃性类风湿关节炎（RA）患者中的疗效引起了广泛关注。在随机对照试验中，OKZ显示出相较于阿达木单抗（ADLM）和安慰剂的显著疗效，并在后续的开放标签单臂扩展研究中确认了其在106周内的持续疗效。为进一步评估OKZ的长期疗效，本研究采用基于人群药代动力学/药效学（PK/PD）模型的虚拟临床试验模拟，预测OKZ 64 mg在每两周（q2w）和每四周（q4w）给药下，与ADLM和安慰剂在1年内的疗效。

研究使用了III期研究的汇总数据，开发了非线性混合效应模型，并应用最大抑制Imax型关系的周转模型进行分析。通过模拟临床试验，研究团队估算了52周内患者达到低疾病活动性（DAS28-CRP ≤ 3.2）和缓解（CDAI ≤ 2.8）的反应率。结果显示，对数转化的C反应蛋白（CRP）基线水平和地区被确定为显著协变量，影响RA活动评分的动态变化。此外，OKZ和ADLM的预测疗效曲线相似，且95%的预测区间重叠，表明两者在疗效上具有相似性。

综上所述，本研究通过人群PK/PD模型的虚拟临床试验，成功预测了OKZ在RA患者中的长期疗效，结果显示OKZ与ADLM的疗效相近，为临床应用提供了重要的理论依据。这一发现为进一步的临床决策和治疗方案的制定提供了参考，尤其是在选择合适的生物制剂治疗RA患者时。

items.title: Reflexive Practice as a Site for Identity Work: A Duoethnographic Study of Doctoral Pedagogy and Support
items.abstract: Doctoral study is marked by identity disruption, emotional strain, and isolation. Students may benefit from pedagogical support that facilitates identity development. While reflexivity is commonly positioned as a critical competence in doctoral training, it is less frequently explored as a pedagogical process for identity work. The study aimed to interrogate reflexive practice as a site for identity work. Adopting a duoethnographic methodology, two lecturers engaged in dialogical reflection about their experiences of teaching reflexive practice. Data included recorded dialogues and written reflections to explore how reflexive practice was enacted in teaching. Data were analysed with identity work theory as the analytic spine. Findings pose reflexive practice as a site where identity formation can be made explicit, strengthening selfhood and belonging through ongoing relational sensemaking. Teaching reflexive practice is framed as the task of creating and holding space for the emotionally demanding self-work fundamental to a doctoral journey. Teachers of reflexive practice should intentionally engage in reflexivity to enhance their use of self in service of facilitating students’ identity work in this pedagogy. By foregrounding educators’ identity work through reflexive practice, the study contributes to the doctoral support literature without claiming that reflexive pedagogy is a straightforward solution to the emotional challenges that doctoral students experience.
items.authors: Antoni Barnard, Aden-Paul Flotman

items.title: Low-Velocity Impact Response of Biaxial Glass-Fiber Fabric Composites: Influence of Fabric Layer Number Under Progressively Increasing Impact Energy
items.abstract: Glass-fiber-reinforced polymer composites are of interest for lightweight structural applications, including marine structures, where accidental low-velocity impact is an important design consideration. This study investigates the low-velocity impact response of polyester-matrix composites reinforced with 4 layers, 6 layers, and 8 layers of biaxial glass fabric. A progressive test program, designed according to the number of fabric layers, used increasing impact-energy levels to cover both an indentation-dominated non-perforating regime and complete perforation, with the transition toward complete perforation in each configuration guiding the energy range selected for the configuration with the next higher number of fabric layers. Instrumented drop-weight tests with a 16 mm hemispherical impactor were analyzed using force, displacement, velocity, and energy histories. At the highest fully non-perforating energy levels of 30 J, 60 J, and 100 J, maximum contact forces were 7.25 kN, 13.05 kN, and 17.45 kN, while absorbed energies were approximately 28.7 J, 54.1 J, and 95.3 J. At 40 J, 80 J, and 120 J, respectively, the composite series entered the transition regime, with complete perforation observed for some of the tested specimens. The investigated parameters showed different diagnostic values: some were sensitive to the impactor mass–velocity combination, whereas displacement, energy, and velocity histories more clearly reflected the change in impact regime. The progressive test campaign, extended up to complete perforation, provides a practical means of identifying the transition between impact regimes and establishing application-specific impact limits. For design purposes, components exposed to accidental impact should therefore incorporate an adequate margin below the experimentally identified transition energy range.
items.authors: George Cătălin Cristea, Lorena Deleanu, Maria Gherghișan, Mario Constandache, Claudiu Marian Martin, Ioana Gabriela Chiracu

items.title: Genome-Wide Identification and Evolution Analysis of the bHLH Gene Family in Cucurbita pepo L.
items.abstract: The basic helix–loop–helix (bHLH) gene family is one of the largest transcription factor families in plants and plays essential roles in growth, development, and responses to environmental stresses. However, the members and functional characteristics of the bHLH gene family in Cucurbita pepo L. remain largely unclear. In this study, a total of 175 bHLH genes were identified in Cucurbita pepo L., exhibiting considerable variation in protein length and structural features. Phylogenetic analysis classified these genes into 24 subgroups (Subgroup 1–24), with conserved motif compositions within each subgroup but clear divergence among different subfamilies, indicating functional differentiation. Gene duplication analysis revealed that WGD/segmental duplication was the primary driving force underlying the expansion of the bHLH gene family. Cis-regulatory element analysis showed that CpbHLH genes are mainly associated with light responsiveness, as well as plant growth and developmental processes. Furthermore, RNA-seq analysis revealed that CpbHLH genes exhibit tissue-specific expression patterns and dynamic responses to cold stress, and quantitative real-time PCR (qRT-PCR) analysis confirmed their tissue-specific expression patterns, together suggesting their potential roles in flower development and stress adaptation. Overall, this study provides a comprehensive overview of the CpbHLH gene family and lays a solid foundation for future functional characterization.
items.authors: Qinghua Liu, Aiwan Cao, Hongwei He, Chenchen Dong, Yuanjun Nie, Xin Zhao
items.title_zh: 葫芦科植物Cucurbita pepo L. bHLH基因家族的全基因组鉴定与进化分析
items.summary_zh: 基本螺旋-环-螺旋（bHLH）基因家族是植物中最大的转录因子家族之一，在生长、发育及环境胁迫响应中发挥重要作用。然而，Cucurbita pepo L.中bHLH基因家族的成员及功能特征尚不清楚。本研究鉴定了175个Cucurbita pepo L.的bHLH基因，显示出蛋白质长度和结构特征的显著变异。系统发育分析将这些基因分为24个亚组，各亚组内具有保守的基序组成，但不同亚家族之间存在明显的分化，表明功能差异。基因重复分析显示，全基因组重复/片段重复是bHLH基因家族扩展的主要驱动力。顺式调控元件分析表明，CpbHLH基因主要与光响应及植物生长发育过程相关。此外，RNA-seq分析显示CpbHLH基因具有组织特异性表达模式及对冷胁迫的动态响应，定量实时PCR（qRT-PCR）分析证实了其组织特异性表达模式，提示其在花发育和胁迫适应中的潜在作用。总体而言，本研究为CpbHLH基因家族提供了全面的概述。
items.l1_lead: 本研究鉴定了175个Cucurbita pepo L.的bHLH基因，揭示其在植物生长、发育及环境胁迫响应中的多样性和功能特征，为进一步研究提供了基础。
items.l2_summary:
本研究针对葫芦科植物Cucurbita pepo L.中的基本螺旋-环-螺旋（bHLH）基因家族进行了全基因组鉴定与进化分析，旨在揭示该基因家族的成员及其功能特征。研究共鉴定出175个Cucurbita pepo L.的bHLH基因，结果显示这些基因在蛋白质长度和结构特征上存在显著变异。通过系统发育分析，这些基因被划分为24个亚组，各亚组内具有保守的基序组成，但不同亚家族之间则表现出明显的分化，暗示其在功能上存在差异。

基因重复分析表明，全基因组重复和片段重复是bHLH基因家族扩展的主要驱动力。此外，顺式调控元件分析显示，CpbHLH基因主要与光响应及植物生长发育过程密切相关。RNA-seq分析进一步揭示了CpbHLH基因在不同组织中的特异性表达模式及其对冷胁迫的动态响应，定量实时PCR（qRT-PCR）分析也证实了其组织特异性表达模式。这些结果提示CpbHLH基因在花发育和胁迫适应中可能发挥重要作用。

总体而言，本研究为Cucurbita pepo L.的bHLH基因家族提供了全面的概述，揭示了其在植物生长、发育及环境适应中的潜在功能，为进一步研究该基因家族的生物学功能奠定了基础。

items.title: Preliminary Synthesis and Basic Performance Characterization of Bio-Based Composite Materials Using Starch and Gelatin as Representative Matrix Phases: Exploratory Conceptual Design for Sustainable Toy Scenarios
items.abstract: The overconsumption of traditional plastic products causes serious white pollution and ecological pressure. Bio-based composites derived from natural polymers have emerged as promising sustainable alternatives. This work preliminarily fabricates starch- and gelatin-based composite films modified with natural fillers, and characterizes their basic physicochemical properties, dyeing performance, mechanical behavior, soil burial mass loss, and seed germination responses. On the basis of the tested baseline properties, tentative conceptual design schemes for eco-friendly toys were proposed. Notably, all experimental results in this work are preliminary and limited by insufficient experimental replicates. This study provides only basic experimental data and preliminary feasibility references for developing natural polymer composites for low-carbon consumer product scenarios.
items.authors: Lijuan Mao, Yuxin Gong, Chenyang Liu, Zhenpeng Li

items.title: Exploring SPI-Based Machine Learning and Statistical Models for Drought Prediction in Southeastern Romania
items.abstract: This study analyzes the performance of several forecasting models applied to Standardized Precipitation Index (SPI) time series for the 1967–2021 period, using data from six weather stations in southeastern Romania. Four temporal aggregation scales (SPI3, SPI6, SPI12, and SPI24) were considered for one-step-ahead (one-month) forecasting. The evaluated models included Random Forest, XGBoost, Support Vector Regression (SVR), N-BEATS (generic variant), and SARIMA (Seasonal Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average), covering machine learning, deep learning, and statistical approaches. To ensure a rigorous out-of-sample evaluation, SPI distribution parameters were estimated solely based on the pre-test calibration period and held constant when calculating SPI values for the independent test period, thereby preventing information leakage from the preprocessing stage. Forecast performance was assessed using RMSE, MAE, NSE, and a skill score relative to a persistence benchmark, while differences in forecast accuracy were statistically evaluated using the Diebold–Mariano test. The results revealed a clear scale-dependent pattern: absolute forecast accuracy increased with the SPI aggregation scale—alongside more pronounced temporal persistence—though this did not necessarily translate into superior skill compared to the persistence model. Among the data-driven models, SVR demonstrated the most robust performance, particularly at shorter timescales, while N-BEATS also provided competitive forecasts without consistently outperforming SVR. SARIMA showed the clearest gains over the persistence model at the SPI12 and SPI24 scales. The maximum NSE increased from 0.61 for SPI3 and 0.81 for SPI6, both obtained with SVR, to 0.94 for SPI12 (obtained with SARIMA) and 0.97 for SPI24 (obtained with SARIMA, N-BEATS and SVR).
