In conclusion, the results demonstrate that the SPI accumulation scale, temporal structure, and performance relative to persistence must be considered simultaneously when selecting forecasting models for drought prediction.
items.authors: Cristina Serban, Anata-Flavia Ionescu, Carmen Maftei, Mihaela-Bianca Alexoiu (Malancus)

items.title: Developing a Dual-Targeting CD33/CD70 CAR T-Cell Strategy Against Acute Myeloid Leukemia to Overcome Tumor Heterogeneity
items.abstract: Background: Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) remains the deadliest form of leukemia in children and adults despite therapeutic advances in recent decades. Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell therapy is one such therapeutic approach that has been explored preclinically and clinically in AML; however, its efficacy is limited by antigen heterogeneity. To overcome this roadblock, we propose a dual-targeting CAR T-cell strategy, targeting the AML-associated antigens CD33 and CD70. Methods: To recapitulate tumor heterogeneity, we genetically edited the AML cell line Molm-13 using CRISPR-Cas9 to generate distinct sublines, namely CD33+/CD70−, CD33−/CD70+, and CD33+/CD70+. Two dual-targeting CAR T-cell approaches were developed: a “pooled” product, in which CAR T cells directed towards CD33 or CD70 are combined and co-administered, and a “co-transduced” product, wherein one population of T cells is transduced with both CD33-CAR- and CD70-CAR-encoding viral vectors. Results: Pooled and co-transduced products demonstrated potent cytotoxicity against all Molm-13 populations, whereas single-antigen CAR approaches were not as effective when their respective target antigen was absent. Mice engrafted with CD33/CD70 heterogeneous Molm-13 cells were treated with pooled or co-transduced CD33/CD70 CAR T cells. Both groups exhibited a significant survival advantage over the untreated group, with the co-transduced approach showing a statistically significant advantage over the pooled group. Conclusions: In summary, engineering one T cell to express both CARs yielded superior cytotoxicity when targeting a heterogeneous AML blast population.
items.authors: Emily C. Sullivan, Nabil Saleem, Areeba A. Hashmi, Kristopher A. Knight, Austre Y. Schiaffino Bustamante, Ahmed A. Aljudi

items.title: Beyond Affine Layers: Bounded Ball Coverings to Preclude Gradient Vanishing
items.abstract: Traditional deep learning architectures relying on standard affine layers partition the representation space into unbounded polyhedral regions, which inherently introduce systemic structural vulnerabilities when learning complex, non-convex data manifolds. To resolve these limitations, we introduce an alternative "bounded-by-design" geometric framework that completely moves beyond traditional affine transformations. By replacing hyperplanes entirely with variable-radius ball coverings, we reformulate layer mechanics around the fundamental metric of a feature point's proximity to localized multi-spherical anchor centers. Crucially, by mapping this distance metric directly onto localized, parallel inner products, the formulation fully preserves standard batch-level GPU parallelization performance without higher-order computational overhead. Mathematical and visual validation demonstrates that our bounded formulation effectively encapsulates complex topological boundaries, eliminates representational redundancy in empty background spaces, and structurally stabilizes error propagation at the mathematical root.
items.authors: Mengnien Wu

items.title: Effects of Mineral Vitamin Premixes on Dough Mixing and Bread Properties in White and Wholemeal Wheat Formulations
items.abstract: This study compared white type 650 and wholemeal wheat breads containing two mineral–vitamin premixes, with or without dried sourdough. Twelve formulations contained 0 or approximately 0.10% premix relative to flour. In the farinograph data, Premix 2 increased dough stability from 5:55 to 15:00 min in white flour and from 1:56 to 9:42 min in wholemeal flour. Premix-only bread volumes were 355–360 versus 370 cm³/100 g for the white control and 305–308 versus 310 cm³/100 g for the wholemeal control. Across all 12 breads, the tabulated zinc and selenium concentrations ranged from 0.155 to 0.851 mg/100 g and 0.369 to 9.457 µg/100 g; vitamin D and E ranged from 0.10 to 8.40 µg/100 g and 0.06 to 4.42 mg/100 g, respectively. All comparisons are descriptive; no estimates of baking retention or nutrient bioavailability were made.
items.authors: Șerban-Eugen Cucu, Alina Alexandra Dobre, Elena Mirela Cucu

items.title: Non-Archimedean Smale Mean Value and Dubinin–Sugawa Dual Mean Value Problems
items.abstract: Motivated by the Smale mean value and the Dubinin–Sugawa dual mean value theorems, we formulate non-Archimedean Smale mean value and Dubinin–Sugawa dual mean value problems. We show that if a universal constant satisfying the non-Archimedean Smale mean value problem exists, it must be greater than or equal to one and if a universal constant satisfying the non-Archimedean Dubinin–Sugawa dual mean value problem exists, it must be less than or equal to one. We also derive other bounds whenever roots of unity exist in a non-Archimedean field.
items.authors: K. Mahesh Krishna

items.title: Harnessing Ratoon Cropping for Mitigating Greenhouse Gas Emissions
items.abstract: Ratoon cropping systems have gained increasing attention for their potential to mitigate greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, including carbon dioxide (CO2), methane (CH4), and nitrous oxide (N2O). Building on the well-established root system of the previous crop, ratoon crops require no land preparation, sowing, or transplanting and need less fertilizer, water, and pesticides than annual crops while achieving earlier harvests, thereby reducing GHG emission intensity (GHGI) by 7.9–17.3% and N2O emissions by 40.4–78.1%. Reduced fertilization, efficient water management, and integrated pest management can further curtail GHG emissions, while improved soil fertility, sustainable land management, and cover crop integration enhance soil carbon sequestration. Genetic improvement of ratoon crops can additionally enhance stress tolerance and resource use efficiency, reducing fertilizer requirements and ultimately lowering GHG emissions. This review also addresses ratoon cropping in dryland systems, including sugarcane, sorghum, cotton, and pigeon pea, highlighting their distinct GHG emission profiles and mitigation potential. Its innovative contribution is an integrated framework—synthesizing crop physiology, soil carbon processes, agronomic management, and genetic improvement—that evaluates GHG mitigation opportunities across both ratoon rice and dryland ratoon crops while explicitly addressing trade-offs, context-dependency, and evidence gaps.
items.authors: Xin Zhang, Hai Huang, Zengqiang Li, Xiangjun Kong, Aziz Khan, Yanbo Zhang

items.title: Hysteresis of Suspension Shock Absorbers: Modeling and Effects on Vehicle Dynamic Performance
items.abstract: Hysteresis is widely observed in vehicle suspension shock absorbers and can significantly influence vehicle dynamic responses. Although various hysteresis models have been developed to reproduce experimentally observed force–velocity loops, the effects of damper hysteresis on the overall dynamic performance of passive and semi-active suspension systems remain insufficiently quantified. In this study, a parameterized physics-based damper model is developed by incorporating hydraulic-oil compressibility and pressure-dependent gas dissolution and release. The model is experimentally validated using the force–velocity characteristics of a commercial twin-tube hydraulic shock absorber and is subsequently integrated into passive and semi-active suspension systems. Suspension performance is evaluated under bump and random road excitations in terms of settling time, body acceleration (BA), suspension working space (SWS), and dynamic tire deflection (DTD). The results show that the influence of damper hysteresis depends on both the excitation condition and the suspension configuration. Under bump-road excitation, hysteresis reduces the peak BA and DTD while increasing the peak SWS for both passive and semi-active suspensions, and it shortens the corresponding settling times. The variations are more pronounced in the semi-active suspension. Under random road excitation, hysteresis increases the RMS values of BA and DTD by 6.10% and 4.70%, respectively, for the passive suspension, and by 11.09% and 6.86%, respectively, for the semi-active suspension employing skyhook control. The RMS value of SWS also increases, although its variation is comparatively smaller. These results demonstrate that damper hysteresis produces excitation- and response-dependent effects rather than a uniformly detrimental influence on suspension performance. The proposed modeling framework provides a physically interpretable basis for high-fidelity suspension simulation and for the design and evaluation of suspension control strategies considering damper hysteresis.
items.authors: Dongliang Wang, Jun Wang, Diandian Cui, Ning Zhang

items.title: Irisin in Cardiovascular Health and Disease: A Review of Its Function as a Biomarker and Therapeutic Target in Atherosclerosis and Related Conditions
items.abstract: Atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) remains the leading cause of mortality worldwide, necessitating novel biomarkers and therapeutic targets. Irisin, a myokine derived from FNDC5, has emerged as a molecule of interest owing to its pleiotropic effects, yet its role in cardiovascular health is debated amid conflicting clinical findings and severe measurement challenges. This review synthesizes and critically evaluates the evidence on irisin in ASCVD, examining its molecular mechanisms, potential as a clinical biomarker, and hurdles for therapeutic application. Preclinical evidence has demonstrated that irisin exerts multifaceted cardioprotective effects: it mitigates cellular stress by enhancing mitochondrial quality control and inhibiting apoptosis and pyroptosis; preserves vascular integrity by promoting angiogenesis and preventing pathological remodeling; and enhances the efficacy of regenerative stem cell therapies. Most clinical studies have revealed an inverse correlation between circulating irisin levels and the presence and severity of ASCVD, heart failure, and related inflammatory conditions. However, these studies are predominantly observational and often cross-sectional, frequently with small sample sizes, and paradoxical elevations occur in certain metabolic states and during acute cardiac injury. Critically, the field is hampered by profound measurement inconsistencies, with reported values spanning picograms to micrograms per millilitre, making cross-study comparisons and clinical cutoffs currently impossible. Irisin appears to be an important endogenous factor in cardiovascular health, and preclinical evidence suggests that it is a promising candidate therapeutic target; however, clinical validation is lacking. Standardization of irisin assays remains the critical step required to determine whether irisin can become a reliable clinical biomarker.
items.authors: Siarhei A. Dabravolski, Sergey Shityakov, Nikita A. Mitkin, Ulyana V. Rozhkova, Stanislav A. Antonov, Aleksandra S. Utkina
items.title_zh: Irisin在心血管健康与疾病中的作用综述
items.summary_zh: 动脉粥样硬化性心血管疾病（ASCVD）是全球主要死亡原因，急需新的生物标志物和治疗靶点。Irisin是一种源自FNDC5的肌肉细胞因子，因其多重效应而受到关注，但其在心血管健康中的作用存在争议。本文综述了Irisin在ASCVD中的分子机制、作为临床生物标志物的潜力及其治疗应用的挑战。前临床研究表明，Irisin具有多方面的心脏保护作用：通过增强线粒体质量控制和抑制细胞凋亡及焦亡来减轻细胞压力；通过促进血管生成和防止病理重塑来维持血管完整性；并增强再生干细胞治疗的疗效。大多数临床研究显示循环Irisin水平与ASCVD、心力衰竭及相关炎症状态的存在和严重程度呈负相关。然而，这些研究主要为观察性且多为横断面研究，样本量通常较小，并且在某些代谢状态和急性心脏损伤中出现矛盾的升高。
items.l1_lead: Irisin在心血管健康中具有潜在的保护作用，但其作为生物标志物和治疗靶点的有效性仍需进一步研究和验证。
items.l2_summary:
动脉粥样硬化性心血管疾病（ASCVD）是全球主要的死亡原因之一，因此迫切需要新的生物标志物和治疗靶点。Irisin是一种源自FNDC5的肌肉细胞因子，因其多重生物学效应而受到广泛关注，但其在心血管健康中的具体作用仍存在争议。本文综述了Irisin在ASCVD中的分子机制、作为临床生物标志物的潜力以及其在治疗应用中面临的挑战。

前临床研究表明，Irisin具有多方面的心脏保护作用。首先，它通过增强线粒体质量控制和抑制细胞凋亡及焦亡来减轻细胞压力；其次，Irisin能够促进血管生成并防止病理重塑，从而维持血管的完整性；此外，Irisin还被发现能够增强再生干细胞治疗的疗效。这些发现为Irisin在心血管健康中的潜在应用提供了理论基础。

然而，大多数临床研究的结果显示，循环Irisin水平与ASCVD、心力衰竭及相关炎症状态的存在和严重程度呈负相关。这些研究主要是观察性研究，且多为横断面研究，样本量通常较小，导致结果的普遍性和可靠性受到限制。此外，在某些代谢状态和急性心脏损伤中，Irisin水平出现了矛盾的升高现象，这进一步增加了对其生物学作用的复杂性和不确定性。

综上所述，尽管Irisin在心血管健康中展现出一定的保护作用，并且作为生物标志物的潜力值得进一步探索，但目前的临床证据仍不够充分，且存在诸多挑战。因此，未来的研究需要更大规模的样本和更系统的设计，以明确Irisin在ASCVD中的具体作用及其临床应用的可行性。

items.title: Mitochondrial Genomes of Micropterus cataractae, Micropterus henshalli, and Micropterus punctulatus: Expanded Genetic Resources for Management
items.abstract: The shoal bass (SHB; Micropterus cataractae) and the Alabama bass (ALB; Micropterus henshalli) are species of freshwater fish in the Centrarchidae family of the order Centrarchiformes native to many states in the southeastern United States. Shoal bass currently face the threat of introgression with introduced black bass species in their native range. Conversely, Alabama bass have been introduced both intentionally by state resource managers and illegally by anglers outside of their native range throughout the United States, which could cause introgression with largemouth bass (M. nigricans) and other black bass species. In this study, we establish the first reference mitogenomes of ALB, SHB and spotted bass (SPB; M. punctulatus) for mitochondrial phylogenetics and (meta-)barcoding, which will also facilitate further variant detection in this clade by population-level resequencing. Total lengths of the ALB, SHB, and SPB mitogenomes are 16,480 bp (G + C; 47.1%), 16,487 bp (G + C; 46.6%) and 16,486 bp (G + C; 46.7%), respectively. The mitogenomes are consistent with those of other Micropterus spp. in respect of coding region content and organization. Primer sets targeting the 12S rRNA and 16S rRNA genes commonly used in environmental DNA (eDNA) metabarcoding applications were evaluated, and those suitable to discriminate species-level identification of these species were identified. The information presented here can be applied to inform SHB conservation efforts in their native range and the biosurveillance and control of introduced ALB.
items.authors: Julianna J. Jett, Clayton D. Raines, Patricia M. Mazik, Steven M. Sammons, Cynthia F. Holt, Morgan B. Cooper

items.title: Performance Analysis of Clustered Integrated Sensing and Communication Networks
items.abstract: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) provides a promising approach for IoT networks by combining data transmission with target sensing over shared hardware. Different from prior studies centered on the performance of ISAC networks with uniformly distributed nodes, this work explores ISAC networks with clustered distributed nodes. An analytical model based on stochastic geometry is established to assess both the probabilities of sensing and communication in clustered ISAC networks. The study highlights the influence of factors such as cluster density, node distribution, and cluster size on both sensing and communication performance. Simulations validate the accuracy of the proposed model and demonstrate that fine-tuning cluster parameters can significantly improve the performance of clustered ISAC networks.
items.authors: Qiu Wang, Yunbo Zhao, Mingzhi Song, Xuran Li, Lei Chen, Chuangeng Tian

items.title: From Thoracotomy to Robotic Platforms in Thoracic Surgery: Technical Evolution, Simulation-Based Training, and Surgical Outcomes
items.abstract: Thoracic surgery has progressively moved from open thoracotomy to video-assisted and robot-assisted approaches, reducing access-related trauma while changing the technical environment in which pulmonary resections are performed and taught. This narrative review examines the clinical evolution of open, video-assisted thoracic surgery (VATS), and robot-assisted thoracic surgery (RATS), with particular attention to the evidence supporting their perioperative and oncological outcomes, the learning curves associated with minimally invasive surgery, and the role of simulation-based training. Randomized trials now provide robust evidence that VATS improve postoperative recovery compared with thoracotomy in appropriately selected patients with predominantly early-stage non-small cell lung cancer, without compromising long-term oncological outcomes. Randomized comparisons between RATS and VATS support RATS as an oncologically acceptable minimally invasive alternative and suggest advantages in selected technical endpoints, particularly blood loss and lymph node retrieval, but do not demonstrate consistent superiority in major clinical or survival outcomes. Learning curves vary according to previous experience, case complexity, supervision, institutional volume, and the endpoint used to define competence, making fixed case-number thresholds an incomplete measure of proficiency. Simulation can improve selected technical skills and provide objective performance assessment, although evidence becomes progressively less robust when moving from simulator performance to operating room transfer and patient-level outcomes. Surgical approach, therefore, should be interpreted within a broader framework that includes patient and tumour characteristics, oncological quality, surgical expertise, institutional resources, and structured training.
items.authors: Michele Piazzolla, Doroty Sampietro, Marco Donatello Delcuratolo, Paolo Nicola Camillo Girotti, Lucia Anna Muscarella, Paola Parente
items.title_zh: 胸外科手术技术演变：从开胸到机器人平台
items.summary_zh: 胸外科手术逐渐从开放性开胸手术转向视频辅助和机器人辅助方法，减少了手术相关创伤，同时改变了肺切除手术的技术环境及教学方式。本文综述了开放性胸外科手术、视频辅助胸外科手术（VATS）和机器人辅助胸外科手术（RATS）的临床演变，重点关注其围手术期和肿瘤学结果的证据、微创手术的学习曲线及模拟训练的作用。随机试验提供了有力证据，表明在适当选择的早期非小细胞肺癌患者中，VATS相比开胸手术改善了术后恢复，且不影响长期肿瘤学结果。RATS与VATS的随机比较支持RATS作为一种肿瘤学上可接受的微创替代方案，并在特定技术指标上显示出优势，尤其是出血量和淋巴结回收，但在主要临床或生存结果上未表现出一致的优越性。学习曲线因先前经验、病例复杂性、监督、机构量和定义能力的终点而异，固定病例数量阈值无法完整衡量熟练程度。
items.l1_lead: 胸外科手术技术正从开放手术向微创视频辅助和机器人辅助方法转变，显著减少创伤并改善术后恢复，但不同技术的临床效果尚需进一步研究。
items.l2_summary:
胸外科手术技术经历了显著的演变，从传统的开放性开胸手术逐渐转向视频辅助胸外科手术（VATS）和机器人辅助胸外科手术（RATS），这一转变不仅减少了手术相关的创伤，也改变了肺切除手术的技术环境和教学方式。研究表明，VATS在适当选择的早期非小细胞肺癌患者中，相较于开胸手术，能够改善术后恢复，并且不影响长期的肿瘤学结果。随机试验提供了有力的证据支持这一观点，显示出VATS在围手术期的优势。

与此同时，RATS作为一种新兴的微创手术方法，与VATS的随机比较显示出RATS在某些技术指标上具有优势，例如出血量和淋巴结回收。然而，在主要的临床或生存结果上，RATS并未表现出一致的优越性。这表明，尽管RATS在某些方面可能更具优势，但在整体效果上仍需进一步的研究和验证。

此外，学习曲线的研究显示，手术者的先前经验、病例的复杂性、监督程度、机构的手术量以及定义能力的终点等因素都会影响学习曲线的表现。因此，固定的病例数量阈值并不能全面衡量外科医生的熟练程度，这提示我们在培训和评估外科医生时需要更加灵活和全面的方法。

综上所述，胸外科手术技术的演变不仅提升了手术的安全性和有效性，也对外科医生的培训和技术掌握提出了新的挑战和要求。随着微创手术技术的不断发展，未来的研究将继续探索如何优化手术方法，提高患者的术后恢复质量和长期生存率。

items.title: Synergetic Control Framework for Autonomous UAV Swarm Coordination
items.abstract: This study presents a synergetic control approach for coordinating the motion of a UAV swarm based on self-organization principles and energy potential interactions. The proposed method effectively addresses the known limitations of traditional potential field techniques by introducing a procedure for synthesizing the synergetic control of swarm motion using a virtual force field with symmetric attraction and repulsion functions. A Lyapunov/LaSalle stability analysis and a geometric safety radius argument show that this keeps the swarm’s motion conflict-free, subject to the platform’s kinematic constraints, and supports stable formation maintenance. Damping terms are incorporated into the equations of motion to eliminate self-oscillations and, via an energy (Lyapunov) argument, we show that the resulting system converges to the critical point set of the total interaction potential. A synergetic controller based on virtual pendulum meters is introduced to prevent stagnation. A specialized mathematical framework is developed to mitigate the curse of dimensionality, as confirmed through simulations, although the per-step computational cost scales approximately quadratically with swarm size. The swarm formation time increases sublinearly with the number of UAVs, highlighting the approach’s scalability. A swarm self-organization modeling study reveals three characteristic phases: namely, chaotic motions, transitional reconfiguration, and ordered swarm behavior. The formation process corresponds to a gradual minimization of inter-UAV interaction energy, while stable collective motion is achieved by maintaining a constant polarization of vehicle heading angles. Through simulations, parameter ranges that provide optimal synergetic properties during swarm formation and coordinated movement are identified. The findings are further illustrated, as a proof of concept, through real-world experimental tests of swarm control.
items.authors: Valerii Chepizhenko, Svitlana Pavlova, Fuzhong Li

items.title: Phosphatidic Acid Vesicles Convert the Prion Protein into β-Sheet Fibrils with a Thermostable Structure but Temperature-Sensitive Packing
items.abstract: Biomolecular cofactors, including nucleic acids and lipids, promote conversion of the cellular prion protein (PrPC) into pathogenic assemblies (prion scrapie, PrPSc), yet the mechanistic role of specific membrane lipids in the earliest stages remains unclear. Previous work showed that phosphatidic acid (PA) vesicles interact in vitro with murine recombinant PrP (recPrP) and trigger PrP aggregation without additional cofactors. Here, we dissect the PA-driven conversion pathway by monitoring PrP assembly and aggregate stability using spectroscopy and by comparing full-length recPrP with an N-terminally truncated construct. PA vesicles induced aggregation in both PrP constructs with similar efficiency, indicating that PA-mediated conversion does not require residues 23–89. Thermal stability analyses revealed a thermally resilient β-structured state accompanied by temperature-sensitive, partially reversible ThT binding, which we interpret as remodelling of higher-order packing. Time-resolved measurements showed that assembly reached a plateau within the measurement time resolution at all temperatures tested, with no resolvable lag phase. At plateau, the extent of ThT-positive assembly was greatest under conditions of higher bilayer order, while light scattering and secondary-structure content were comparable across temperatures. PrP alone showed no detectable temperature-dependent secondary-structure changes between 10 and 40 °C, consistent with membrane organization contributing to assembly architecture. Together, these results establish PA vesicles as a tractable model for interrogating cofactor-driven early prion aggregation and support membrane lipids and their physical state as modulators of PrP conversion into β-structured assemblies, with implications for mechanistic studies and screening strategies targeting lipid–protein interactions.
items.authors: Cyntia Alves, Gabriela Assis-de-Lemos, Michel W. Jaworek, Guilherme A. P. de Oliveira, Roland Winter, Jerson Lima Silva

items.title: Spatial Data Fusion and Machine Learning Bias Correction for Convection-Permitting Atmospheric Downscaling and Multi-Criteria Site Feasibility Mapping in Complex Coastal Terrains
items.abstract: High-resolution atmospheric modeling over topographically complex coastal zones requires multi-source spatial data fusion to bridge the scale gap between satellite-assimilated global reanalysis and localized boundary layer dynamics. This study presents a spatial data fusion framework coupling convection-permitting Weather Research and Forecasting (WRF) simulations (3 km grid spacing) with machine learning calibration and GIS multi-criteria decision analysis across continuous computational grids (24,871 cells). Focusing on a high-resolution seasonal case study during the peak Caribbean Low-Level Jet (CLLJ) and Trade Winds regime along the Colombian Caribbean coast, predictive algorithms were benchmarked across day-grouped and Leave-One-Station-Out (LOSO) spatial transfer protocols against classical meteorological baselines. Support Vector Regression (SVR) with an RBF kernel achieved superior residual calibration (R2=0.9523, RMSE=0.4601 m/s) under day-grouped cross-validation, and an average Leave-One-Station-Out (LOSO) spatial transfer RMSE of 1.1030 m/s under blind geographic transfer to unmonitored stations, corresponding to a 76% RMSE reduction relative to raw, uncalibrated WRF output in that same spatial-transfer setting. Chronological forward-forecasting tests further showed that this seasonally augmented kernel model does not extrapolate reliably to calendar months absent from training (R2=−0.09), so a reduced 8-variable configuration is recommended for genuine forward forecasting into unseen seasons. Scalar calibrations were transferred to horizontal wind vectors preserving simulated flow direction, and vertically scaled to 80 m hub height using WRF prognostic shear. Calibrated fields were integrated into a Boolean GIS-MCDA model incorporating wind power density, slope limits, environmental/indigenous reserves, and infrastructure proximity. The framework delineated an 8.9% high-feasibility macro-corridor (2214 cells; ≈19,926 km2) in northern La Guajira, while substantially reducing uncalibrated mesoscale overestimation in the sheltered wake of the Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta. The methodology provides a robust screening-level tool for coastal renewable resource assessment.
items.authors: Andres Valle-Gonzalez, Maryam Carrillo-Reales, Adalberto Ospino-Castro, Diego Restrepo-Leal, Carlos Robles-Algarín

items.title: Moisture-Dependent Compressive Behavior of Wheat Kernels: Implications for Energy-Efficient and Resource-Conscious Grain Processing
items.abstract: Improving grain size-reduction efficiency requires settings adapted to raw-material properties. This study examined how moisture, crosshead speed, imposed displacement, cultivar, and wheat quality group affect individual-kernel compression. Four cultivars representing bread and ‘other’ quality groups were tested at nominal moisture contents of 14–20% (wet basis), crosshead speeds of 5–30 mm min−1, and displacements of 1.8–2.2 mm. Maximum force, crushing energy, and apparent cracking were determined. Crosshead speed did not significantly affect maximum force and had a marginal effect on crushing energy. Displacement and cultivar explained the largest variability shares, while both responses reached their highest means at 18% nominal moisture. Lawina and Sikorka, both in the ‘other’ group, differed by approximately 36% in maximum force and 25% in crushing energy. The share without apparent cracking rose from approximately 5% at 14% to 96% at 20%. Unlike our earlier study of six quality wheat cultivars, this study compares bread and ‘other’ groups and examines differences between cultivars assigned to the same group. The findings inform product-specific screening; industrial energy and material savings remain to be verified.
items.authors: Zdzisław Kaliniewicz

items.title: An Integrated Biological Model for Precision Pulmonary Rehabilitation in COPD
items.abstract: Pulmonary rehabilitation improves symptoms, exercise capacity and quality of life in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), although patients with similar clinical characteristics often show different responses. This review summarizes the biological determinants of rehabilitation responsiveness identified through more than 10 years of translational research. Evidence from longitudinal studies of elderly patients with severe COPD undergoing standardized pulmonary rehabilitation was integrated with clinical, functional, molecular, immunological, cognitive, behavioural and lifestyle data, including long-term follow-up. Baseline DNA damage was markedly increased and further rose during rehabilitation (19.6 ± 7.3% vs. 21.8 ± 7.2% tail intensity) despite significant functional improvement. FKBP5 rs4713916 was the only genetic variant associated with better rehabilitation outcomes. Daily vegetable intake independently predicted treatment success, whereas smoking was associated with oxidative DNA damage, immune alterations and higher Torque Teno Virus (TTV) load. TTV ≥ 4 log10 copies/mL was associated with increased regulatory T cells, reduced α7 nicotinic acetylcholine receptor expression (31% vs. 52%; p = 0.023) and shorter 5-year survival (609 ± 160 vs. 937 ± 94 days; p = 0.017). Active Coping, Planning and Self-Distraction were the behavioural strategies most strongly associated with rehabilitation response. Cognitive impairment and obesity-related immune regulation further contributed to patient heterogeneity. These observations suggest that rehabilitation responsiveness reflects the interaction of genomic, immune, behavioural and lifestyle factors. Their integration may improve patient stratification and support the development of precision pulmonary rehabilitation
items.authors: Patrizia Russo, Laura Vitiello, Carlo Tomino, Giorgio Felzani, Massimo Fini, Stefano Bonassi

items.title: Beyond Genotype: Integrating Phenoconversion into Pharmacogenetic Decision-Making in Psychiatry
items.abstract: Interindividual variability in psychotropic drug response contributes to treatment failure, adverse drug reactions, and repeated medication adjustments. Pharmacogenetics supports precision prescribing by identifying genetic variants associated with drug metabolism, efficacy, and tolerability, and evidence-based recommendations are available for several psychotropic medications. However, genotype predicts metabolic capacity rather than the enzyme activity actually expressed in vivo or the systemic drug exposure achieved at a given time. This narrative review examines phenoconversion, the mismatch between genotype-predicted and observed metabolic phenotype, and its implications for psychiatric pharmacotherapy. Drug–drug interactions, smoking, inflammation, physiological changes, and disease-related factors can modify drug-metabolizing enzyme activity or otherwise alter systemic drug exposure despite an unchanged genotype. We discuss how these influences can limit the applicability of genotype-based dosing recommendations and propose a dynamic framework integrating pharmacogenetic results with concomitant medications, clinical conditions, lifestyle factors, therapeutic drug monitoring, and longitudinal changes in patient status. This framework may also refine the assessment of treatment adequacy, because prescribed dose, duration, and adherence do not necessarily ensure adequate drug exposure. Future clinical decision-support systems should combine pharmacogenetic and longitudinal clinical data to enable more individualized and dynamically informed psychopharmacological treatment.
items.authors: Tiziano Prodi, Maria Gabriela Nielsen, Floriana De Cillis, Nadia Cattane, Moira Marizzoni, Marco Andrea Riva
items.title_zh: 超越基因型：将表型转化纳入精神科药物基因决策
items.summary_zh: 个体间在精神药物反应上的差异导致治疗失败、不良药物反应及反复调整用药。药物基因组学通过识别与药物代谢、疗效和耐受性相关的遗传变异，支持精准处方，并为多种精神药物提供了基于证据的建议。然而，基因型预测的是代谢能力，而非实际在体内表达的酶活性或特定时间内的系统药物暴露。本文回顾了表型转化，即基因型预测与观察到的代谢表型之间的不匹配及其对精神药物治疗的影响。药物间相互作用、吸烟、炎症、生理变化及疾病相关因素可在基因型不变的情况下改变药物代谢酶活性或系统药物暴露。我们讨论了这些影响如何限制基于基因型的剂量推荐的适用性，并提出一个动态框架，将药物基因组学结果与同时用药、临床状况、生活方式因素、治疗药物监测及患者状态的纵向变化相结合。该框架可能还会改善治疗充分性的评估，因为处方剂量、持续时间和依从性并不一定能确保治疗的充分性。
items.l1_lead: 精神药物治疗应超越基因型，结合表型转化和多种影响因素，以提高个体化治疗的有效性和安全性。
items.l2_summary:
在精神药物治疗中，个体间对药物反应的差异常常导致治疗失败、不良反应及频繁的用药调整。药物基因组学（pharmacogenomics）通过识别与药物代谢、疗效及耐受性相关的遗传变异，为精准处方提供了支持，并为多种精神药物提供了基于证据的用药建议。然而，基因型（genotype）只能预测个体的代谢能力，而无法反映体内实际的酶活性或特定时间内的药物暴露情况。因此，本文回顾了表型转化（phenotypic translation）这一概念，强调基因型预测与观察到的代谢表型之间的不匹配对精神药物治疗的影响。

研究表明，药物间的相互作用、吸烟、炎症、生理变化及疾病相关因素等都可能在基因型不变的情况下，显著改变药物代谢酶的活性或系统药物的暴露水平。这些因素的变化限制了基于基因型的剂量推荐的适用性，可能导致治疗效果不佳。因此，本文提出了一个动态框架，旨在将药物基因组学的结果与同时用药、临床状况、生活方式因素、治疗药物监测及患者状态的纵向变化相结合。该框架的引入可能有助于改善治疗充分性的评估，因为处方剂量、持续时间和依从性并不一定能确保治疗的充分性。

综上所述，尽管药物基因组学为精神药物的个体化治疗提供了重要的理论基础，但在实际应用中，考虑表型转化及其影响因素对于提高治疗效果和患者安全性至关重要。通过整合多种临床和生活方式因素，能够更全面地评估患者的治疗需求，从而优化精神药物的使用。

items.title: Phenyllactic Acid Suppresses Growth and Induces Coordinated Changes in PSII Photochemistry and Energy Dissipation in the Filamentous Cyanobacterium Dolichospermum sp. FACHB-82
items.abstract: Dolichospermum sp. FACHB-82, a representative harmful bloom-forming cyanobacterium, has garnered widespread attention in freshwater ecosystems due to its high environmental adaptability and potential for rapid proliferation. Phenyllactic acid (PLA) is a structurally defined aromatic organic acid with known antimicrobial activity, but its inhibitory effects on FACHB-82 and their photosynthetic apparatus remain poorly understood. In this study, we investigated the concentration-dependent effects of PLA on biomass accumulation, photosynthetic pigment production and photosynthetic activity in FACHB-82. The findings revealed that PLA induced a concentration-dependent biphasic response on biomass accumulation and photosynthetic pigment synthesis of FACHB-82. Chlorophyll a fluorescence analyses revealed that high-concentration PLA exposure disrupted functions of PSII at multiple levels, including reduced PSII performance, enhanced QA− accumulation, accelerated reaction center closure, decreased energetic connectivity, impaired donor side function, and restricted downstream electron transport. Although NPQ was significantly upregulated under high PLA stress, dark-recovery analysis demonstrated that the increased non-photochemical energy dissipation was accompanied by incomplete recovery of PSII photochemical efficiency. Our finding, for the first time, provides physiological insight into the anticyanobacterial activity of PLA for the control of FACHB-82 growth, thus offering a theoretical basis for the control of cyanobacterial blooms.
items.authors: Jie Cheng, Long Tan, Xiu Zhang, Zhenxia Zhu, Jiashun Li, Chaobo Zhang

items.title: Ubiquitination-Dependent Cyclin Regulation in Gastric Cancer and Emerging Targeted Therapies with Chinese Herbal Bioactive Compounds
items.abstract: Gastric cancer (GC) remains one of the most prevalent malignancies worldwide, with a high mortality rate primarily attributable to late-stage diagnosis and limited therapeutic options. Aberrant cell proliferation arising from cell cycle dysregulation is a hallmark of GC pathogenesis. Cyclins, as core regulators of cell cycle progression, exhibit dynamic protein expression patterns that are tightly controlled by the ubiquitin–proteasome system (UPS). In GC, cyclins are frequently overexpressed due to impaired ubiquitination and subsequent proteasomal degradation. This review systematically elucidates the ubiquitination-mediated regulation of distinct cyclins (Cyclins D, E, A, and B) at specific cell cycle phases—G1, S, G2, and M—and highlights the critical roles of E3 ubiquitin ligases, including SCF complexes and APC/C, in GC progression. We further discuss how dysregulated non-coding RNAs and altered E3 ligase expression contribute to aberrant cyclin ubiquitination, thereby promoting GC cell proliferation, metastasis, and poor prognosis. Importantly, emerging evidence demonstrates that bioactive compounds derived from traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) can counteract these abnormalities by directly downregulating cyclin expression, modulating E3 ligase activity, or inhibiting 26S/20S proteasome function, thus restoring cell cycle homeostasis and suppressing GC growth. This review integrates molecular mechanisms of cyclin ubiquitination with TCM-based therapeutic strategies, offering novel insights into targeted interventions for GC.
items.authors: Sicheng Qian, Xinyi Zheng, Jiaqi Li, Jiahan Le, Jiangjiang Qin, Yitao Chen
items.title_zh: 胃癌中依赖泛素化的细胞周期蛋白调控及中药活性成分的靶向治疗
items.summary_zh: 胃癌（GC）是全球最常见的恶性肿瘤之一，因晚期诊断和治疗选择有限而导致高死亡率。细胞周期失调引起的异常细胞增殖是GC发病机制的特征。细胞周期蛋白作为细胞周期进程的核心调控因子，其蛋白表达模式受到泛素-蛋白酶体系统（UPS）的严格控制。在GC中，细胞周期蛋白因泛素化受损及随后的蛋白酶体降解而常常过表达。本文系统阐述了不同细胞周期阶段（G1、S、G2和M）中细胞周期蛋白（D、E、A和B型）的泛素化调控，并强调了E3泛素连接酶（如SCF复合物和APC/C）在GC进展中的关键作用。此外，讨论了非编码RNA失调和E3连接酶表达改变如何促进异常的细胞周期蛋白泛素化，从而推动GC细胞增殖、转移及预后不良。重要的是，越来越多的证据表明，传统中药中的活性成分可以通过直接下调细胞周期蛋白表达、调节E3连接酶活性或抑制26S/20S蛋白酶体功能，逆转这些异常，恢复细胞周期稳态并抑制GC生长。
items.l1_lead: 研究表明，胃癌中细胞周期蛋白的泛素化调控失常促进肿瘤进展，而中药活性成分可通过调节相关机制逆转这一过程，抑制胃癌生长。
items.l2_summary:
胃癌（GC）是全球最常见的恶性肿瘤之一，因其晚期诊断和治疗选择有限，导致了高死亡率。细胞周期失调引起的异常细胞增殖是胃癌发病机制的一个重要特征。细胞周期蛋白作为细胞周期进程的核心调控因子，其表达模式受到泛素-蛋白酶体系统（UPS）的严格控制。在胃癌中，细胞周期蛋白因泛素化受损及随后的蛋白酶体降解而常常出现过表达现象。研究表明，不同细胞周期阶段（G1、S、G2和M）中的细胞周期蛋白（如D型、E型、A型和B型）的泛素化调控具有重要意义，E3泛素连接酶（如SCF复合物和APC/C）在胃癌的进展中扮演着关键角色。

此外，非编码RNA的失调和E3连接酶表达的改变也被认为是促进异常细胞周期蛋白泛素化的重要因素，这些变化进一步推动了胃癌细胞的增殖、转移及预后不良。越来越多的证据表明，传统中药中的活性成分能够通过多种机制逆转这些异常现象。这些活性成分可以直接下调细胞周期蛋白的表达，调节E3连接酶的活性，或抑制26S/20S蛋白酶体的功能，从而恢复细胞周期的稳态并抑制胃癌的生长。这些发现为胃癌的靶向治疗提供了新的思路，强调了中药活性成分在调控细胞周期和改善胃癌预后方面的潜力。

items.title: Self-Perceived Knowledge and Self-Reported Clinical Use of Minimally Invasive Endodontics Among General Dentists and Endodontists in Türkiye: A Cross-Sectional Survey
items.abstract: Background/Objectives: Minimally invasive endodontics (MIE) has gained increasing attention as an approach focused on preserving dental tissues while achieving the objectives of endodontic treatment. This study compared self-perceived knowledge, perceived adequacy of education, self-reported clinical use and practices, implementation difficulties, and barriers to routine use of MIE approaches among general dentists and endodontists in Türkiye. Methods: This online cross-sectional survey used non-probability voluntary sampling and included 300 participants (150 general dentists and 150 endodontists). Group comparisons used Pearson’s chi-square test, Yates-corrected Pearson’s chi-square test, or Fisher’s exact test as appropriate. For multiple-response items, option-specific comparisons were adjusted using the Benjamini–Hochberg false discovery rate (FDR) procedure. Associated factors were evaluated using binary logistic regression, with professional group, professional experience, institutional setting, and weekly number of root canal treatments included simultaneously in multivariable models. Results: Endodontists reported higher self-perceived knowledge of MIE and more frequent self-reported use of MIE approaches than general dentists (both p 0.001). In multivariable models, endodontist status was associated with higher odds of reported use of vital pulp therapies (odds ratio (OR) = 5.626) and minimally invasive root canal preparation (OR = 2.238), whereas the association with minimally invasive access cavity use was not statistically significant (OR = 1.668; p = 0.200). General dentist status was associated with higher odds of reporting difficulties during vital pulp therapies (OR = 10.420) and minimally invasive root canal preparation (OR = 2.379), whereas no significant association was detected for minimally invasive access cavity difficulties. The use of magnification systems and specialized endodontic burs for access cavity preparation or refinement was reported more frequently among endodontists. Reduced loss of tooth structure was the most frequently selected reason for using MIE, while inadequate training or lack of knowledge was the most frequently reported barrier to routine implementation. Conclusions: Among the participating dentists, endodontists reported higher self-perceived MIE knowledge and more frequent self-reported clinical use than general dentists. Professional and practice-related characteristics were associated with several MIE-related outcomes. Greater emphasis on practical, case-based training may support the appropriate implementation of MIE; however, the findings should be interpreted in light of the cross-sectional, self-reported design.
items.authors: Selin Bıçaklıoğlu, Melis Oya Ateş

items.title: A Critical Reflection on the Eroded Burial Rites Among the Zezuru People of Chiota Area in Zimbabwe
items.abstract: In African societies, death is never viewed as the end of life but as a transition to another life. Among the Zezuru People of Zimbabwe, words such as watisiya, “he has left us”, and waenda, “he has gone”, present death as not the end but a rite of passage to the spiritual life. The same language of hope describes burial. Tamuviga: we have buried him, meaning something hidden will be sought later; tamuradzika: “we have slept him”; lit., we will bring back the spirit of the deceased during the kurova guva ceremony. Because of this hope for the future life, the traditional burial among Zezuru people is characterised by collective rituals such as kugeza mufi, “washing the deceased”, kupeta mufi, “folding the deceased”, kutenderera musha, “going round the home, zvioneko, “farewells”, kutema rukawo, “marking the grave”, and kuviga, ”burial”. Among the Zezuru people, death was a rite of passage in which ancestors were present. Communities conducted death, mourning, and burial rituals to mediate between the world of the dead and the world of the living; however, the church, funeral homes, and urban burials have eroded these burial traditions. This paper reflects on the erosion of burial rites among the Zezuru People of the Chihota area in Zimbabwe. This qualitative study asks: “How are the Zezuru people resacralising burial rites that had been eroded while also maintaining their identity?” Using postcolonial theory, the study collected data through observation of Zezuru burial traditions and interviews with 10 purposively selected participants. This paper concludes that, although Zezuru culture has been and is being eroded, they employ Homi Bhabha’s hybridity theory to maintain a balance between tradition and modernity. Structurally, this paper will present the introduction, the literature review, methods, theory, results, conclusion, and recommendations.
items.authors: Martin Mujinga

items.title: Trade-Offs in Growth Performance, Serum Biochemistry, and Fillet Amino Acid Profiles of Red Tilapia Fed Graded Levels of Azolla microphylla Meal in a Fishmeal Replacement Blend, with Exploratory Observations on Intestinal Microbiota
items.abstract: This study evaluated the replacement of commercial fishmeal with a combination of Azolla microphylla meal (AMM) and soybean meal in red tilapia (Oreochromis spp.) diets at 0%, 25%, 50%, and 75% fishmeal replacement over 60 days, followed by a sublethal Aeromonas hydrophila exposure. Soybean meal was increased alongside AMM to maintain isonitrogenous and isoenergetic diets; therefore, the observed responses reflect the combined replacement of fishmeal rather than the effect of AMM alone. Growth performance (WG, ADG, SGR) progressively declined and FCR increased with higher fishmeal replacement levels (p 0.05). Serum aspartate transaminase (AST) rose and alkaline phosphatase (ALP) fell at elevated replacement levels. Fillet total essential amino acids were significantly reduced only at 75% fishmeal replacement, indicating that moderate substitution (up to 50%) preserves nutritional quality. As an exploratory, descriptive endpoint, the intestinal microbiota was profiled using pooled samples (n = 1 composite per treatment per time point), precluding statistical inference. Within the pooled post-challenge profiles, Cetobacterium represented a high relative proportion in T1–T3, whereas the pooled T4 profile showed a more heterogeneous taxonomic composition. Because no independent microbiota replicates were available, these observations are descriptive and hypothesis-generating rather than evidence of dietary or challenge effects. Overall, fishmeal replacement above 25% impaired growth, whereas fillet total essential amino acids were maintained through 50% replacement. These effects should be interpreted as the combined outcome of replacing fishmeal with AMM and soybean meal. The pooled microbiota profiles provide preliminary observations for future replicated studies.
items.authors: Panitnart Auputinan, Nantapong Sumket, Somchart Tana, Payungsuk Intawicha, Phanit Srisuttha, Phadungnaree Saenmuang

items.title: Time-Dependent Dispersion of TiO2 Nanoparticles in 3D-Printed Denture Base Resin Using Probe Sonication
items.abstract: Titanium dioxide (TiO2) nanoparticles (NPs) can improve the performance of 3D-printed denture base resins; however, the reinforcing benefit depends on achieving uniform dispersion, and the effect of probe-sonication time on NP dispersion remains unclear. This study aimed to determine the sonication time (among 3, 5, and 7 min) producing the most qualitatively uniform TiO2 distribution. TiO2 NPs were silanized using 3-(trimethoxysilyl)propyl methacrylate, incorporated at 0.3 wt.% into a light-polymerizing 3D-printing resin, and probe sonicated. The resulting specimens were characterized by scanning electron microscopy, energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy, and Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy, and tested for surface roughness (Ra, μm) and Vickers hardness. Qualitatively, increasing sonication time progressively improved dispersion: the 7 min group showed the most homogeneous microstructure and titanium map. FTIR spectra were comparable across the groups, indicating preserved matrix chemistry. Surface roughness and hardness were not significantly different among the groups (p = 0.686 and p = 0.510, respectively). The 7 min group had the most qualitatively uniform TiO2 distribution. Although it had the numerically lowest surface hardness, it was not comparatively statistically significant. Therefore, within the tested conditions, the 7 min can be described as the most suitable duration for the primary dispersion objective. Additional tests (flexural strength, flexural modulus, and impact toughness) and degree-of-conversion analysis are necessary to confirm the effects of different sonication times.
items.authors: Berivan Nawzad Hadi, Rizgar Mohammed Ameen Hasan

items.title: Dual-Functionalized Electrospun PCL Membranes with Polydopamine/Gold Nanoparticles: Cytocompatibility Assessment for a Potential Cardiac Patch
items.abstract: Myocardial infarction causes scar tissue formation and poor electrical conduction. Cardiac patches are used to functionally support damaged cardiac tissue. Electrospun polycaprolactone (PCL) membranes, one of the most investigated biocompatible and biodegradable materials to be used as cardiac patch, have limitations due to inherent hydrophobicity and weak electrical conductivity. It was aimed at developing a material in membrane form as cardiac patch to overcome these limitations for supporting damaged myocardium during therapy stage, and for better adhesion and proliferation of cardiac cells. For this purpose, the electrospun membranes were coated with polydopamine (PDA) or in situ gold nanoparticle (AuNP) decorated following PDA coating. The analyses exhibited that the PDA-AuNP modification transformed the hydrophobic PCL to a microenvironment with higher hydrophilicity and enhanced electrical conductivity with PDA concentration dependent manner. Indirect extract-based indirect cytotoxicity assessment assay on human cardiomyocyte (HCM) and human neuroblastoma cells revealed no toxicity. Seven and 14 days of HCM culture studies showed that cell adhesion and proliferation significantly increased in accordance with the increasing PDA concentration. However, highest AuNP deposition exhibited a slight decrease compared to its lower concentration group since all AuNP deposited groups exhibited increased cell adhesion and proliferation compared to their only PDA coated analogues. This decrease was attributed to extreme hydrophilicity and surface energy of the membranes diminishing the effective adhesion of the cells to fiber surface. The dual functionalized electrospun PCL membranes were concluded to be a promising candidate to be used as cardiac patch, especially the ones coated with PDA in 2 mg/mL solution and decorated with AuNPs, exhibiting an electrical conductivity enhancement by approximately 1000-fold and highest cell adhesion and proliferation.
items.authors: Taha Buğra Taşdelen, Busra Kilic, Özlem Eğri, Halil Murat Aydin, Sinan Eğri

items.title: Beyond Compliance: AI, GDPR, and ESG as Pillars of Emerging Responsible Corporate Governance in the EU Regulatory Landscape
items.abstract: The European Union’s regulatory landscape is undergoing a fundamental transformation, characterised by the simultaneous emergence of three distinct yet interconnected governance frameworks: the Artificial Intelligence Act, the General Data Protection Regulation, and the expanding ESG obligations encompassing sustainability reporting and due diligence. While traditionally treated as separate compliance domains, this paper argues that these frameworks increasingly operate as interconnected mechanisms of corporate responsibility, requiring companies to integrate technological, informational, social, and environmental considerations into governance processes. Through a systematic analysis of the accountability principles embedded within each framework, this paper demonstrates that AI regulation, GDPR obligations, and ESG requirements are converging into a unified governance architecture that extends corporate responsibility beyond traditional compliance toward proactive, stakeholder-oriented governance. The paper develops an integrated governance model that positions AI governance (algorithmic responsibility), GDPR (information responsibility), and ESG (societal responsibility) as three interconnected pillars of responsible corporate governance in the EU. This paper extends this literature by demonstrating how these three frameworks collectively form an integrated model of corporate responsibility. The paper concludes that the EU is developing a distinctive model where legal compliance becomes the foundation for responsible corporate conduct, signalling a fundamental change in the purpose and practice of corporate governance.
items.authors: Charalampos Stamelos

items.title: Molecular Epidemiology and Conjugative Transferability of blaOXA-48/blaNDM-1 Co-Occurrence in Extensively Drug-Resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae from Egyptian Tertiary Care Hospitals
items.abstract: Carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae is a major threat to global health, with increasing incidence in developing countries, including Egypt. This study determined carbapenem-resistance prevalence among clinical K. pneumoniae isolates from two Egyptian tertiary hospitals, characterized the major carbapenemase genes, and assessed the transferability of the resistance plasmids. VITEK® 2 and MALDI-TOF MS identified 94 non-duplicate isolates. Susceptibility was determined by Kirby–Bauer diffusion and VITEK® 2. MICs of imipenem, meropenem and colistin were confirmed by broth microdilution. Isolates were classified as multidrug-resistant (MDR), extensively drug-resistant (XDR), or pandrug-resistant (PDR) according to established definitions. Phenotypic (modified Hodge test [MHT], modified carbapenem inactivation method [mCIM], modified Carba NP test [mCNP]) and genotypic (PCR/BlastN) evaluation of carbapenemase production and plasmid transferability by conjugation were carried out in 18 isolates, selected to represent every carbapenemase genotype identified in the collection. All isolates were MDR, and 94.68% were carbapenem-resistant and fulfilled the criteria for XDR, remaining susceptible only to colistin and tigecycline. Carbapenemase production was confirmed phenotypically in 98.9% and genotypically in 97.9% of isolates. blaOXA-48 (94.7%) and blaNDM-1 (69.1%) predominated, with 67.0% co-carriage; blaKPC occurred in 5.3%. Conjugation transferred carbapenemase-encoding plasmids to Escherichia coli J53 from 77.8% (14/18) of donors, conferring carbapenem non-susceptibility in all transconjugants. All isolates were colistin-susceptible by broth microdilution, the reference method. The high XDR prevalence, along with the conjugative transferability of blaOXA-48/blaNDM-1, is consistent with a mobile carbapenemase-encoding plasmid reservoir in Egyptian tertiary care, highlighting the significance of carbapenemase surveillance and stewardship. Plasmid characterization and clonal typing were not performed and are required to define that reservoir fully.
items.authors: Mohamed Abd El-Gawad El-Sayed El-Sayed Ahmed, Amr Elsayed Ibrahim Elghopashy, Yasser M. Ragab, Reham R. EL-Lakany, Doaa Abdelrahman, Alaa A. Omar

items.title: Investigation on Hot-Carrier Injection Mechanisms and Reliability Design-Based Strategies in Cryogenically Operated CMOS ROICs for Infrared Focal Plane Arrays
items.abstract: Cryogenic operation of CMOS read-out integrated circuits (ROICs) is essential for high-performance infrared focal plane arrays but significantly affects carrier transport and device reliability. This work investigates hot-carrier injection (HCI) mechanisms in 180 nm NMOS transistors operating from room temperature down to 140 K. Electrical characterization and accelerated stress measurements reveal a strong impact of hot-carrier effects at low temperatures, resulting in increased degradation of device characteristics, particularly under channel hot-electron (CHE) and drain avalanche hot carrier (DAHC) stress conditions. Time-to-failure modeling confirms accelerated degradation kinetics while validating conventional substrate-current-based reliability methodologies at cryogenic temperatures. Geometry-based design strategies, notably gate-length optimization, are proposed to mitigate cryogenic HCI effects, enabling an improved performance–reliability trade-off. These results provide key guidelines for design reliability of cryogenic CMOS ROICs for infrared imaging applications.
items.authors: Ayoub El El Abdi, Philippe Martin-Gonthier, Valentin Badefort-Baril

items.title: Integrated Electrical Resistivity Tomography and Borehole Correlation for Characterizing Salt Formation Geometry and Groundwater Circulation at Slănic Prahova, Romania
items.abstract: Salt (halite) massifs undergoing active dissolution are among the most hazard-prone geological settings for ground instability, and their monitoring requires a reliable geometric model of the salt body and its overburden. This study presents an integrated geoelectrical–geological characterization of the salt formation at Slănic Prahova (Romania), carried out in 2026 within the GEOMONITOR project. Six electrical resistivity tomography (ERT) profiles were acquired along three transects, each surveyed with both Wenner and Schlumberger electrode configurations (5 m electrode spacing), and correlated with lithological logs from three boreholes (F1, F2, F3) that intercepted the salt formation at 98.0 m, 44.1 m and 68.0 m below ground, corresponding to 301.0, 346.4 and 327.0 m a.s.l. respectively. Reading both datasets in absolute elevation is the key step of the workflow: it shows that the salt roof enters the imaged volume only in the Baia Roșie sector, where a body exceeding 1000 Ω·m occupies the 348–370 m a.s.l. interval—an elevation range that agrees, to within the ±15 m datum uncertainty of the sections, with the shallowest salt roof recorded by drilling (346.4 m a.s.l.)—whereas along the other two transects, the salt roof lies 35–80 m below the base of the inverted models. The sections delineate a strongly heterogeneous cover, predominantly conductive (1–10 Ω·m) and punctuated by transition zones with steep lateral resistivity gradients. Two consequences follow for hazard-oriented surveys of this kind: shallow resistive anomalies confined to the uppermost meters cannot be attributed to the salt roof, and the absence of a resistive anomaly along a line of this length is not evidence for the absence of salt. The conductive–resistive contact zones, rather than the resistive cores themselves, are identified as the priority targets for hydrogeological monitoring, since they can concentrate permeability contrasts and control dissolution. The survey is a single, non-repeated campaign without pore-fluid characterization, and is therefore presented as the baseline from which a monitoring network can be designed rather than as a record of temporal change. The elevation-based reconciliation of ERT and borehole data proposed here is transferable to other salt karst settings.
items.authors: Liliana Irina Stoian, Anca Margareta Isac, Violeta Monica Radu, Valentina Maria Cetean, Elena Aurelia Tudor, Antonio Ulmeanu

items.title: Effectiveness of the 23-Valent Pneumococcal Polysaccharide Vaccine in Reducing Mortality Among Older Adults: A Real-World Retrospective Cohort Study in Guangzhou, China
items.abstract: Objectives: To evaluate the real-world effectiveness of the 23-valent pneumococcal polysaccharide vaccine (PPSV23) in reducing all-cause, pneumonia-related, and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD)-related mortality in adults aged ≥60 years. Methods: In this retrospective cohort study using existing health surveillance data, individuals aged ≥60 years on 1 January 2020 were followed until 31 August 2025 and classified by PPSV23 vaccination status. Propensity score matching (PSM) at a 1:1 ratio balanced sex, age, regional distribution, urbanization level and influenza vaccination status. Time-dependent Cox proportional hazards models estimated hazard ratios (HR) and vaccine effectiveness (VE), defined as (1 − HR) × 100%. Subgroup, negative control (mortality from traffic accidents), and E-value sensitivity analyses were performed. Results: After PSM, 453,500 individuals were included, with a mean follow-up of 5.61 years. All-cause mortality was 3.93 per 1000 person-years in vaccinated versus 9.57 in unvaccinated individuals. PPSV23 vaccination reduced all-cause mortality (VE = 43.1%, 95% CI: 41.2–45.0%), pneumonia-related mortality (VE = 46.2%, 95% CI: 39.6–52.1%), and COPD-related mortality (VE = 33.5%, 95% CI: 20.9–44.2%) (all p 0.001). In a cause-specific decomposition, pneumonia- and COPD-related deaths together explained only 14.9% of the absolute reduction in all-cause deaths, whereas circulatory diseases and malignant tumors accounted for 36.8% and 31.9%, respectively. Among those also vaccinated against influenza, VE was 48.0% and 38.2% for pneumonia- and COPD-related mortality, respectively. For COPD-related mortality, the benefit was greater in men (VE = 42.3%) and in those aged ≥70 years (70–79 years, VE = 45.6%; ≥80 years, VE = 52.0%). PPSV23 was not associated with the negative control outcome (p = 0.247); E-values (1.98–2.44) indicated robustness to unmeasured confounding. Conclusions: PPSV23 vaccination was associated with significantly lower all-cause, pneumonia-related, and COPD-related mortality among elderly individuals aged ≥60 years. However, the observed association with all-cause mortality should be interpreted cautiously. Continued promotion of PPSV23 vaccination and advocacy for combined influenza–pneumococcal vaccination strategies are recommended.
items.authors: Yan Kang, Zhiwei Zheng, Juan Qi, Lin Tang, Wen Wang, Xinqi Lin
items.title_zh: 23价肺炎球菌多糖疫苗对老年人死亡率的影响研究
items.summary_zh: 目的：评估23价肺炎球菌多糖疫苗（PPSV23）在降低60岁及以上成人的全因、肺炎相关及慢性阻塞性肺疾病（COPD）相关死亡率的实际效果。方法：本回顾性队列研究使用现有健康监测数据，追踪2020年1月1日年龄≥60岁的个体至2025年8月31日，并按PPSV23接种状态分类。采用1:1比例的倾向评分匹配（PSM）平衡性别、年龄、地区分布、城市化水平和流感疫苗接种状态。使用时间依赖的Cox比例风险模型估计风险比（HR）和疫苗有效性（VE），定义为（1 − HR）× 100%。结果：经过PSM后，共纳入453,500名个体，平均随访5.61年。接种者的全因死亡率为每千人年3.93，而未接种者为9.57。PPSV23接种显著降低全因死亡率（VE = 43.1%，95% CI: 41.2–45.0%）、肺炎相关死亡率（VE = 46.2%，95% CI: 39.6–52.1%）及COPD相关死亡率（VE = 33.5%，95% CI: 20.9–44.2%）（均p < 0.001）。
items.l1_lead: 23价肺炎球菌多糖疫苗显著降低60岁及以上老年人的全因、肺炎及COPD相关死亡率，疫苗有效性分别为43.1%、46.2%和33.5%。
items.l2_summary:
本研究旨在评估23价肺炎球菌多糖疫苗（PPSV23）对60岁及以上成人的全因死亡率、肺炎相关死亡率及慢性阻塞性肺疾病（COPD）相关死亡率的影响。研究采用回顾性队列设计，利用现有健康监测数据，追踪2020年1月1日至2025年8月31日期间年龄≥60岁的个体，并根据PPSV23接种状态进行分类。为确保样本的均衡性，研究采用1:1比例的倾向评分匹配（PSM），控制了性别、年龄、地区分布、城市化水平和流感疫苗接种状态等变量。最终，共纳入453,500名个体，平均随访时间为5.61年。

研究结果显示，接种PPSV23的个体全因死亡率为每千人年3.93，而未接种者的全因死亡率为9.57，表明接种显著降低了全因死亡率，疫苗有效性（VE）为43.1%（95% CI: 41.2–45.0%）。此外，肺炎相关死亡率的疫苗有效性为46.2%（95% CI: 39.6–52.1%），COPD相关死亡率的疫苗有效性为33.5%（95% CI: 20.9–44.2%），所有结果均具有统计学意义（p < 0.001）。综上所述，PPSV23疫苗在降低老年人群体的全因及特定疾病相关死亡率方面具有显著效果，为老年人接种肺炎球菌疫苗提供了有力的证据支持。

items.title: Dual-Pigmented Rice: A Dual-Pigmented Whole Grain with Enhanced Nutritional and Antioxidant Properties
items.abstract: Pigmented rice is valued for its abundant natural bioactive compounds and potential health-promoting properties. In this study, the black rice cultivar Huamoxiang No. 5 (HMX) was used to develop three genetically similar rice lines with distinct pericarp pigmentation. Among them, BRHMX (a dual-pigmented rice accumulating both anthocyanins and proanthocyanidins) and RHMX (a red rice accumulating proanthocyanidins) were generated through hybridization, successive backcrossing, and marker-assisted selection, whereas the white rice line WHMX was derived from a spaceflight-induced mutant of HMX. Comparative analyses revealed that differences in pericarp pigmentation had negligible effects on grain morphology and major nutritional components, including starch, protein, and amino acids. Compared with HMX, BRHMX maintained more than 80% of the anthocyanin content of HMX, while its proanthocyanidin content was 103% higher than that of RHMX. Furthermore, BRHMX exhibited the highest total phenolic content and the highest levels of 31 soluble phenolic acids, together with the strongest chemical antioxidant capacity, as determined by ABTS and FRAP assays. Untargeted metabolomic profiling showed that flavonoids and soluble phenolic acids were the major metabolite classes associated with pericarp color divergence. Integrated metabolomic and transcriptomic analyses further suggested a potential reallocation of metabolic flux between anthocyanin and proanthocyanidin biosynthetic pathways during early pericarp development. Cooking generally reduced the contents of anthocyanins, proanthocyanidins, and total phenolics, as well as chemical antioxidant capacity, although the magnitude of these changes varied among the four lines. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that the newly developed dual-pigmented rice line combines characteristics associated with conventional black and red rice, providing a valuable genetic resource for whole-grain rice product development.
items.authors: Zijin Weng, Wenjun Wei, Faming Dong, Yilong Yao, Yanhua Li, Qinglu Zhang

items.title: Next-Generation Modulation and Control of Power Electronic Systems: AI-Enabled Control, Digital Twins, Fault-Tolerant Operation, and Cyber-Physical Security
items.abstract: Power electronic systems are evolving from conventional fixed-function converters toward intelligent, adaptive, and cyber-physical energy-conversion platforms in which modulation, predictive control, artificial intelligence (AI), digital twins (DTs), fault diagnosis, and cybersecurity increasingly interact within a unified closed-loop architecture. This paper presents an integrated review and mathematical framework for next-generation modulation and control of power electronic systems, with an emphasis on advanced modulation, predictive control, AI-assisted adaptation, converter-oriented digital state estimation, fault-tolerant operation, and cyber-resilient control. The proposed framework links converter dynamics, state and parameter estimation, physical faults, cyber disturbances, supervisory anomaly assessment, and mode-dependent control reconfiguration. Two clearly separated validation levels complement the literature synthesis: experimentally measured operating data are used to establish physically representative operating conditions, whereas a dedicated converter-control model is used to evaluate closed-loop dynamic resilience. Under a combined physical/cyber disturbance, resilient reconfiguration reduced the post-event speed RMSE from 9.203 to 0.425 rad/s, the peak speed error from 29.999 to 1.724 rad/s, and the maximum current from 69.112 to 10.662 A, while eliminating 829 current-constraint violations observed without resilience. Across 100 randomized Monte Carlo trials, the mean post-event RMSE decreased from 11.951 ± 3.060 to 0.769 ± 0.291 rad/s, with the corresponding 95% confidence interval narrowing from 11.351–12.550 to 0.712–0.826 rad/s. The results provide simulation-based, closed-loop evidence that coordinated state estimation, anomaly assessment, and resilient reconfiguration can substantially limit disturbance propagation while maintaining converter-control performance under combined physical and cyber abnormalities. Hardware-in-the-loop and embedded real-time implementation remain subjects for future validation.
items.authors: Somayeh Soroush, Samir Abood, Annamalai Annamalai, Mohamed Chouikha, Turki Nejress

items.title: The Effect of Maternal Cigarette Smoking and Alcohol Consumption During Pregnancy on Cardio-Metabolic Risk Factors in Infants, Children, and Adolescents: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
items.abstract: Background: The studies on the direct and indirect effects of maternal cigarette smoking and alcohol consumption during pregnancy on cardiometabolic risk in offspring have been rather inconsistent. This review evaluated the associations between maternal cigarette smoking and alcohol exposure during pregnancy and cardiometabolic outcomes in infants, children, and adolescents. Methods: PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science and Google Scholar were searched in May 2026. Twenty-five prospective cohort studies published from 2001 onwards, investigating maternal cigarette smoking, alcohol use, or both during pregnancy, and offspring vascular or cardiometabolic outcomes, were included. Results: The association between maternal cigarette smoking during pregnancy and offspring systolic blood pressure was inconclusive. The pooled estimate suggested a small increase; however, the result was at borderline statistical significance (MD = 0.40 mmHg; 95% CI = 0.00, 0.81; Z = 1.96; p = 0.05). No significant associations were observed for diastolic blood pressure (MD = −0.16 mmHg; 95% CI = −0.59, 0.28; Z = 0.71; p = 0.48) and right carotid intima-media thickness (MD = 0.01 mm; 95% CI = −0.01, 0.03; Z = 1.27; p = 0.20), as well as maternal alcohol exposure and DBP (MD = −0.00 mmHg; 95% CI = −2.60, 2.59; Z = 0.00; p = 1.00). Evidence relating to alcohol exposure alone, dual exposure to smoking and alcohol, vascular outcomes, and lipid profiles was limited and synthesised narratively. Conclusions: The association between maternal cigarette smoking and offspring systolic blood pressure was inconclusive due to borderline significance. The evidence regarding vascular outcomes and lipid profiles remained limited and inconsistent. The certainty of the evidence was low for the adjusted systolic and diastolic analyses and very low for all remaining outcomes.
items.authors: Tammy C. Ras, Jaron Ras, Eunice B. Turawa, André Oelofse, Juléy J. A. De Smidt

items.title: Physicochemical Properties, Hemocompatibility, Cytotoxicity and Antibacterial Activity of Biopolymeric Sponges Containing Chlorhexidine/Ca sup 2+ /sup for Potential Applications in Post‐Dental Extraction Wounds
items.abstract: Biopolymer-based sponges incorporating chlorhexidine (CHX) and CaCl₂ were developed as potential topical biomaterials for post-dental extraction wound management. Carboxymethylcellulose (CMC) and Chitosan (CHS) sponges containing hyaluronic acid (HA), glycerol (G), chlorhexidine (CHX) and calcium chloride (CaCl₂, Ca2+) were characterized in terms of their physicochemical properties, hemocompatibility, cytotoxicity, neutrophil activation and microbial growth control. The CHX-loaded sponges exhibited no detectable hemolysis (0%), compared with 22.67% for the control formulation, and markedly reduced neutrophil activation, as indicated by CD11b and CD69 expression. Although no significant growth inhibition was observed, the sponges prevented abnormal microbial proliferation, maintaining a stable microbial population. Collectively, these findings highlight the potential of CHX-loaded biopolymer sponges as hemocompatible topical biomaterials for post-extraction wound management alveolar tissue repair.
items.authors: Mayra González-Martínez, Alexa Chacón-Ortega, Laura Abisai Pazos-Rojas, Diana del C. Pazos-Guarneros, Eric Reyes-Cervantes, Abigailt Flores-Ledesma

items.title: Synthesis, Antiproliferative Activity and In Silico Docking Analysis of Tubulin-Polymerase-Targeting Triazole-Tethered Vindoline-Chalcone Hybrids
items.abstract: In the frame of our ongoing research on multitarget alkaloid-derived anticancer agents, relying on a modular synthetic strategy terminated by well-established sequential Sonogashira and CuAAC protocols, we synthesized a systematic selection of chalcone-vindoline hybrids incorporating 1,4-disubstituted 1,2,3-triazole as a linker. The use of the same synthetic approach led to the construction of a zidovudine-derived vindoline hybrid, which served as a negative control highlighting the essential contribution of the chalcone moiety to the antiproliferative activity. Two analogous aryl-substituted chalcone hybrids 14a,b were also prepared to assess the contribution of the vindoline fragment to the desired effect. The targeted hybrids and the references were evaluated for their antiproliferative activity against a panel of human adherent gynecological cancer cell lines (HeLa, SiHa, MCF-7, MDA-MB-231 and A2780) as well as on non-malignant fibroblasts (NIH/3T3). Vindoline hybrids 10a and 10i comprising 3,4,5- and 1,4,6-trimethoxyphenyl-substituted chalcone fragments, respectively, displayed substantial activity, featuring IC50 values lower than 0.4 µM on all the investigated cancer cell lines. On the other hand, hybrids 10c–e containing monomethoxy-substituted chalcones, also featuring submicromolar IC50 values on malignant cells, showed moderately lower activities against non-malignant fibroblasts (NIH/3T3), indicating a certain degree of cancer selectivity. The related ferrocene-derived hybrid (10i) and vindoline-free chalcones 14a,b were identified as antiproliferative agents with significantly decreased efficiency, while the ferrocene hybrid comprising an alternative enone sequence in the chalcone residue (11) as well as the zidovudine-derived vindoline hybrid 12 were inactive. Modeling results indicate that the vindoline hybrids bind to the inter-dimer vinca crevice of tubulin oligomers and confirm that the two segments exert a mutually stabilizing effect on the binding of the other, providing a framework for future structure optimization.
items.authors: Etelka Ferenczi, Dóra K. Menyhárd, Adriána Kovács, Ágnes Gömöry, László Drahos, Péter Keglevich

items.title: Tree Felling by Chainsaw: A Laboratory Assessment of the Hinge Flexibility in Relation to Its Width and to the Back-Cut Height
items.abstract: Motor-manual tree felling by chainsaws remains a widespread but hazardous forestry practice. This operation consists of executing a directional notch followed by a felling cut that releases a hinge. The hinge geometry (defined by its height, width, and alignment relative to the directional notch) is a critical determinant of safe felling, controlling the direction and stability of the falling tree. How the hinge's geometry might affect these aspects has not yet been studied. This study evaluates variations in hinge flexibility and bending stiffness using wooden square beams of European beech (Fagus sylvatica) and silver fir (Abies alba) in a rig reproducing the classical felling cuts, varying hinge geometry combinations. Two geometric parameters, back-cut height (S) and hinge width (C) were examined. Mechanical testing was performed using a universal testing machine, and load–deformation curves were smoothed with a Savitzky–Golay filter; the Critical Bending Angle and Yield Point were determined by using the 0.02° offset method and absorbed energy by Simpson integration. Results reveal different mechanical behavior between the two dimensions: hinge width primarily determines yield force, whereas back-cut height governs flexibility, showing a strong negative correlation with the critical bending angle. Significant species-specific differences were observed for both response variables. Hinge toughness, expressed as absorbed energy per unit hinge cross-section, was found to be independent of back-cut height and about 1.8 times higher in beech (0.39 kJ·m⁻²) than in fir (0.22 kJ·m⁻²).
items.authors: Cristiano Foderi, Francesco Neri, Fabio Fabiano, Simone Calamai, Andrea Laschi, Marco Togni

items.title: Artificial Intelligence in 3D Aortic CTA Segmentation for Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm Management: A Narrative Review
items.abstract: Computed tomography angiography (CTA) is the reference imaging modality for diagnosis, endovascular planning, and surveillance of abdominal aortic aneurysms (AAAs), but conventional assessment remains time-consuming, operator-dependent, and limited by complex anatomy. This narrative review examines the role of artificial intelligence (AI) in three-dimensional aortic CTA segmentation for AAA management. The narrative synthesis drew on literature identified through PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus and the Cochrane Library, with the original search covering January 2000 to July 2026. Ten primary studies from the existing bibliography were characterized in a study-level table, and reported Dice coefficients were displayed for nine studies. Current evidence indicates that AI-based segmentation, particularly using convolutional neural networks, U-Net-derived models, and nnU-Net frameworks, can improve the speed and reproducibility of aortic lumen, wall, thrombus, branch vessel, endograft, and aneurysm sac delineation. These techniques may support more accurate morphometric measurements, device sizing, procedural planning, quantitative surveillance, and the development of advanced imaging biomarkers. However, available studies remain heterogeneous in datasets, anatomical evaluation, imaging protocols, validation strategies, and reported performance metrics, limiting direct comparison and clinical generalizability. AI-assisted 3D segmentation represents a promising tool for transforming CTA from descriptive imaging into quantitative decision support, but robust multicenter validation, workflow integration, and expert supervision remain essential before widespread clinical adoption.
items.authors: Leonardo Pasquetti, Edoardo Pasqui, Eleonora Cerbini, Manfredi Giuseppe Anzaldi, Giovanna Grasso, Bruno Gargiulo

items.title: A Review of Pendulum Systems and Structures for Wave Energy Conversion
items.abstract: Wave energy has emerged as a promising renewable energy source due to its high energy density and consistency compared to solar and wind. This literature review explores the technological components and design considerations of wave energy converters (WECs), focusing on primary systems, power take-off (PTO) mechanisms, and innovative concepts utilizing enclosed-hull converters based on pendulum systems and structures. Various WEC designs are analyzed with respect to their operational principles, advantages and limitations. Special attention is given to recent advances in enclosed WEC systems utilizing pendulum-based inertial converters. These devices offer a flexible means for establishing resonant response of a PTO enclosed within the WEC buoy or hull, and as such, pendulum-based WECs have attracted significant interest within academia and relevant industry stakeholders. Through comprehensive comparison and evaluation, this review identifies key trends and challenges in the development, optimization and commercialization of pendulum-based wave energy technology.
items.authors: Mihai Ionut Trandafir, Spiros Papaefthimiou, Panagiotis Alevras

items.title: Agricultural Waste as a Raw Material Source for Biofuel Production: Analysis of Methods, Models and Intelligent Technologies
items.abstract: With growing global demand for renewable energy and the need for efficient use of organic waste, agricultural waste (including animal excrement and plant residues) is considered a key and promising feedstock for biogas production via anaerobic digestion. Despite the environmental and energy benefits of this approach, significant variability in the chemical composition and quality of the feedstock poses a serious obstacle to ensuring consistently high methane yields. This review systematizes and evaluates modern approaches aimed at overcoming this variability. Particular attention is paid to the integration of machine learning methods, particularly artificial neural networks. These methods demonstrate high accuracy in modeling and predicting methanogenesis efficiency based on analysis of input biomass characteristics. Furthermore, the review critically evaluates the role of intelligent control and automation systems using hybrid algorithms for adaptive adjustment of process parameters (carbon-to-nitrogen ratio, temperature, pH) in real time. The implementation of these intelligent technologies is key to process optimization, increased reliability, and the economic competitiveness of the biogas industry.
items.authors: Oleksiy Opryshko, Nikolay Kiktev, Taras Lendiel, Vladyslav Yakushov, Borys Hrudynin, Zoia Pustova

items.title: Machine Learning for Screening Bioactive Compounds in Traditional Chinese Medicine: Computational Prediction, Multi-Omics Integration, and Clinical Translation Potential
items.abstract: Identifying bioactive compounds in traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) requires computational prioritization to be connected with chemical and pharmacological evidence. This structured narrative and critical review examines machine learning applications in compound prediction, formula-compatibility analysis, multi-omics integration, and drug development and repurposing. Molecular fingerprints, graph and sequence representations, knowledge graphs, and generative models are discussed in relation to their intended endpoints and validation conditions. Studies are classified along two independent dimensions: application scope, distinguishing direct TCM applications from natural-product studies and general drug-discovery methods, and validation level, ranging from computational prediction to chemical, experimental, and clinical evidence. Three case analyses illustrate a TCM-specific graph-learning platform with chemical confirmation, a downstream animal and metabolomics study without machine learning screening, and a proposed causal framework assembled from separate studies. Across these applications, machine learning supports candidate ranking and hypothesis generation, but predicted targets, attention weights, and multi-omics associations do not independently establish target engagement, formula synergy, or therapeutic efficacy. Major limitations include chemical-domain shift, inconsistent database provenance, data leakage, sparse negative results, and incomplete experimental follow-up. Reliable advancement requires scaffold-aware or external evaluation, explicit applicability domains and uncertainty, traceable data processing, and constituent-resolved intervention studies. A minimum reporting checklist consolidates these requirements, while route-specific assessment distinguishes synthetic accessibility from biosynthetic feasibility. Together, these considerations provide a basis for evaluating screening claims and designing reproducible workflows toward experimentally supported TCM compound discovery.
items.authors: Zi-Meng Qi, Jing-Zhen Wu, Pan Li, Tian-Yang Xu, Peng Yu

items.title: First Detection and Delimiting Survey of the Emerald Ash Borer (Agrilus planipennis Fairmaire, 1888 (Coleoptera: Buprestidae)) in Slovakia
items.abstract: The emerald ash borer, Agrilus planipennis Fairmaire, 1888 (Coleoptera: Buprestidae), is an invasive pest in Europe and North America, responsible for extensive mortality of ash (Fraxinus spp.). This study reports its first confirmed occurrence in Slovakia and summarises the subsequent delimiting survey. On 25 June 2026, specimens morphologically resembling A. planipennis were collected from a monitoring trap in a park in Streda nad Bodrogom, south-eastern Slovakia.
