Two senior experts evaluated 36 dimension-level relationships, and retained LLM quotations were manually checked against the original transcripts; no fabricated quotations were identified. Direct coverage ranged from 75.0% to 91.7%, broad coverage from 83.3% to 100.0%, and frequency-weighted mapping from 80.3% to 94.9%. Theme-count precision was 50.0% for DeepSeek, 69.2% for Qwen, and 55.6% for GPT. Eight dimensions were directly recovered across all outputs, whereas guidance and motivation, big-picture awareness, care and support orientation, and teamwork varied across outputs. An independent expert reproduced all 36 mappings, yielding 100% raw agreement. The findings distinguish thematic granularity from construct-boundary recovery and support LLMs as complementary analytical assistants.
items.authors: Yuhan Xie, Shifeng Lei, Guang Yang, Feng Yao

items.title: Bayesianand Frequentist Estimation of Adaptability and Stability Parameters of Cucumis melo L. Genotypes Using the Toler Model Under Semi-Arid Conditions
items.abstract: Melon (Cucumis melo L.) production in Brazil is concentrated in the semi-arid Northeast region, where environmental variability hinders the selection of stable, high-yielding genotypes. This study evaluated the adaptability and phenotypic stability of experimental hybrids of yellow melon, cantaloupe melon, and Galia melon under contrasting environmental conditions, using Toler’s bi-segmented and simple linear models under frequentist and Bayesian approaches. The experiments were conducted in the Brazilian semi-arid region, comprising 8 environments for the first Yellow melon group, 12 for the second Yellow melon group, 9 for Cantaloupe, and 12 for Galia. Bayesian inference was implemented using nested sampling with the UltraNest package to estimate the intercept (α)and regression coefficients (β1 and β2) of the bi-segmented model, as well as the common regression coefficient (βcommon) of the simple linear model, together with their posterior uncertainty. The Bayesian analysis provided 95% highest-density intervals (HDIs) for these parameters, with convergence assessed using trace and corner plots. The frequentist and Bayesian approaches showed consistent classifications for 37 of the 38 genotypes (97.37%), with an isolated difference observed for AM-12. Based on the Bayesian analysis, Group A genotypes were identified among the Yellow melon and Cantaloupe materials, whereas the Galia genotypes were classified into Groups C and E. Group A genotypes exhibited a convex and doubly desirable response pattern, characterized by low sensitivity in unfavorable environments and high responsiveness under favorable conditions; Group C represented broad adaptability, whereas Group E represented a concave and doubly undesirable response. The results indicate that Bayesian inference provides complementary information to traditional analyses by explicitly quantifying parameter uncertainty, supporting the interpretation of genotype adaptability and phenotypic stability in melon breeding under semi-arid conditions.
items.authors: Maxsuel Marcos Fernandes de de Lima, Adriano Ferreira Martins, João Everthon da Silva Ribeiro, Ester dos Santos Coêlho, Cintya Mikaelly Pereira Gaia Souza, Edicleide Macedo da Silva

items.title: “Still French, Still Home”: Colonial Citizenship, Family Memory, and Intergenerational Belonging in Franco-India, 1721–1954
items.abstract: Mahé (Mayyazhi), a French enclave on India’s Malabar coast, remained under French administration from 1721 to 1954, and its French-Indian families have carried the legal and cultural consequences of that rule across generations ever since. This study examines how colonial-era intimacy was configured within the broader structures of colonial governance in a small, decentralised enclave largely absent from mainstream accounts of empire. Combining a structured literary analysis of M. Mukundan’s novel On the Banks of the Mayyazhi with ethnographic fieldwork among Mahé’s French-Indian families, the study applies a four-phase Historiographic Narrative Analysis Framework (HNAF) to trace how face-to-face contact, bilingual schooling, and household ritual mediated colonial authority and shaped patterns of loyalty, mimicry, and inherited identity across generations. Fiction and lived testimony reveal overlapping but non-identical traces of an affectively saturated, person-to-person contact zone whose effects outlasted formal decolonisation by decades and continue to shape Franco-Indian family memory and commemorative practice today. The findings suggest that genealogical continuity, rather than political rupture alone, offers a productive lens for understanding how colonial subjecthood is inherited, reworked, and lived within families long after an empire’s formal end. These findings carry implications for the study of other small, materially thin colonial enclaves and for broader methodological debates about using literary sources genealogically. The study also speaks to SDG 10, particularly its emphasis on social, economic, and political inclusion and on reducing inequalities rooted in origin and status, by showing how colonial hierarchies can persist through citizenship, family memory, and inherited forms of belonging.
items.authors: Sayant Vijay

items.title: Bearing Names of the Dead: Memory, Identity Formation, and Family History in Bekwarra Naming Culture
items.abstract: Earlier studies on Bekwarra names have focused on cultural and syntactic perspectives, with limited attention to how the Bekwarra naming culture transmits family history and serves as a cultural archive in which the experiences, struggles, and social roles of departed relatives are encoded. This study, therefore, takes a different direction by showing how name bearers become living extensions of ancestral memory, thereby strengthening and reinforcing kinship ties within the community. Ethnopragmatic theory was adopted as an analytical framework to uncover the cultural meanings embedded in these names. Data were gathered through semi-structured interviews and informal conversations with 25 participants in Nyanya and Abuochiche Wards, Bekwarra Local Government Area, Cross River State, southeastern Nigeria. The findings reveal that Bekwarra people use naming practices to retain memory, sustain lineage consciousness, and maintain intergenerational connections. Beyond functioning as linguistic labels, Bekwarra names constitute an active social process through which the past informs present identities. To conclude, this study deepens the understanding of the intricate relationship between names, memory, and the ways in which naming acts as a repository of cultural knowledge.
items.authors: Benjamin Okon Nyong, Prince Agbor Onyi

items.title: A Physics-Guided Statistical Framework for Bearing Fault Diagnosis Under Unit Variability and Rotational Speed Uncertainty
items.abstract: Reliable bearing fault diagnosis must differentiate between defects and normal-operation-condition variation. The predictor must remain accurate when shaft speed is uncertain. Conventional accuracy-driven models often ignore false-positive rates and fail to accurately locate faults on unseen bearings’ data. This study proposes a physics-guided statistical framework that integrates resolution-based order screening, envelope peak-to-floor evidence, search- and collision-matched empirical nulls, and conformal calibration against healthy reference data. A two-stage bearing-level rule detects abnormal operation before localizing the dominant fault order. Evaluation comprised controlled simulations, unit-disjoint Paderborn experiments, and a prospectively frozen external test using the University of Ottawa Rolling-Element Dataset: Vibration and Acoustic Faults under Constant Load and Speed Conditions (UORED-VAFCLS). In simulation, family-wise false-positive rates were 2.58% and 3.12% for the two bearing geometries; detection power reached 83.3–93.8% at −4 dB and 98.3–100% at 0 dB, satisfying all registered criteria. On Paderborn, the overall false-positive rate was 7.08%, but condition-specific false alarms reached 17.5%; inner- and outer-race detection reached only 49.8% and 71.5%, despite high localization accuracy. On UORED-VAFCLS, the healthy false-alarm rate remained 5% (1/20 bearings), while developing-fault detection was 40% for both classes and faulty-state detection was 0% for inner-race and 20% for outer-race bearings. All ten inner-race states were mislocalized to the outer-race order. A post-evaluation diagnostic estimated a median speed of 1784 rpm rather than 1750 rpm. The resulting 1.94% discrepancy exceeded the admissible errors for the ball-pass frequency of the inner race (BPFI) and ball-pass frequency of the outer race (BPFO), 0.61% and 0.98%, respectively, indicating order-probe misalignment. These results show that false-alarm calibration can transfer while diagnostic sensitivity and physical localization fail. The study therefore separates calibration from diagnostic transferability and establishes independent bearing-level validation and explicit speed-uncertainty treatment as requirements for trustworthy physics-guided diagnosis.
items.authors: Muhammad Farooq Siddique, Muhammad Wisal, Muhammad Umar, Saad Ali, Muhammad Mansoor Janjua, Haris Khalid

items.title: Design and Evaluation Based on Excessive-Acceleration Mode Analysis Applying IMO Second-Generation Intact Stability Criteria for Ships
items.abstract: This study evaluated excessive-acceleration vulnerability based on the Level 1 and Level 2 criteria of the IMO second-generation intact stability framework. A 13K oil chemical tanker was analyzed, incorporating wave-induced dynamic effects into the assessment. The comparison between Level 1 and Level 2 results showed that the Level 2 criterion provided a less conservative evaluation, allowing a wider acceptable range of vertical positions relative to the roll axis. This highlights the necessity of dynamic analysis under realistic wave conditions. To improve the accuracy of the evaluation, the Froude–Krylov roll moment was reformulated by incorporating diffraction effects. Unlike conventional approaches that consider only incident-wave excitation, the proposed method accounts for both incident- and diffracted-wave components. This results in a smoother frequency-dependent effective wave slope function and a more consistent representation of hydrodynamic excitation. The results demonstrate that including diffraction effects extends the allowable range satisfying the Level 2 criterion, thereby increasing the design margin associated with the vertical center of gravity. Although the proposed approach requires additional computational effort, it provides a basis for examining the influence of diffraction on excessive-acceleration assessment.
